source: Written 2026-10-17 by Claude Sonnet and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin. Hand-written fixture questions are "approved".

notes.NC26.7.RPR.3: No figures needed: every circle graph is described by its sectors in words (percent, fraction or degrees) and every circle by its radius, diameter or circumference. Circumference questions say which value of pi to use (3.14 almost always; 22/7 only where the diameter or radius makes it exact). Answers are exact with that value. Choice items whose options are statements have no compute.
notes.NC26.7.ANR.3: No figures: number-line graphs are described in words (the kind of circle, where it is, and which way the line is shaded). Every equation key is solved exactly by a script; every inequality key and every distractor is checked against the solved inequality. Variables stay on one side. Inequalities with a negative coefficient (reversing the sign) appear only at difficulty 3, four questions. Skills: two-step equations, parentheses, fractions/decimals/negatives, writing and solving equations from situations, solving and writing inequalities, interpreting solutions in context, graphing on a number line, checking a value, and choosing an equation or an inequality.
notes.NC26.7.RPR.1: Seven skills drawn from the summary, each at all three difficulties: what stays constant (S1), the constant of proportionality from a table or pairs (S2), unit rates with fractions (S3), testing for proportionality (S4), writing and using y = kx (S5), comparing relationships (S6) and reading points in context (S7). Graphs are only ever described in words (a line through the origin, the point (3, 12)); no figure is referred to. No dollar signs: money is written in words. Fraction answers are accepted in any equivalent form.
notes.NC26.7.SGMR.2: Eleven skills, 8 or 9 questions each. Figures are described in words only. Pi is 3.14 (or 22/7 where the radius is a multiple of 7) as stated in each stem; "in terms of pi" appears in a few choice questions. No question needs a square root or cube root.
notes.NC26.7.SGMR.3: Written from the standard's summary only. No figures: every crossing is described by letters (lines AB and CD cross at O, which lies between A and B and between C and D) or by numbered angles in order, so no picture is needed. Answers are whole degrees; no decimal solutions. Questions that name three or more steps are kept to difficulty 3.
notes.NC26.7.RD.1: No figures: every table and tree diagram is described in words (for example "all 36 outcomes are written in a table", or a tree's stages and branch probabilities), and sample spaces are listed in the solutions. Spinners are described by equal sections or by the probability of each outcome. Choice items on fractions use plain a/b options (not LaTeX) so the compute check can run. Without-replacement items use two or three small draws. One difficulty-3 tree item (rain and a canceled game) puts different probabilities on the second-stage branches, the stretch end of the standard. Sample spaces of four coin flips (16 outcomes) appear only at difficulty 3.
notes.NC26.7.RD.2: Written from the standard's summary only. Text only: data are given as lists or counts in words (no graphs, dot plots or two-way tables). Where sampling, bias or wording is the skill, the answer is a statement (choice); the numeric questions cover estimating from samples, combining samples, counts and means, simulations and counting data. Answers are whole numbers, fractions or decimals; percents are given as a plain number with "percent" in the question.
notes.NC26.7.RD.3: Questions use text-only descriptions of dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots, histograms and box plots (five-number summaries written out); no figure is referred to.
notes.NC26.7.RD.4: Questions give lists, frequency tables and dot plots in words; no figure is referred to. Quartiles use the median-of-halves method; odd-sized sets are used only where the two common conventions agree (checked in the builder), and most sets have an even number of values.
notes.NC26.7.RD.5: Data are given as lists or as summary statistics (medians, IQRs), not as graphs. Items cover comparing medians and means, reading a spread, choosing a sensible plan, drawing only what the data support and communicating a comparison.
notes.NC26.7.ANR.1: No figures needed. Answers are integers, decimals, fractions or mixed numbers (negative where the signs make them so). Choice items whose options are expressions or statements have no compute; the build script checked every key with exact fraction arithmetic and refused any wrong option equal to its key. Repeating decimals are written with an overline (\overline) in the choice options only; numeric answers about them are single digits or sums of digits. Order of operations uses at most one square, of a fraction.
notes.NC26.7.ANR.2: No figures: areas and perimeters are given by side lengths in words. Choice items on expressions use options checked by a polynomial engine (the key is equivalent to the target, every other option is not). Skills: combining like terms, the distributive property (including negative and fractional factors), distributing and combining, factoring out a common factor, deciding whether two expressions are equivalent, adding and subtracting expressions, writing expressions for situations, what an equivalent form shows in context, and naming the properties of operations.
notes.NC26.7.RPR.2: Eight skills drawn from the summary: unit conversions (U1), actual size from a scale drawing (U2), constructing a drawing or finding a scale (U3), how a scale changes area (U4), sales tax and tip (U5), markup and discount (U6), commission (U7) and percent increase and decrease (U8). All scale-drawing questions give the scale in words (1 cm : 2 m); no figure is referred to. Numeric answers that are percents are written as plain numbers (the stem says "what percent"); choice answers may carry a percent sign. No dollar signs: money is written in words.
notes.NC26.7.SGMR.1: Ten skills, nine questions each, three at each difficulty. Figures are described in words only. Answers use 3.14 (or 22/7 where the radius is a multiple of 7) for pi, stated in each stem. No question needs a square root.

questions.skill: Find the constant of proportionality from a table of values
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y = 10$ when $x = 2$, $y = 20$ when $x = 4$, and $y = 30$ when $x = 6$. What is the constant of proportionality $k$ in $y = kx$?
questions.solution: In $y = kx$, $k = y \div x$. Use the first pair: $k = 10 \div 2 = 5$. The other pairs agree: $20 \div 4 = 5$ and $30 \div 6 = 5$.

questions.skill: Recognize a proportional relationship from pairs of values
questions.stem: Which list of $(x, y)$ pairs shows a proportional relationship?
questions.solution: In a proportional relationship, $y \div x$ is the same for every pair. For (1, 3), (2, 6), (3, 9) it is always 3. In the other lists $y$ goes up by a fixed amount each time, but $y \div x$ changes, so they are not proportional.

questions.skill: Unit rate when the time is a fraction
questions.stem: Maya walks 2 miles in $\frac{1}{2}$ hour at a steady pace. How many miles does she walk in 1 hour?
questions.solution: Miles per hour is $2 \div \frac{1}{2} = 2 \times 2 = 4$. In half an hour she walks 2 miles, so in a whole hour she walks twice as far, 4 miles.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: A store sells notebooks at the same price for each notebook. Which of these stays the same no matter how many notebooks are bought?
choices: The total cost
The number of notebooks
The total cost plus the number of notebooks
The cost of one notebook
questions.answer: The cost of one notebook
questions.solution: Each notebook has the same price, so the cost of one notebook never changes. The total cost and the number of notebooks both change as more notebooks are bought.

solve.answer: The cost of one notebook
solve.work: Same price per notebook, so the cost of one notebook (the unit rate) is constant. Total cost and count change; their sum changes.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, the ratio of $y$ to $x$ is always 4 to 1. What is $y$ when $x = 5$?
questions.solution: A ratio of 4 to 1 means $y$ is 4 times $x$. When $x = 5$, $y = 5 \times 4 = 20$.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, the value of $x$ is doubled. What happens to $y$?
choices: $y$ is doubled
$y$ is increased by 2
$y$ stays the same
$y$ is cut in half
questions.answer: $y$ is doubled
questions.solution: In a proportional relationship $y$ is always the same multiple of $x$. If $x$ is doubled, then $y$ is doubled too.

solve.answer: $y$ is doubled
solve.work: y = kx, so 2x gives 2kx = 2y: y doubles.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y = 4$ when $x = 3$. What is $y$ when $x = 9$?
questions.solution: $x$ goes from 3 to 9, which is 3 times as much, so $y$ is 3 times as much: $4 \times 3 = 12$.

solve.work: x goes 3 to 9 (times 3), so y goes 4 to 12. k = 4/3, 9 x 4/3 = 12.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: A table shows the cost of tickets: 3 tickets cost 12 dollars, 5 tickets cost 20 dollars and 8 tickets cost 32 dollars. The cost is proportional to the number of tickets. What is the constant of proportionality, in dollars per ticket?
questions.solution: Divide the cost by the number of tickets: $12 \div 3 = 4$. Check: $20 \div 5 = 4$ and $32 \div 8 = 4$. The constant of proportionality is 4 dollars per ticket.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: The pairs $(x, y)$ of a proportional relationship are $(4, 6)$, $(8, 12)$ and $(10, 15)$. The constant of proportionality is the number $k$ in $y = kx$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: $k = y \div x = 6 \div 4 = \frac{3}{2}$. Check with $12 \div 8$ and $15 \div 10$, which are also $\frac{3}{2}$. ($\frac{2}{3}$ is $x \div y$, and 2 is $y - x$ for the first pair.)

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: A proportional relationship includes the point $(5, 35)$. In $y = kx$, what is the value of $k$?
questions.solution: Since $y = kx$, $k = y \div x = 35 \div 5 = 7$.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: A table of a proportional relationship lists $x$ = 10, 20 and 30, with $y$ = 4, 8 and 12. What is the constant of proportionality of $y$ to $x$?

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: Omar works 2, 4 and 6 hours and earns 30, 60 and 90 dollars. The pay is proportional to the hours. What is the constant of proportionality of pay to hours?
questions.solution: Pay divided by hours: $30 \div 2 = 15$, $60 \div 4 = 15$ and $90 \div 6 = 15$. The constant is 15 dollars per hour. ($\frac{1}{15}$ is hours divided by pay.)

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A printer prints 12 pages in $\frac{1}{3}$ of a minute. How many pages does it print in 1 minute?
questions.solution: In 1 minute there are 3 thirds of a minute, so the printer prints $12 \times 3 = 36$ pages. (This is $12 \div \frac{1}{3} = 36$.)

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A pipe fills $\frac{1}{2}$ of a bucket in 2 minutes. What fraction of the bucket does it fill in 1 minute?
questions.solution: In 1 minute it fills half as much as in 2 minutes: $\frac{1}{2} \div 2 = \frac{1}{4}$ of the bucket.

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A horse eats 8 pounds of hay in $\frac{1}{2}$ of a day. How many pounds of hay does it eat in 1 day?
questions.solution: A whole day is 2 halves of a day, so the horse eats $8 \times 2 = 16$ pounds. (This is $8 \div \frac{1}{2} = 16$.)

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A runner covers $\frac{1}{4}$ mile in 2 minutes. Which expression gives the number of miles the runner covers in 1 minute?
choices: $\frac{1}{4} \times 2$
questions.solution: The unit rate is miles divided by minutes: $\frac{1}{4} \div 2 = \frac{1}{8}$ mile per minute. ($2 \div \frac{1}{4}$ would be minutes per mile.)

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A recipe uses $\frac{3}{4}$ cup of sugar to make 3 cakes. How much sugar is used for 1 cake?
choices: $\frac{1}{4}$ cup
$\frac{3}{4}$ cup
$\frac{9}{4}$ cups
4 cups
questions.answer: $\frac{1}{4}$ cup
questions.solution: Share the sugar among the 3 cakes: $\frac{3}{4} \div 3 = \frac{1}{4}$ cup for each cake.

solve.answer: $\frac{1}{4}$ cup

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: Which taxi price shows a proportional relationship between the cost of a ride and the number of miles?
choices: 5 dollars to start, plus 3 dollars for each mile
3 dollars for each mile and no other charge
4 dollars for the first mile and 2 dollars for each mile after that
12 dollars for any ride up to 6 miles
questions.answer: 3 dollars for each mile and no other charge
questions.solution: A proportional relationship has a constant cost per mile and costs 0 for 0 miles. Only "3 dollars for each mile" does: 1 mile costs 3, 2 miles cost 6, 3 miles cost 9. The others have a starting fee, a changing price per mile, or a flat price.

solve.answer: 3 dollars for each mile and no other charge
solve.work: Proportional needs cost = k x miles with 0 cost at 0 miles and a constant rate. Only 3 dollars per mile with no other charge (c = 3m).

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: A table shows the pairs $(x, y)$: $(1, 4)$, $(2, 8)$, $(3, 12)$ and $(4, 16)$. Is $y$ proportional to $x$?
choices: No, because $y$ is not equal to $x$
No, because $y$ keeps getting larger
Yes, because $y \div x$ is 4 for every pair
No, because the table has no pair with $x = 0$
questions.answer: Yes, because $y \div x$ is 4 for every pair
questions.solution: $4 \div 1$, $8 \div 2$, $12 \div 3$ and $16 \div 4$ are all 4, so $y = 4x$ and the relationship is proportional. A proportional relationship does not need $y = x$, may increase, and the table need not list $x = 0$.

solve.answer: Yes, because $y \div x$ is 4 for every pair

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: Four pairs are listed: $(2, 6)$, $(3, 9)$, $(5, 14)$ and $(6, 18)$. Three follow one proportional relationship and one does not. What is the $x$-value of the pair that does not follow it?
questions.solution: $6 \div 2 = 3$, $9 \div 3 = 3$ and $18 \div 6 = 3$, so the relationship is $y = 3x$. But $14 \div 5 = 2.8$, not 3. The pair that does not fit is $(5, 14)$, so the $x$-value is 5.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: The graph of every proportional relationship passes through the point $(0, y)$. What is the value of $y$?
questions.solution: In a proportional relationship $y = kx$. When $x = 0$, $y = k \times 0 = 0$. So every proportional relationship contains the point $(0, 0)$.

solve.work: y = kx at x = 0 gives y = 0; the graph passes through the origin.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: Each ticket to a school play costs 7 dollars. Which equation gives the total cost $y$, in dollars, of $x$ tickets?
choices: $y = \frac{x}{7}$
questions.solution: The total cost is 7 dollars times the number of tickets: $y = 7x$.

solve.work: Total = 7 x number of tickets: y = 7x.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: The cost $y$, in dollars, of $x$ gallons of fuel is given by $y = 3.5x$. What is the cost of 4 gallons?
questions.solution: Put $x = 4$ into the equation: $y = 3.5 \times 4 = 14$ dollars.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: A bakery packs 12 rolls in each box. Which equation gives the number of rolls $r$ in $b$ boxes?
questions.solution: Each box has 12 rolls, so the number of rolls is 12 times the number of boxes: $r = 12b$.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: A car's distance $d$, in miles, after $t$ hours is $d = 55t$. In how many hours has the car gone 220 miles?
questions.solution: Put $d = 220$ into the equation: $220 = 55t$, so $t = 220 \div 55 = 4$ hours.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: At Store A, 4 apples cost 2 dollars. At Store B, 5 apples cost 3 dollars. Which store charges less for each apple, and how much is it?
choices: Store B, 0.60 dollar
Store A, 2 dollars
Store B, 3 dollars
Store A, 0.50 dollar
questions.answer: Store A, 0.50 dollar
questions.solution: Store A: $2 \div 4 = 0.50$ dollar per apple. Store B: $3 \div 5 = 0.60$ dollar per apple. Store A charges less, 0.50 dollar for each apple.

solve.answer: Store A, 0.50 dollar
solve.work: A: 2/4 = 0.50 per apple. B: 3/5 = 0.60 per apple. Store A is cheaper at 0.50 dollar each.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Car A travels 120 miles in 2 hours. Car B travels 150 miles in 3 hours. Each car goes at a constant speed. How many more miles per hour does Car A travel than Car B?
questions.solution: Car A: $120 \div 2 = 60$ miles per hour. Car B: $150 \div 3 = 50$ miles per hour. Car A is $60 - 50 = 10$ miles per hour faster.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Runner P runs 30 meters in 5 seconds. Runner Q runs 35 meters in 7 seconds. Both run at constant speeds. Which statement is true?
choices: Q is faster: 7 meters per second compared with 5 meters per second
P and Q run at the same speed
Q is faster, because 35 meters is more than 30 meters
P is faster: 6 meters per second compared with 5 meters per second
questions.answer: P is faster: 6 meters per second compared with 5 meters per second
questions.solution: P runs $30 \div 5 = 6$ meters each second. Q runs $35 \div 7 = 5$ meters each second. P is faster. Q runs farther in total but takes longer.

solve.answer: P is faster: 6 meters per second compared with 5 meters per second
solve.work: P: 30/5 = 6 m/s. Q: 35/7 = 5 m/s. P faster.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Relationship A is $y = 5x$. In Relationship B, $y = 18$ when $x = 3$. Both relationships are proportional. What is the greater of the two constants of proportionality?
questions.solution: For A the constant is 5. For B it is $18 \div 3 = 6$. The greater constant is 6.

solve.work: A: k = 5. B: k = 18/3 = 6. Greater is 6.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The point $(3, 12)$ is on the graph of a proportional relationship between the hours $x$ Kim works and the dollars $y$ she earns. What does the point mean?
choices: In 12 hours, Kim earns 3 dollars
In 3 hours, Kim earns 12 dollars
Kim earns 12 dollars each hour
Kim earns 3 dollars each hour
questions.answer: In 3 hours, Kim earns 12 dollars
questions.solution: A point $(x, y)$ means $x$ hours go with $y$ dollars, so $(3, 12)$ means 3 hours earn 12 dollars. That is $12 \div 3 = 4$ dollars for each hour.

solve.answer: In 3 hours, Kim earns 12 dollars
solve.work: (x, y) = (3 hours, 12 dollars): in 3 hours she earns 12 dollars (rate 4 per hour, so the 3 and 12 per hour options are wrong).

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The graph of a proportional relationship between the pounds of grapes $x$ and the cost $y$ in dollars passes through the point $(1, 3.25)$. What is the cost, in dollars, of 4 pounds of grapes?
questions.solution: The point $(1, 3.25)$ says 1 pound costs 3.25 dollars. For 4 pounds the cost is $3.25 \times 4 = 13$ dollars.

solve.work: Unit rate 3.25 dollars per pound; 4 x 3.25 = 13.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The graph of a proportional relationship between the hours $x$ spent walking and the miles $y$ walked passes through the point $(0, 0)$. What does that point mean?
choices: After 0 hours, 0 miles have been walked
The walker walks 0 miles every hour
The walk lasts 0 hours
The walker is 0 miles from home at all times
questions.answer: After 0 hours, 0 miles have been walked
questions.solution: The point $(0, 0)$ means that when $x = 0$ hours, $y = 0$ miles. Before any time has passed, no distance has been walked.

solve.answer: After 0 hours, 0 miles have been walked
solve.work: (0, 0) = 0 hours, 0 miles: before any walking, no distance covered.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: A proportional relationship between the number of packs $x$ and the number of pens $y$ includes the point $(2, 14)$. How many pens are in 5 packs?
questions.solution: The point $(2, 14)$ says 2 packs have 14 pens, so 1 pack has $14 \div 2 = 7$ pens. Five packs have $7 \times 5 = 35$ pens.

questions.skill: Unit rate from two fractional quantities
questions.stem: Ben reads $\frac{3}{4}$ of a chapter in $\frac{1}{2}$ hour. At this rate, how many chapters does he read in 1 hour?
questions.solution: The unit rate is $\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{4} \times 2 = \frac{3}{2}$, which is $1\frac{1}{2}$ chapters per hour.

questions.skill: Write an equation y = kx for a proportional situation
questions.stem: Ribbon is sold at a constant price per meter. 4 meters cost 10 dollars. Which equation gives the cost $y$, in dollars, of $x$ meters of ribbon?
questions.solution: The price for 1 meter is $10 \div 4 = 2.5$ dollars, so $k = 2.5$ and $y = 2.5x$. Check: $x = 4$ gives $y = 10$.

solve.work: Unit price = 10/4 = 2.5 dollars per meter, proportional, so y = 2.5x. Check: 2.5 x 4 = 10.

questions.skill: Interpret a point on a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: A proportional relationship between hours worked $x$ and pay $y$, in dollars, includes the point $(4, 52)$. How many dollars is the pay for 1 hour of work?
questions.solution: The point $(4, 52)$ means 4 hours earn 52 dollars. The pay for 1 hour is the unit rate $52 \div 4 = 13$ dollars.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: Dana bikes at a constant speed. Her distance $d$, in miles, after $t$ hours is $d = 12t$. Which statement is true?
choices: She bikes for 12 hours in all
She bikes 12 miles in all
She bikes 12 miles each hour
She starts 12 miles from home
questions.answer: She bikes 12 miles each hour
questions.solution: In $d = 12t$ the distance is 12 times the time, so the number 12 is the miles she bikes in each hour. It does not tell how long she bikes in all or where she starts.

solve.answer: She bikes 12 miles each hour
solve.work: d = 12t: the rate is 12 miles per hour. Time and total distance are not given; d = 0 at t = 0, so she starts at home.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y \div x$ is the same for every pair. One pair is $(6, 15)$ and another pair is $(10, y)$. What is $y$?
questions.solution: $y \div x = 15 \div 6 = 2.5$ for every pair. So $y = 2.5 \times 10 = 25$.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: Which statement is true for every proportional relationship between $x$ and $y$?
choices: $y - x$ is the same for every pair
$y \div x$ is the same for every pair
$y$ is always greater than $x$
$x$ is always a factor of $y$
questions.answer: $y \div x$ is the same for every pair
questions.solution: The quotient $y \div x$ is the constant of proportionality, so it is the same for every pair. The difference $y - x$ changes, $y$ can be less than $x$ (for example $y = 0.5x$), and $x$ need not divide $y$ (for example $y = 1.5x$).

solve.answer: $y \div x$ is the same for every pair
solve.work: Proportional means y = kx, so y/x = k for every pair (x not 0). Differences vary; x need not be a factor; k < 1 makes y < x.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: Gasoline costs the same amount for each gallon. 6 gallons cost 21 dollars. How many dollars do 10 gallons cost?
questions.solution: One gallon costs $21 \div 6 = 3.5$ dollars. Ten gallons cost $3.5 \times 10 = 35$ dollars.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y = 10$ when $x = 3$, $y = 20$ when $x = 6$ and $y = 30$ when $x = 9$. What is the constant of proportionality $k$ in $y = kx$? Give it as a fraction.
questions.solution: $k = y \div x = 10 \div 3 = \frac{10}{3}$. Check: $20 \div 6 = \frac{10}{3}$ and $30 \div 9 = \frac{10}{3}$.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: Which set of pairs $(x, y)$ shows a proportional relationship with a constant of proportionality of 2.5?
questions.solution: Check $y \div x$ for each pair. In the first set it is $5 \div 2$, $10 \div 4$ and $15 \div 6$, all 2.5. The second set always has $y = x + 2.5$, the third has a constant of 0.4, and in the fourth $14 \div 6$ is not 2.5.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y = 28$ when $x = 8$, and $y = 42$ when $x = 12$. What is the constant of proportionality?

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: Omar reads 6 pages in 15 minutes, 12 pages in 30 minutes and 18 pages in 45 minutes. The pages are proportional to the minutes. What is the constant of proportionality of pages to minutes?
questions.solution: Pages divided by minutes: $6 \div 15 = 0.4$, $12 \div 30 = 0.4$ and $18 \div 45 = 0.4$. (2.5 is minutes divided by pages, 9 is $15 - 6$, and 21 is $15 + 6$.)

solve.work: pages = k x minutes: k = 6/15 = 12/30 = 18/45 = 0.4 pages per minute. (2.5 is minutes per page, the reverse.) Same 'of y to x' convention as Q16/Q17.

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A hiker walks $1\frac{1}{2}$ miles in $\frac{3}{4}$ of an hour at a steady pace. How many miles does the hiker walk in 1 hour?
questions.solution: Unit rate = miles divided by hours = $1\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{3}{4} = \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{4}{3} = 2$ miles per hour.

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A recipe uses $\frac{2}{3}$ cup of oil for every $\frac{1}{2}$ of a batch. How many cups of oil are needed for 1 whole batch?
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{3} \times 2 = \frac{4}{3}$ cups, which is $1\frac{1}{3}$ cups.

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A painter covers $\frac{2}{3}$ of a wall with $\frac{1}{4}$ gallon of paint. How many walls can be covered with 1 gallon of paint?
questions.solution: Walls per gallon is $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{3} \times 4 = \frac{8}{3}$. ($\frac{3}{8}$ is gallons per wall, $\frac{1}{6}$ is the product and $\frac{11}{12}$ is the sum.)

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: $\frac{3}{4}$ pound of cheese costs 6 dollars. How many dollars does 1 pound of the cheese cost?
questions.solution: $6 \div \frac{3}{4} = 6 \times \frac{4}{3} = 8$ dollars per pound. (Check: $\frac{3}{4}$ of 8 is 6.)

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A machine fills $\frac{1}{2}$ of a tank in 3 minutes. How many minutes does it take to fill 1 whole tank at this rate?
questions.solution: A whole tank is twice as much as half a tank, so it takes twice as long: $3 \div \frac{1}{2} = 6$ minutes. ($\frac{1}{6}$ is the fraction of a tank filled each minute.)

solve.work: Half a tank in 3 min, so a whole tank in 3 / (1/2) = 6 min.

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A bamboo plant grows $\frac{3}{8}$ inch in $\frac{1}{4}$ of a day. How many inches does it grow in 1 day?
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{8} \div \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{8} \times 4 = \frac{12}{8} = \frac{3}{2}$ inches, which is $1\frac{1}{2}$ inches.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: Which equation represents a proportional relationship?
questions.solution: A proportional relationship has the form $y = kx$: $y$ is a constant times $x$ with nothing added or subtracted. Only $y = 0.75x$ has that form.

solve.work: Only y = 0.75x has the form y = kx; the others have a constant added or subtracted.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: Which description of a graph shows a proportional relationship?
choices: A straight line that crosses the $y$-axis at $(0, 3)$
A straight line that passes through the origin
A curve that passes through the origin
A straight line that passes through $(1, 0)$
questions.answer: A straight line that passes through the origin
questions.solution: The graph of a proportional relationship is a straight line through the origin $(0, 0)$. A line crossing the $y$-axis at $(0, 3)$ or passing through $(1, 0)$ does not go through the origin, and a curve is not a straight line.

solve.answer: A straight line that passes through the origin
solve.work: A proportional graph is a straight line through the origin. (0,3) and (1,0) lines miss the origin; a curve is not proportional.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: Only one of these sets of three points lies on the graph of a proportional relationship. Which set is it?
questions.solution: In the first set $y \div x$ is 6 each time: $3 \div 0.5$, $12 \div 2$ and $21 \div 3.5$. In the others the quotient changes: the second set follows $y = x + 2.5$, the third ends with $20 \div 3.5$, which is not 6, and the fourth follows $y = 6x + 1$.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: For a proportional relationship, the pairs $(2, 7)$, $(4, 14)$ and $(6, c)$ must have the same $y \div x$. What is $c$?
questions.solution: $y \div x = 7 \div 2 = 3.5$ for the first pair (and $14 \div 4 = 3.5$). So $c = 3.5 \times 6 = 21$.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: The five pairs $(2, 5)$, $(4, 10)$, $(6, 14)$, $(8, 20)$ and $(10, 24)$ are tested against the rule $y = 2.5x$. How many of the pairs follow the rule?
questions.solution: Compute $2.5x$ for each: $2.5 \times 2 = 5$ (yes), $2.5 \times 4 = 10$ (yes), $2.5 \times 6 = 15$ but $y = 14$ (no), $2.5 \times 8 = 20$ (yes), $2.5 \times 10 = 25$ but $y = 24$ (no). Three pairs follow the rule.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y = 2$ when $x = 3$, $y = 4$ when $x = 6$ and $y = 6$ when $x = 9$. Which equation matches?
questions.solution: $k = y \div x = 2 \div 3 = \frac{2}{3}$, and $4 \div 6$ and $6 \div 9$ agree. So $y = \frac{2}{3}x$. ($y = \frac{3}{2}x$ has the constant upside down.)

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: A canoe rental costs the same amount for each hour. The cost $c$, in dollars, for $h$ hours is $c = 6.5h$. Jo pays 52 dollars. For how many hours does Jo rent the canoe?
questions.solution: Put $c = 52$ into the equation: $52 = 6.5h$, so $h = 52 \div 6.5 = 8$ hours.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. Which equation gives the cups of flour $f$ needed for $s$ cups of sugar?
questions.solution: There are $\frac{3}{2}$ cups of flour for each cup of sugar, so $f = \frac{3}{2}s$. ($f = \frac{2}{3}s$ and $s = \frac{3}{2}f$ have the quantities the wrong way round.)

solve.work: f/s = 3/2, so f = (3/2)s. Check s = 2: f = 3.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: The equation $y = kx$ fits a table where $y = 5.4$ when $x = 3$, $y = 9$ when $x = 5$ and $y = 14.4$ when $x = 8$. What is $y$ when $x = 12$?

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Machine A fills $y$ liters in $x$ minutes, where $y = 2.4x$. Machine B fills 11 liters in 5 minutes. Both work at constant rates. Which statement is true?
choices: Machine A fills 0.2 liter more each minute than Machine B
Machine B fills 0.2 liter more each minute than Machine A
Machine A fills 1 liter more each minute than Machine B
The two machines fill at the same rate
questions.answer: Machine A fills 0.2 liter more each minute than Machine B
questions.solution: Machine A fills 2.4 liters each minute. Machine B fills $11 \div 5 = 2.2$ liters each minute. A fills $2.4 - 2.2 = 0.2$ liter more each minute. (In 5 minutes A fills 12 liters, 1 more than B, but that is not the amount per minute.)

solve.answer: Machine A fills 0.2 liter more each minute than Machine B
solve.work: A: 2.4 L/min. B: 11/5 = 2.2 L/min. A fills 0.2 L more each minute.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: A car travels at a constant speed given by $d = 48t$, where $d$ is miles and $t$ is hours. A truck travels 135 miles in 3 hours at a constant speed. In 5 hours, how many more miles does the car travel than the truck?
questions.solution: In 5 hours the car travels $48 \times 5 = 240$ miles. The truck goes $135 \div 3 = 45$ miles each hour, so $45 \times 5 = 225$ miles. The car goes $240 - 225 = 15$ miles farther.

solve.work: Car 48 mph; truck 135/3 = 45 mph. In 5 h: 240 - 225 = 15 miles.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Plant A grows 12 cm in 4 weeks. Plant B grows $h$ cm in $w$ weeks, where $h = 2.5w$. Plant C grows 7 cm in 2 weeks. All grow at constant rates. Which plant grows the least each week?
choices: Plant A
Plant B
Plant C
All three grow equally fast
questions.answer: Plant B
questions.solution: Plant A grows $12 \div 4 = 3$ cm a week, Plant B grows 2.5 cm a week and Plant C grows $7 \div 2 = 3.5$ cm a week. Plant B grows the least.

solve.answer: Plant B
solve.work: A: 12/4 = 3 cm/wk. B: 2.5 cm/wk. C: 7/2 = 3.5 cm/wk. Least is B.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The graph of a proportional relationship between the cups of flour $x$ and the loaves of bread $y$ has the equation $y = 1.5x$. Which point on the graph shows the number of loaves made from 1 cup of flour?
questions.solution: The point for 1 cup of flour has $x = 1$, and then $y = 1.5 \times 1 = 1.5$. So the point is $(1, 1.5)$. The point $(2, 3)$ is on the graph but shows 2 cups, and $(1.5, 1)$ and $(0, 1.5)$ are not on the graph.

solve.work: x = 1 cup gives y = 1.5 loaves: point (1, 1.5).

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The point $(4, 10)$ is on the graph of a proportional relationship between the miles $x$ a bus travels and the minutes $y$ it takes. How many minutes does the bus take to travel 6.4 miles?
questions.solution: $(4, 10)$ says 4 miles take 10 minutes, so 1 mile takes $10 \div 4 = 2.5$ minutes. For 6.4 miles: $2.5 \times 6.4 = 16$ minutes.

solve.work: k = 10/4 = 2.5 minutes per mile; 6.4 x 2.5 = 16 minutes.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The point $(8, 6)$ is on the graph of a proportional relationship between the laps $x$ a runner completes and the minutes $y$ it takes. Which statement is true?
choices: Each lap takes $\frac{3}{4}$ minute
Each lap takes $\frac{4}{3}$ minutes
The runner completes $\frac{3}{4}$ lap each minute
Each lap takes 2 minutes
questions.answer: Each lap takes $\frac{3}{4}$ minute
questions.solution: 8 laps take 6 minutes, so one lap takes $6 \div 8 = \frac{3}{4}$ minute. (The runner completes $8 \div 6 = \frac{4}{3}$ laps each minute.)

solve.answer: Each lap takes $\frac{3}{4}$ minute
solve.work: 8 laps take 6 minutes: 6/8 = 3/4 minute per lap. Laps per minute = 8/6 = 4/3, so the 3/4 lap per minute option is false, as are 4/3 and 2 minutes per lap.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The points $(2, 7)$ and $(a, 24.5)$ are both on the graph of the same proportional relationship. What is $a$?

questions.skill: Compare a unit rate from a description with one from an equation
questions.stem: Store A sells 3 pounds of apples for 7.50 dollars. At Store B, the cost $y$ in dollars of $x$ pounds is given by $y = 2.4x$. Which statement is true?
choices: Store A costs 0.10 dollars less per pound.
Store B costs 0.10 dollars less per pound.
Store B costs 5.10 dollars less per pound.
The two stores charge the same price per pound.
questions.answer: Store B costs 0.10 dollars less per pound.
questions.solution: Store A: $7.50 \div 3 = 2.50$ dollars per pound. Store B: $k = 2.4$ dollars per pound. Store B is cheaper by $2.50 - 2.40 = 0.10$ dollars per pound.

solve.answer: Store B costs 0.10 dollars less per pound.
solve.work: Store A: 7.50/3 = 2.50 dollars per pound. Store B: 2.40 per pound. B is cheaper by 2.50 - 2.40 = 0.10 dollars per pound.

questions.skill: Use a unit rate with decimals to find a missing value
questions.stem: A paint covers an area proportional to the amount used. 3.5 liters of paint cover 5.6 square meters. At this rate, how many square meters can 8 liters of paint cover?
questions.solution: One liter covers $5.6 \div 3.5 = 1.6$ square meters. So 8 liters cover $1.6 \times 8 = 12.8$ square meters.

solve.work: Rate = 5.6/3.5 = 1.6 square meters per liter. 8 x 1.6 = 12.8.

questions.skill: Find another point on a proportional relationship
questions.stem: A proportional relationship includes the point $(6, 15)$. Which point is also on this relationship?
questions.solution: The constant of proportionality is $15 \div 6 = 2.5$, so $y = 2.5x$. For $x = 4$, $y = 2.5 \times 4 = 10$, so $(4, 10)$ is on it. The other points do not have $y \div x = 2.5$.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: A proportional relationship has the pairs $(2, 5)$, $(4, 10)$ and $(6, 15)$. Which statement about it is NOT true?
choices: $y - x$ is the same for every pair
$y \div x$ is 2.5 for every pair
$y$ is 2.5 times as large as $x$
When $x$ goes up by 2, $y$ goes up by 5
questions.answer: $y - x$ is the same for every pair
questions.solution: The differences $y - x$ are 3, 6 and 9, so they are not the same. The other statements are true: $5 \div 2$, $10 \div 4$ and $15 \div 6$ are all 2.5, and each time $x$ goes up by 2, $y$ goes up by 5.

solve.answer: $y - x$ is the same for every pair
solve.work: y/x = 5/2 = 10/4 = 15/6 = 2.5 (true). y - x = 3, 6, 9: not the same, so that statement is NOT true. x up 2 gives y up 5 (true). y = 2.5x (true).

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y = 1.5$ when $x = 0.4$. What is $y$ when $x = 2.4$?

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: The ratio $y : x$ is always $3 : 4$ in a proportional relationship. Which pair could be $(x, y)$?
questions.solution: The ratio $y : x$ is $3 : 4$, so $y$ is $\frac{3}{4}$ of $x$. For $(12, 9)$, $9 : 12 = 3 : 4$. The pair $(9, 12)$ has the numbers reversed, and $(12, 11)$ and $(4, 7)$ come from subtracting or adding instead of using the ratio.

questions.skill: What stays constant in a proportional relationship
questions.stem: The cost is proportional to the number of items bought. 5 items cost 12 dollars. How many items can be bought for 28.8 dollars?
questions.solution: One item costs $12 \div 5 = 2.4$ dollars. The number of items for 28.8 dollars is $28.8 \div 2.4 = 12$.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: In a proportional relationship, $y = 2.4$ when $x = 0.6$. What is the constant of proportionality $k$ in $y = kx$?
questions.solution: $k = y \div x = 2.4 \div 0.6 = 4$. (Multiply both by 10 to get $24 \div 6 = 4$.)

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: A table for a proportional relationship lists $y = 11.2$ when $x = 2$, $y = 28$ when $x = 5$ and $y = 44.8$ when $x = 8$. What is the constant of proportionality?

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: A proportional relationship has the pairs $(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{5}{6})$, $(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{5}{3})$ and $(1, \frac{5}{2})$. What is the constant of proportionality?
questions.solution: $k = y \div x$. For the first pair, $\frac{5}{6} \div \frac{1}{3} = \frac{5}{6} \times 3 = \frac{5}{2}$. The last pair gives $\frac{5}{2} \div 1 = \frac{5}{2}$ as well.

questions.skill: Constant of proportionality from a table or ordered pairs
questions.stem: In the proportional relationship $y = 2.5x$, $x$ can also be written as a multiple of $y$: $x = ky$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: Divide both sides of $y = 2.5x$ by 2.5 to get $x = \frac{1}{2.5}y = 0.4y$. So $k = 0.4$. (2.5 is the constant the other way around, and the others do not come from $1 \div 2.5$.)

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: Lena walks $\frac{3}{4}$ mile in 15 minutes at a steady pace. At this rate, how many miles does she walk in 1 hour?
questions.solution: 15 minutes is $\frac{1}{4}$ of an hour. Miles per hour = $\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{1}{4} = 3$ miles. (Or: 1 hour is 4 times 15 minutes, so $\frac{3}{4} \times 4 = 3$.)

solve.work: 1 hour = 60 min = 4 x 15 min; 4 x 3/4 = 3 miles.

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A tap fills $1\frac{1}{2}$ liters in $\frac{3}{8}$ of a minute. At this rate, how many liters does it fill in $2\frac{1}{2}$ minutes?
questions.solution: Liters per minute = $1\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{3}{8} = \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{8}{3} = 4$. In $2\frac{1}{2}$ minutes the tap fills $4 \times 2.5 = 10$ liters.

solve.work: Rate = (3/2) / (3/8) = 4 liters per minute; 4 x 5/2 = 10 liters.

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: A car uses $\frac{3}{5}$ gallon of gas to travel 12 miles. Which statement is correct?
choices: The car travels $\frac{1}{20}$ mile on 1 gallon
The car travels 7.2 miles on 1 gallon
The car travels 20 miles on 1 gallon
The car travels 12 miles on 1 gallon
questions.answer: The car travels 20 miles on 1 gallon
questions.solution: Miles per gallon = $12 \div \frac{3}{5} = 12 \times \frac{5}{3} = 20$. ($\frac{1}{20}$ is gallons per mile, and 7.2 is $12 \times \frac{3}{5}$.)

solve.answer: The car travels 20 miles on 1 gallon

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: Which rate is the same as walking $\frac{2}{3}$ mile in $\frac{1}{4}$ hour?
choices: $\frac{1}{6}$ mile in 1 hour
$\frac{3}{8}$ mile in 1 hour
$\frac{2}{3}$ mile in 1 hour
4 miles in $1\frac{1}{2}$ hours
questions.answer: 4 miles in $1\frac{1}{2}$ hours
questions.solution: The speed is $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{4} = \frac{8}{3}$ miles per hour. For 4 miles in $1\frac{1}{2}$ hours, $4 \div \frac{3}{2} = \frac{8}{3}$ as well. The others are $\frac{1}{6}$, $\frac{3}{8}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$ miles per hour.

solve.answer: 4 miles in $1\frac{1}{2}$ hours

questions.skill: Unit rate with fractions
questions.stem: Pat reads $\frac{1}{6}$ of a book in $\frac{1}{4}$ of an hour. At this rate, how many hours will it take Pat to read the whole book?
questions.solution: The whole book is 6 times $\frac{1}{6}$ of the book, so it takes 6 times as long: $6 \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{2}$ hours, which is $1\frac{1}{2}$ hours.

solve.work: Whole book = 6 sixths; 6 x 1/4 = 3/2 = 1.5 hours. (Rate 2/3 book per hour; 1 / (2/3) = 1.5.)

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: Maria looks at the pairs $(1, 5)$, $(2, 9)$, $(3, 13)$ and $(4, 17)$. She says $y$ is proportional to $x$ because $y$ goes up by the same amount, 4, each time $x$ goes up by 1. Which is correct?
choices: She is right, because the change in $y$ is always the same
She is wrong, because $y$ must stay the same when $x$ goes up
She is right, because $y$ is always greater than $x$
She is wrong, because $y \div x$ is not the same for every pair
questions.answer: She is wrong, because $y \div x$ is not the same for every pair
questions.solution: $y \div x$ is $5$, $4.5$, $\frac{13}{3}$ and $4.25$, which are not equal. The relationship is $y = 4x + 1$, a straight line that does not pass through the origin. A constant change in $y$ alone does not make a relationship proportional.

solve.answer: She is wrong, because $y \div x$ is not the same for every pair
solve.work: y/x = 5, 4.5, 13/3, 4.25: not constant (y = 4x + 1, not through origin). She is wrong for that reason.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: The pairs $(6, 4)$, $(9, 6)$ and $(15, 10)$ are given. Which statement, true for every pair, shows that $y$ is proportional to $x$?
choices: $y \div x$ equals $\frac{2}{3}$
$y$ is larger when $x$ is larger
$x - y$ is the same
$x$ is a multiple of 3
questions.answer: $y \div x$ equals $\frac{2}{3}$
questions.solution: $4 \div 6$, $6 \div 9$ and $10 \div 15$ all equal $\frac{2}{3}$, which is what proportional means. The other statements do not show it: $x - y$ is 2, 3 and 5 (not the same), and "larger $x$ gives larger $y$" and "$x$ is a multiple of 3" do not show a constant ratio.

solve.answer: $y \div x$ equals $\frac{2}{3}$
solve.work: 4/6 = 6/9 = 10/15 = 2/3, constant, which shows proportionality. x - y = 2, 3, 5 not same. 'x multiple of 3' and 'y larger when x larger' are true but do not show proportionality.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: A table has the pairs $(0.4, 1)$, $(1.2, 3)$ and $(x, 7.5)$. If $y$ is proportional to $x$, what is $x$?

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: The pairs $(2, 9)$, $(4, 17)$ and $(6, 25)$ are not proportional. If $y$ were proportional to $x$ and passed through $(2, 9)$, its $y$ at $x = 6$ would be greater than 25. By how much?
questions.solution: If $y$ were proportional through $(2, 9)$, then $y \div x = 4.5$ and at $x = 6$ we would get $y = 4.5 \times 6 = 27$. That is $27 - 25 = 2$ more than 25.

questions.skill: Test whether a relationship is proportional
questions.stem: Which equation does NOT represent a proportional relationship?
choices: $y = \frac{x}{3}$
questions.solution: $y = \frac{x + 2}{3}$ is the same as $y = \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{2}{3}$, which has $\frac{2}{3}$ added, so $y = \frac{2}{3}$ when $x = 0$ and $y \div x$ is not constant. The others are $y = kx$ with $k = \frac{1}{3}$, $1.2$ and $\frac{2}{5}$.

solve.work: 1.2x, 2x/5 = 0.4x, x/3 are all kx. (x + 2)/3 = x/3 + 2/3 has a constant term: not proportional.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: The graph of a proportional relationship passes through the point $(5, 12)$. Which equation represents the relationship?
questions.solution: $k = y \div x = 12 \div 5 = 2.4$, so $y = 2.4x$. Check with the point: $2.4 \times 5 = 12$. ($y = 7x$ uses the difference $12 - 5$ as the constant.)

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: A proportional relationship is given by $y = \frac{5}{8}x$. What is $x$ when $y = 15$?
questions.solution: Put $y = 15$ into the equation: $15 = \frac{5}{8}x$. Multiply both sides by $\frac{8}{5}$: $x = 15 \times \frac{8}{5} = 24$.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: A pool fills at 12 gallons per minute, so the gallons $g$ in the pool after $m$ minutes is $g = 12m$. Which equation gives the minutes $m$ in terms of the gallons $g$?
questions.solution: Divide both sides of $g = 12m$ by 12 to get $m = \frac{g}{12}$.

questions.skill: Write and use an equation y = kx
questions.stem: The price $p$, in dollars, of $n$ pencils is $p = 0.35n$. How many more dollars do 12 pencils cost than 8 pencils?
questions.solution: 12 pencils cost $0.35 \times 12 = 4.20$ dollars and 8 pencils cost $0.35 \times 8 = 2.80$ dollars. The difference is $4.20 - 2.80 = 1.40$ dollars.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Tap A fills $2\frac{1}{2}$ liters in $\frac{1}{2}$ of a minute. Tap B fills $4\frac{1}{2}$ liters in $\frac{3}{4}$ of a minute. How many more liters per minute does the faster tap fill than the slower tap?
questions.solution: Tap A: $2\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{2} = 5$ liters per minute. Tap B: $4\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{2} \times \frac{4}{3} = 6$ liters per minute. Tap B is faster, by $6 - 5 = 1$ liter per minute.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Runner P runs $d$ kilometers in $m$ minutes, where $d = 0.15m$. Runner Q runs 2.4 kilometers in 15 minutes. Runner R runs 3.5 kilometers in 25 minutes. All run at constant speeds. Who runs the most kilometers each minute?
choices: Runner P
Runner R
Runner Q
Runners P and Q tie
questions.answer: Runner Q
questions.solution: P runs 0.15 kilometer each minute. Q runs $2.4 \div 15 = 0.16$ kilometer each minute. R runs $3.5 \div 25 = 0.14$ kilometer each minute. Q is the fastest.

solve.answer: Runner Q

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: The graph of Line 1 passes through the origin and $(4, 10)$. The graph of Line 2 passes through the origin and $(10, 24)$. Which statement is true?
choices: Line 2 has the greater constant of proportionality, 24 compared with 10
The two lines have the same constant of proportionality
Line 1 has the greater constant of proportionality, 2.5 compared with 2.4
Line 2 has the greater constant of proportionality, 10 compared with 4
questions.answer: Line 1 has the greater constant of proportionality, 2.5 compared with 2.4
questions.solution: Line 1: $k = 10 \div 4 = 2.5$. Line 2: $k = 24 \div 10 = 2.4$. Line 1 has the greater constant of proportionality. Comparing the points' numbers directly does not compare the constants.

solve.answer: Line 1 has the greater constant of proportionality, 2.5 compared with 2.4
solve.work: Line 1: k = 10/4 = 2.5. Line 2: k = 24/10 = 2.4. Line 1 greater.

questions.skill: Compare proportional relationships
questions.stem: Plan A charges 0.07 dollar for each text message. Plan B charges 3 dollars for every 50 messages. Tina sends 500 messages. How many dollars cheaper is Plan B than Plan A?
questions.solution: Plan A: $0.07 \times 500 = 35$ dollars. Plan B: $3 \div 50 = 0.06$ dollar per message, so $0.06 \times 500 = 30$ dollars. Plan B is $35 - 30 = 5$ dollars cheaper.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The point $(1.5, 9)$ is on the graph of a proportional relationship between the hours $x$ and the gallons $y$ of water a pump moves. Which statement is true?
choices: The pump moves 9 gallons each hour
The pump moves 13.5 gallons each hour
The pump moves 6 gallons each hour
The pump moves 1.5 gallons each hour
questions.answer: The pump moves 6 gallons each hour
questions.solution: 1.5 hours move 9 gallons, so each hour the pump moves $9 \div 1.5 = 6$ gallons. (13.5 is $1.5 \times 9$.)

solve.answer: The pump moves 6 gallons each hour

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The point $(\frac{2}{3}, 5)$ is on the graph of a proportional relationship. What is the value of $y$ when $x = 1$?
questions.solution: $k = y \div x = 5 \div \frac{2}{3} = 5 \times \frac{3}{2} = 7.5$. When $x = 1$, $y = 7.5 \times 1 = 7.5$.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: Which pair of points can both be on the graph of one proportional relationship?
questions.solution: Both points must have the same $y \div x$. For $(4, 6)$ it is $1.5$, and for $(14, 21)$ it is $21 \div 14 = 1.5$. The others have $y \div x$ of $\frac{8}{7}$ (adding 2 to both), $\frac{2}{3}$ (the numbers swapped) and $1.4$.

questions.skill: Interpret a point of a proportional relationship in context
questions.stem: The point $(12, 7.2)$ is on the graph of a proportional relationship between the ounces $x$ of cheese and the cost $y$ in dollars. What is the cost of 25 ounces of the cheese?
questions.solution: $12$ ounces cost 7.2 dollars, so 1 ounce costs $7.2 \div 12 = 0.6$ dollar. For 25 ounces: $0.6 \times 25 = 15$ dollars.

questions.skill: Use a map scale
questions.stem: On a map, 1 centimeter stands for 5 kilometers. Two towns are 6 centimeters apart on the map. How many kilometers apart are the towns?
questions.solution: Each map centimeter is 5 kilometers, so 6 centimeters is $6 \times 5 = 30$ kilometers.

questions.skill: Find a tip as a percent
questions.stem: A meal costs 40 dollars. Sam leaves a tip of 15% of the cost of the meal. How many dollars is the tip?
questions.solution: 15% of 40 is $0.15 \times 40 = 6$ dollars.

questions.skill: Find a total price with sales tax
questions.stem: A book costs 20 dollars before tax. The sales tax is 8%. What is the total cost of the book with tax, in dollars?
questions.solution: The tax is 8% of 20, which is $0.08 \times 20 = 1.60$ dollars. The total is $20 + 1.60 = 21.60$ dollars. (Or multiply by $1.08$.)

questions.skill: How a scale changes area
questions.stem: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 4 km. A lake covers 6.5 square centimeters on the map. What is the real area of the lake, in square kilometers?
questions.solution: Each square centimeter on the map stands for $4 \times 4 = 16$ square kilometers. The lake is $6.5 \times 16 = 104$ square kilometers.

questions.skill: How a scale changes area
questions.stem: A real garden has an area of 360 square meters. A scale drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 6 m. What is the area of the garden on the drawing, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each square centimeter on the drawing stands for $6 \times 6 = 36$ square meters. So the drawing has an area of $360 \div 36 = 10$ square centimeters.

solve.work: 1 sq cm = 6 x 6 = 36 sq m; 360/36 = 10 sq cm.

questions.skill: How a scale changes area
questions.stem: A designer shrinks a rectangle so that every side is $\frac{1}{3}$ as long as before. The new area is what fraction of the old area?
questions.solution: Both the length and the width are multiplied by $\frac{1}{3}$, so the area is multiplied by $\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{9}$.

questions.skill: How a scale changes area
questions.stem: On a scale drawing, a room has an area of 8 square inches. The real room has an area of 288 square feet. What is the scale of the drawing?
choices: 1 inch : 36 feet
1 inch : 280 feet
1 inch : 6 feet
1 inch : 18 feet
questions.answer: 1 inch : 6 feet
questions.solution: 288 square feet is shown by 8 square inches, so 1 square inch stands for $288 \div 8 = 36$ square feet. A square that is 1 inch on each side stands for a square that is 6 feet on each side, because $6 \times 6 = 36$. The scale is 1 inch : 6 feet.

solve.answer: 1 inch : 6 feet
solve.work: 288/8 = 36 sq ft per sq in, so 1 inch stands for 6 ft (6 x 6 = 36).

questions.skill: Sales tax and tip
questions.stem: Mia's meal costs 36 dollars before tax. The sales tax is 7.5%, and she leaves a tip of 15% of the cost before tax. What is the total she pays, in dollars?
questions.solution: The tax is $36 \times 0.075 = 2.70$ dollars. The tip is $36 \times 0.15 = 5.40$ dollars. The total is $36 + 2.70 + 5.40 = 44.10$ dollars.

questions.skill: Sales tax and tip
questions.stem: A jacket's total price, including 8% sales tax, is 54 dollars. What was the price of the jacket before tax, in dollars?
questions.solution: The total is 108% of the price before tax, so the price is $54 \div 1.08 = 50$ dollars. Check: 8% of 50 is 4, and $50 + 4 = 54$.

questions.skill: Sales tax and tip
questions.stem: A group's bill is 64 dollars before tax. The sales tax is 7%, and the tip is 20% of the cost before tax. Four friends split the total equally. How many dollars does each friend pay?
questions.solution: The tax is $64 \times 0.07 = 4.48$ and the tip is $64 \times 0.20 = 12.80$. The total is $64 + 4.48 + 12.80 = 81.28$ dollars. Each friend pays $81.28 \div 4 = 20.32$ dollars. (81.28 is the whole bill, 17.12 leaves out the tip and 19.20 leaves out the tax.)

questions.skill: Markup and discount
questions.stem: A store marks up the cost of a chair by 35% and sells it for 81 dollars. What did the store pay for the chair, in dollars?
questions.solution: The selling price is 135% of the cost, so the cost is $81 \div 1.35 = 60$ dollars. Check: 35% of 60 is 21, and $60 + 21 = 81$.

questions.skill: Markup and discount
questions.stem: After a 15% discount, a scooter sells for 68 dollars. What was the price before the discount, in dollars?
questions.solution: The sale price is 85% of the original price, so the original price is $68 \div 0.85 = 80$ dollars. Check: 15% of 80 is 12, and $80 - 12 = 68$.

questions.skill: Markup and discount
questions.stem: A 50 dollar item is discounted by 20%. Then the new price is discounted by a further 10%. What is the final price, in dollars?
questions.solution: After 20% off, the price is $50 \times 0.8 = 40$ dollars. The further 10% off 40 dollars is 4 dollars, so the final price is $40 - 4 = 36$ dollars. (35 adds the discounts to make 30% off.)

questions.skill: Markup and discount
questions.stem: A store marks up an item by 50% of its cost. Later it sells the item at 50% off that marked-up price. Compared with what the store paid, the final price is...
choices: the same as the cost
25% less than the cost
25% more than the cost
50% less than the cost
questions.answer: 25% less than the cost
questions.solution: With a cost of 100, the marked-up price is 150. Half off is 75. Compared with the cost of 100, 75 is 25% less.

solve.answer: 25% less than the cost
solve.work: Cost c: marked up to 1.5c, then 0.5 x 1.5c = 0.75c, which is 25% less than the cost.

questions.skill: Commission
questions.stem: Plan A pays a commission of 8% of sales. Plan B pays 150 dollars plus a commission of 3% of sales. Jin's sales are 2000 dollars. How many more dollars would Plan B pay than Plan A?
questions.solution: Plan A pays 8% of 2000, which is 160 dollars. Plan B pays $150 + 0.03 \times 2000 = 150 + 60 = 210$ dollars. Plan B pays $210 - 160 = 50$ dollars more.

questions.skill: Commission
questions.stem: Maya is paid 120 dollars a week plus a commission of 4% of her sales. How many dollars of sales does she need in a week to earn 200 dollars in all?
questions.solution: She needs $200 - 120 = 80$ dollars from commission. 4% of her sales must be 80 dollars, so her sales are $80 \div 0.04 = 2000$ dollars.

questions.skill: Commission
questions.stem: A salesperson earns 5% commission on the first 1000 dollars of sales in a week and 8% on all sales over 1000 dollars. In one week the sales are 1500 dollars. How many dollars is the commission?
questions.solution: On the first 1000 dollars: $1000 \times 0.05 = 50$ dollars. On the other 500 dollars: $500 \times 0.08 = 40$ dollars. The total is $50 + 40 = 90$ dollars.

questions.skill: Percent increase and decrease
questions.stem: A town's population grew from 2500 to 3150. What is the percent increase?
questions.solution: The increase is $3150 - 2500 = 650$ people. As a fraction of the original 2500 it is $650 \div 2500 = 0.26$, which is 26%.

questions.skill: Percent increase and decrease
questions.stem: After a 12% decrease, a number is 66. What was the number before the decrease?
questions.solution: After a 12% decrease the number is 88% of the original, so the original is $66 \div 0.88 = 75$. Check: 12% of 75 is 9, and $75 - 9 = 66$.

questions.skill: Percent increase and decrease
questions.stem: A price goes up by 20%, and then the new price goes down by 20%. Compared with the starting price, the final price is...
choices: the same as the starting price
4% less than the starting price
4% more than the starting price
20% more than the starting price
questions.answer: 4% less than the starting price
questions.solution: Start with 100. Up 20% gives 120. Down 20% of 120 is 24, which gives 96. Compared with 100, 96 is 4% less.

solve.answer: 4% less than the starting price

questions.skill: Percent increase and decrease
questions.stem: A hiker's pack weighs 8 pounds. After adding supplies, it weighs 11 pounds. What is the percent increase in its weight?
questions.solution: The increase is $11 - 8 = 3$ pounds. As a fraction of the original 8 pounds it is $3 \div 8 = 0.375$, which is 37.5%. (27.3% comes from dividing by the new weight, 11.)

questions.skill: Percent increase and decrease
questions.stem: Which is the greater percent increase: from 40 to 50, or from 20 to 26?
choices: From 40 to 50, which is a 25% increase
The two increases are equal
From 40 to 50, because 10 is more than 6
From 20 to 26, which is a 30% increase
questions.answer: From 20 to 26, which is a 30% increase
questions.solution: From 40 to 50 the increase is 10, and $10 \div 40 = 0.25$, a 25% increase. From 20 to 26 the increase is 6, and $6 \div 20 = 0.30$, a 30% increase. The second is greater, even though its increase is smaller in size.

solve.answer: From 20 to 26, which is a 30% increase
solve.work: 40 to 50: 10/40 = 25%. 20 to 26: 6/20 = 30%. The second is greater.

questions.skill: Percent increase and decrease
questions.stem: A recipe changes the sugar from $\frac{2}{5}$ cup to $\frac{3}{5}$ cup. What is the percent increase?
questions.solution: The increase is $\frac{3}{5} - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{5}$ cup. As a fraction of the original $\frac{2}{5}$ cup it is $\frac{1}{5} \div \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{2}$, which is 50%.

questions.skill: Read a circle graph sector in degrees and percent
questions.stem: A sector of a circle graph measures 90 degrees. What percent of the whole circle graph is this sector?
questions.solution: A whole circle is 360 degrees. $90 \div 360 = \frac{1}{4}$, which is 25%.

questions.skill: Know that circumference divided by diameter is pi
questions.stem: For any circle, the circumference divided by the diameter is closest to which number?
questions.solution: The ratio of circumference to diameter is the same for every circle. It is called $\pi$, about 3.14.

questions.skill: Find circumference from diameter
questions.stem: A circle has a diameter of 10 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is its circumference, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Circumference $= \pi \times d = 3.14 \times 10 = 31.4$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Convert a percent or fraction to degrees in a circle graph
questions.stem: The sector for pizza in a class-vote circle graph is 25% of the circle. How many degrees does that sector measure?
questions.solution: A full circle is 360 degrees. 25% of 360 is $0.25 \times 360 = 90$ degrees.

questions.skill: Convert a percent or fraction to degrees in a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph shows how a family spends its weekend. The sports sector is 10% of the circle. What is the angle of the sports sector, in degrees?
questions.solution: The whole circle is 360 degrees, so 10% of it is $0.1 \times 360 = 36$ degrees. (10 uses the percent as degrees, 3.6 slips the decimal point, and 360 is the whole circle.)

questions.skill: Convert a percent or fraction to degrees in a circle graph
questions.stem: In a circle graph, 75% of the votes went to one choice. What angle, in degrees, should that sector have?
questions.solution: 75% of 360 degrees is $0.75 \times 360 = 270$ degrees. (Another way: $\frac{3}{4}$ of 360 is 270.)

questions.skill: Convert degrees to a percent or fraction of a circle graph
questions.stem: A sector in a circle graph measures 120 degrees. What fraction of the whole circle is that sector?
questions.solution: The whole circle is 360 degrees. $\frac{120}{360} = \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.skill: Convert degrees to a percent or fraction of a circle graph
questions.stem: A sector in a circle graph measures 36 degrees. What percent of the circle is that sector?

questions.skill: Convert degrees to a percent or fraction of a circle graph
questions.stem: An angle of 72 degrees in a circle graph stands for what percent of the whole circle?

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find a count
questions.stem: A circle graph shows the favorite fruits of 80 children. The apple sector is 25% of the circle. How many children chose apples?
questions.solution: 25% of 80 is $\frac{1}{4} \times 80 = 20$ children.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find a count
questions.stem: A circle graph shows 40 votes. The sector for "yes" measures 180 degrees. How many of the votes were "yes"?
questions.solution: 180 degrees is half of the 360-degree circle, so "yes" is half of the 40 votes: 20 votes.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find a count
questions.stem: A circle graph shows how 300 people travelled. The sector for train is 10% of the circle. How many people took the train?
questions.solution: 10% of 300 is $0.1 \times 300 = 30$ people.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find the whole
questions.stem: In a circle graph, the cat sector is 50% of the circle and stands for 12 pets. How many pets does the whole circle graph stand for?
questions.solution: 12 pets is half of the whole, so the whole is $12 \times 2 = 24$ pets.

solve.work: 50% stands for 12, so the whole is 12 x 2 = 24 pets.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find the whole
questions.stem: A sector that is 25% of a circle graph stands for 15 students. How many students are in the graph altogether?
questions.solution: 25% is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the whole, so the whole is $15 \times 4 = 60$ students.

questions.skill: Find a missing sector of a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph has three sectors. Two of them are 40% and 35% of the circle. What percent of the circle is the third sector?
questions.solution: All the sectors make 100%. $40 + 35 = 75$, so the third sector is $100 - 75 = 25\%$.

questions.skill: Find a missing sector of a circle graph
questions.stem: Three sectors of a circle graph have angles of 100 degrees, 120 degrees and an unknown number of degrees. What is the unknown angle, in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles make 360 degrees. $100 + 120 = 220$, so the missing angle is $360 - 220 = 140$ degrees.

questions.skill: Find a missing sector of a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph has four sectors. Three of them are 30%, 20% and 10% of the circle. What percent of the circle is the fourth sector?
questions.solution: The sectors make 100%. $30 + 20 + 10 = 60$, so the fourth sector is $100 - 60 = 40\%$.

questions.skill: Compare sectors of a circle graph
questions.stem: Sector A of a circle graph measures 60 degrees and sector B measures 120 degrees. Which statement is true?
choices: Sector A stands for twice as much as sector B.
Sectors A and B stand for the same amount.
Sector B stands for 1.5 times as much as sector A.
Sector B stands for twice as much as sector A.
questions.answer: Sector B stands for twice as much as sector A.
questions.solution: $120 \div 60 = 2$, so sector B is twice as large as sector A and stands for twice as much.

solve.answer: Sector B stands for twice as much as sector A.
solve.work: 120/60 = 2, and in one circle graph the amount is proportional to the angle, so B stands for twice as much as A.

questions.skill: Know that circumference divided by diameter is pi
questions.stem: Which number is the best approximation of $\pi$?
questions.solution: $\pi$ is about 3.14. (6.28 is $2\pi$, and 1.57 is $\frac{\pi}{2}$.)

solve.work: pi = 3.14159..., so 3.14 is the best approximation; 6.28 is 2pi, 1.57 is pi/2, 0.314 is pi/10.

questions.skill: Know that circumference divided by diameter is pi
questions.stem: A circle has a circumference of 31.4 centimeters and a diameter of 10 centimeters. What is the circumference divided by the diameter?
questions.solution: $31.4 \div 10 = 3.14$. For every circle, circumference divided by diameter is $\pi$, about 3.14.

questions.skill: Know that circumference divided by diameter is pi
questions.stem: Which statement about $\pi$ is true?
choices: $\pi$ is the circumference of a circle divided by its diameter.
$\pi$ is the diameter of a circle divided by its circumference.
$\pi$ is the circumference of a circle divided by its radius.
$\pi$ is the diameter of a circle divided by its radius.
questions.answer: $\pi$ is the circumference of a circle divided by its diameter.
questions.solution: For every circle, circumference $\div$ diameter $= \pi$. Dividing the circumference by the radius gives $2\pi$, and dividing the diameter by the radius gives 2.

solve.answer: $\pi$ is the circumference of a circle divided by its diameter.
solve.work: By definition pi = C/d, circumference divided by diameter.

questions.skill: Relate radius and diameter
questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 9 centimeters. What is its diameter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diameter is twice the radius: $2 \times 9 = 18$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Relate radius and diameter
questions.stem: A round pond has a diameter of 14 feet. What is the radius of the pond, in feet?
questions.solution: The radius is half the diameter: $14 \div 2 = 7$ feet.

questions.skill: Relate radius and diameter
questions.stem: Which statement about any circle is true?
choices: The radius is twice the diameter.
The radius and the diameter are equal.
The diameter is twice the radius.
The diameter is half the radius.
questions.answer: The diameter is twice the radius.
questions.solution: The diameter goes all the way across the circle through the center and the radius goes only halfway, so the diameter is twice the radius.

solve.answer: The diameter is twice the radius.
solve.work: d = 2r for every circle, so the diameter is twice the radius.

questions.skill: Find circumference from diameter
questions.stem: A circular coaster has a diameter of 8 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the distance around the coaster, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Circumference $= \pi \times$ diameter $= 3.14 \times 8 = 25.12$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Find circumference from diameter
questions.stem: A pie pan has a diameter of 20 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the circumference of the pan, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $3.14 \times 20 = 62.8$ centimeters. (31.4 uses half the diameter, 23.14 adds instead of multiplying, and 628 slips the decimal.)

questions.skill: Find circumference from diameter
questions.stem: A circle has a diameter of 7 inches. Use $\frac{22}{7}$ for $\pi$. What is the circumference, in inches?
questions.solution: $\frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 22$ inches.

questions.skill: Find circumference from radius
questions.stem: A round button has a radius of 3 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the distance around the button, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Circumference $= 2 \times \pi \times$ radius $= 2 \times 3.14 \times 3 = 18.84$ centimeters. (9.42 forgets the 2, and 28.26 is $3.14 \times 3 \times 3$.)

questions.skill: Find circumference from radius
questions.stem: A circular playground has a radius of 10 meters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is its circumference, in meters?
questions.solution: $2 \times 3.14 \times 10 = 62.8$ meters. (31.4 forgets the 2, and 314 is $3.14 \times 10 \times 10$.)

questions.skill: Find diameter or radius from circumference
questions.stem: A round swimming pool has a circumference of 31.4 meters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the diameter of the pool, in meters?
questions.solution: Circumference $= \pi \times$ diameter, so diameter $= 31.4 \div 3.14 = 10$ meters.

questions.skill: Find diameter or radius from circumference
questions.stem: A circle has a circumference of 25.12 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is its diameter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Diameter $= 25.12 \div 3.14 = 8$ centimeters. (4 is the radius, 12.56 is half the circumference, and 21.98 subtracts.)

questions.skill: Solve a problem using circumference
questions.stem: A bicycle wheel has a circumference of 2 meters. How far does the bicycle travel when the wheel makes 10 full turns, in meters?
questions.solution: Each full turn moves the bicycle one circumference, 2 meters. 10 turns is $10 \times 2 = 20$ meters.

solve.work: Each full turn rolls one circumference, 2 m; 10 turns = 20 m.

questions.skill: Solve a problem using circumference
questions.stem: A circular track has a circumference of 400 meters. A runner goes around it 3 times. How many meters does the runner run?
questions.solution: Each lap is 400 meters, so 3 laps is $3 \times 400 = 1200$ meters.

solve.issues: Very easy: with the circumference given it is only 400 x 3, so it uses almost no circle reasoning. Acceptable as an entry-level item, but weak evidence for the standard.

questions.skill: Convert a circle graph percent to degrees
questions.stem: In a circle graph, one sector shows 35% of the data. How many degrees is the angle of that sector?
questions.solution: The whole circle is 360 degrees. 35% of 360 is $0.35 \times 360 = 126$ degrees.

questions.skill: Find circumference from radius
questions.stem: A circular rug has a radius of 4.5 feet. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the distance around the rug, in feet?
questions.solution: The distance around is the circumference: $2 \times \pi \times r = 2 \times 3.14 \times 4.5 = 28.26$ feet.

questions.skill: Find diameter from circumference
questions.stem: The circumference of a circle is 47.1 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the diameter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Since $C = \pi d$, the diameter is $d = C \div \pi = 47.1 \div 3.14 = 15$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Convert a percent or fraction to degrees in a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph shows how 100 students get to school. Walking is 15% of the circle. What is the angle of the walking sector, in degrees?
questions.solution: 15% of 360 degrees is $0.15 \times 360 = 54$ degrees.

solve.work: 15% of 360 = 0.15 x 360 = 54 degrees. (The 100 students is extra information.)

questions.skill: Convert a percent or fraction to degrees in a circle graph
questions.stem: In a circle graph about lunch, 45% of the students chose a sandwich. What angle, in degrees, should the sandwich sector have?
questions.solution: $0.45 \times 360 = 162$ degrees. (45 treats the percent as degrees, 16.2 slips the decimal, and 198 is the angle for the other 55%.)

questions.skill: Convert a percent or fraction to degrees in a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph of a garden shows that 12.5% of the garden holds carrots. How many degrees is the carrot sector?
questions.solution: 12.5% is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the circle, and $360 \div 8 = 45$ degrees. (Check: $0.125 \times 360 = 45$.)

questions.skill: Convert degrees to a percent or fraction of a circle graph
questions.stem: In a circle graph, the tennis sector has an angle of 54 degrees. What percent of the circle is the tennis sector?

questions.skill: Convert degrees to a percent or fraction of a circle graph
questions.stem: A sector of a circle graph has an angle of 108 degrees. What percent of the whole circle is that sector?
questions.solution: $\frac{108}{360} = 0.3 = 30\%$. (70 is the percent of the rest of the circle.)

questions.skill: Convert degrees to a percent or fraction of a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph has a sector of 135 degrees. What fraction of the whole circle is that sector? Write it in simplest form.
questions.solution: $\frac{135}{360}$: both numbers divide by 45, giving $\frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find a count
questions.stem: A circle graph shows the colors of the 180 marbles in a bag. The blue sector measures 120 degrees. How many marbles are blue?
questions.solution: 120 degrees is $\frac{120}{360} = \frac{1}{3}$ of the circle. $\frac{1}{3} \times 180 = 60$ marbles.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find a count
questions.stem: In a circle graph of 250 library books, the sector for mysteries is 28% of the circle. How many of the books are mysteries?
questions.solution: 28% of 250 is $0.28 \times 250 = 70$ books.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find a count
questions.stem: A circle graph shows how 420 students spend a free period. The sector for reading measures 60 degrees. How many students read?
questions.solution: 60 degrees is $\frac{60}{360} = \frac{1}{6}$ of the circle. $\frac{1}{6} \times 420 = 70$ students. (60 is the angle, 7 divides $420$ by $60$, and 2520 multiplies by 6.)

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find the whole
questions.stem: In a circle graph, a sector of 72 degrees stands for 18 votes. How many votes does the whole graph stand for?
questions.solution: 72 degrees is $\frac{72}{360} = \frac{1}{5}$ of the circle, so the whole is $18 \times 5 = 90$ votes.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find the whole
questions.stem: In a circle graph about how students get to school, the sector for walking is 20% of the circle, and 14 students walk. How many students are shown in all?
questions.solution: 20% is $\frac{1}{5}$ of the whole, so the whole is $14 \times 5 = 70$ students.

questions.skill: Use a circle graph sector to find the whole
questions.stem: In a circle graph, 35% of the circle stands for 28 tickets sold online. How many tickets were sold altogether?
questions.solution: $28 \div 0.35 = 80$ tickets. (Check: 35% of 80 is 28.)

questions.skill: Find a missing sector of a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph has four sectors. Three of them measure 85 degrees, 110 degrees and 45 degrees. How many degrees does the fourth sector measure?
questions.solution: $85 + 110 + 45 = 240$ degrees, so the fourth sector is $360 - 240 = 120$ degrees.

questions.skill: Find a missing sector of a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph shows four categories. Three of them are 22%, 31% and 18% of the circle, and the last one is "other". What percent of the circle is "other"?
questions.solution: $22 + 31 + 18 = 71$, so "other" is $100 - 71 = 29\%$. (71 is the three sectors together; 47 and 51 each leave out one of the three.)

questions.skill: Find a missing sector of a circle graph
questions.stem: In a circle graph about pets, dogs take 135 degrees, cats take 90 degrees and fish take 45 degrees. The rest of the circle is birds. What percent of the circle is birds?

questions.skill: Compare sectors of a circle graph
questions.stem: In a circle graph, the tea sector is 15% of the circle and the juice sector measures 108 degrees. How many degrees larger is the juice sector than the tea sector?
questions.solution: The tea sector is $0.15 \times 360 = 54$ degrees. The juice sector is $108 - 54 = 54$ degrees larger.

solve.work: Tea = 15% of 360 = 54 degrees. Juice = 108. Difference = 108 - 54 = 54 degrees.

questions.skill: Compare sectors of a circle graph
questions.stem: A circle graph has four sectors: red is 30% of the circle, blue measures 80 degrees, green is $\frac{1}{5}$ of the circle, and yellow measures 100 degrees. Which color has the largest sector?
choices: Blue
Green
Red
Yellow
questions.answer: Red
questions.solution: Red is $0.3 \times 360 = 108$ degrees, blue is 80, green is $\frac{1}{5} \times 360 = 72$, and yellow is 100. (These make $108 + 80 + 72 + 100 = 360$.) Red is the largest.

solve.answer: Red
solve.work: Red 30% of 360 = 108; blue 80; green 1/5 of 360 = 72; yellow 100. Sum 360 (consistent). Largest is red at 108.

questions.skill: Know that circumference divided by diameter is pi
questions.stem: A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 70 centimeters and a circumference of 219.8 centimeters. What is the circumference divided by the diameter?
questions.solution: $219.8 \div 70 = 3.14$, the value of $\pi$ rounded to two decimal places.
