questions.stem: A shoe box measures 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 12 cm high. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume = 30 $\times$ 20 $\times$ 12 = 600 $\times$ 12 = 7200 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume as layers of the base
questions.stem: A box is filled with 5 identical layers of cubes. Each layer has 24 cubes. How many cubes are in the box?
questions.solution: Each layer has 24 cubes and there are 5 layers: 24 $\times$ 5 = 120 cubes.

questions.skill: Volume as layers of the base
questions.stem: A stack of 20 identical square tiles is 20 centimeters tall, because each tile is 1 centimeter thick. The top of each tile has an area of 36 square centimeters. What is the volume of the stack, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Each tile is a layer with a volume of 36 cubic centimeters (area 36 times thickness 1). With 20 layers the volume is 20 $\times$ 36 = 720 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume as layers of the base
questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the volume of a right prism?
choices: The area of the base times the height
The perimeter of the base times the height
The area of the base plus the height
The sum of the areas of all the faces
questions.answer: The area of the base times the height

questions.skill: How changing dimensions changes volume

questions.solution: Area of a triangular end = $\frac{1}{2} \times 4.5 \times 4 = 9$ square centimeters. Volume = 9 $\times$ 30 = 270 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A cylinder has a diameter of 10 centimeters and a height of 9 centimeters. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters, in terms of $\pi$?
questions.solution: The radius is 5 cm. Volume = $\pi \times 5^2 \times 9 = \pi \times 25 \times 9 = 225\pi$ cubic centimeters.

solve.work: r = 5. V = pi x 25 x 9 = 225 pi.

questions.skill: Volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A full cylindrical can has a radius of 10 cm and a height of 20 cm. All of the water in it is poured into an empty rectangular tank whose base is 20 cm by 10 cm. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. How deep is the water in the tank, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume of water = $3.14 \times 10^2 \times 20 = 6280$ cubic cm. Base of the tank = 20 $\times$ 10 = 200 square cm. Depth = 6280 $\div$ 200 = 31.4 cm.

questions.skill: Volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A metal pipe is a hollow cylinder 10 cm long. Its outer radius is 5 cm, and the hole through it has a radius of 4 cm. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the volume of the metal in the pipe, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Outer cylinder: $3.14 \times 5^2 \times 10 = 785$. Hole: $3.14 \times 4^2 \times 10 = 502.4$. Metal = 785 $-$ 502.4 = 282.6 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: A shed is a rectangular box that is 4 meters long, 3 meters wide and 2.5 meters tall. The four walls and the flat roof are painted, but not the floor. What is the area painted, in square meters?
questions.solution: Long walls: 2 $\times$ 4 $\times$ 2.5 = 20. Short walls: 2 $\times$ 3 $\times$ 2.5 = 15. Roof: 4 $\times$ 3 = 12. Total = 47 square meters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: Which box has the greatest surface area?
choices: 12 cm by 2 cm by 1 cm
4 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm
5 cm by 3 cm by 3 cm
7 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm
questions.answer: 7 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm
questions.solution: $7 \times 3 \times 2$: $2(21 + 14 + 6) = 82$. $12 \times 2 \times 1$: $2(24 + 12 + 2) = 76$. $4 \times 4 \times 3$: $2(16 + 12 + 12) = 80$. $5 \times 3 \times 3$: $2(15 + 15 + 9) = 78$. The greatest is 82 square centimeters.

solve.answer: 7 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm

questions.skill: Surface area as the sum of the faces (nets and triangular prisms)
questions.stem: The ends of a prism are triangles with sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. The height of each triangle, measured to the 6 cm side, is 4 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its total surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangular end: $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$, so two ends are 24. The three rectangles together: (5 + 5 + 6) $\times$ 10 = 160. Total = 24 + 160 = 184 square centimeters.

solve.work: Ends 2 x (1/2 x 6 x 4) = 24. Sides 16 x 10 = 160. Total 184.

questions.skill: Surface area as the sum of the faces (nets and triangular prisms)
questions.stem: A triangular prism has right-triangle ends with sides of 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm, and it is 20 cm long. It sits on a table on its 15 cm by 20 cm rectangular face, and every other face is painted. What is the painted area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Two ends: 2 $\times$ $\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 12$ = 108. Rectangles: (9 + 12 + 15) $\times$ 20 = 720. Total surface = 828. The face on the table, 15 $\times$ 20 = 300, is not painted: 828 $-$ 300 = 528 square centimeters.

solve.work: Ends 2 x (1/2 x 9 x 12) = 108. Rectangles 9 x 20 = 180 and 12 x 20 = 240 (15 x 20 face unpainted). 108 + 180 + 240 = 528.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cylinder
questions.stem: A closed cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its total surface area, in square centimeters, in terms of $\pi$?
questions.solution: Two circular ends: $2 \times \pi \times 4^2 = 32\pi$. Curved side: $2 \times \pi \times 4 \times 10 = 80\pi$. Total = $112\pi$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Ends 2 x 16 pi = 32 pi. Side 2 pi x 4 x 10 = 80 pi. Total 112 pi.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cylinder
questions.stem: A closed cylindrical tank has a radius of 2 meters and a height of 5 meters. Its whole outside is painted with paint that costs 3 dollars per square meter. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. How many dollars does the paint cost?
questions.solution: Ends: 2 $\times$ 3.14 $\times$ $2^2$ = 25.12. Curved side: 2 $\times$ 3.14 $\times$ 2 $\times$ 5 = 62.8. Surface area = 87.92 square meters. Cost = 87.92 $\times$ 3 = 263.76 dollars.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cylinder
questions.stem: The curved side of a cylinder has an area of 188.4 square centimeters, and the cylinder is 10 centimeters tall. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the radius of the cylinder, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Curved side = 2 $\times$ 3.14 $\times$ radius $\times$ height, so the radius is 188.4 $\div$ (2 $\times$ 3.14 $\times$ 10) = 188.4 $\div$ 62.8 = 3 centimeters.

solve.work: Circumference = 188.4 / 10 = 18.84 = 2 x 3.14 x r, so r = 3.

questions.skill: Unknown dimension from volume or surface area
questions.stem: A closed rectangular box has a base that is 5 cm by 4 cm. Its total surface area is 94 square centimeters. How tall is the box, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Top and bottom: 2 $\times$ 5 $\times$ 4 = 40. The four sides must have area 94 $-$ 40 = 54. The four sides have a total width of 2 $\times$ (5 + 4) = 18, so the height is 54 $\div$ 18 = 3 centimeters.

questions.skill: Unknown dimension from volume or surface area
questions.stem: A rectangular tank has a base that is 50 cm by 30 cm. It holds 45 liters of water. One liter is 1000 cubic centimeters. How deep is the water, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume of water = 45 $\times$ 1000 = 45000 cubic centimeters. Base area = 50 $\times$ 30 = 1500. Depth = 45000 $\div$ 1500 = 30 centimeters.

questions.skill: Unknown dimension from volume or surface area
questions.stem: Which solid has a volume of 150 cubic centimeters?
choices: A rectangular prism that is 6 cm by 5 cm by 10 cm
A triangular prism whose ends have a base of 6 cm and a height of 5 cm, and which is 10 cm long
A cylinder with a radius of 5 cm and a height of 2 cm, using 3.14 for $\pi$
A cube with edges of 5 cm
questions.answer: A triangular prism whose ends have a base of 6 cm and a height of 5 cm, and which is 10 cm long
questions.solution: Triangular prism: $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 5 \times 10 = 150$. The rectangular prism is $6 \times 5 \times 10 = 300$, the cylinder is $3.14 \times 25 \times 2 = 157$, and the cube is $5^3 = 125$.

solve.answer: A triangular prism whose ends have a base of 6 cm and a height of 5 cm, and which is 10 cm long
solve.work: Rect 300; cube 125; cylinder 3.14 x 25 x 2 = 157; triangular prism 1/2 x 6 x 5 x 10 = 150.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A cake has three round layers (cylinders) stacked on each other. Each layer is 5 cm tall. The radii of the layers are 6 cm, 4 cm and 2 cm. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the total volume of the cake, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Layer volumes: $3.14 \times 6^2 \times 5 = 565.2$, $3.14 \times 4^2 \times 5 = 251.2$ and $3.14 \times 2^2 \times 5 = 62.8$. Total = 879.2 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A building is a rectangular prism 12 m long, 8 m wide and 6 m tall. Its roof is a triangular prism 12 m long, with triangular ends that have a base of 8 m and a height of 3 m. A chimney shaped like a 2 m by 2 m by 3 m box stands on the roof. What is the volume of the building, roof and chimney together, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Rectangular part: 12 $\times$ 8 $\times$ 6 = 576. Roof: $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 3 \times 12 = 144$. Chimney: 2 $\times$ 2 $\times$ 3 = 12. Total = 576 + 144 + 12 = 732 cubic meters.

solve.issues: Minor: a box cannot stand flat on a sloped roof without part of it overlapping the roof; the intended reading (just add 12) is clear at this grade.
solve.work: Building 12 x 8 x 6 = 576. Roof 1/2 x 8 x 3 x 12 = 144. Chimney 2 x 2 x 3 = 12. Total 732.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A tower is made of two prisms stacked on each other. Both have a base that is 5 cm by 4 cm. The lower prism is 3 cm tall. The whole tower has a volume of 100 cubic centimeters. How tall is the upper prism, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Base area = 5 $\times$ 4 = 20 square centimeters. The whole tower is 100 $\div$ 20 = 5 cm tall. The upper prism is 5 $-$ 3 = 2 centimeters tall.

questions.skill: Surface area of a composite solid
questions.stem: A cube with edges of 2 cm sits in the middle of the top face of a cube with edges of 4 cm. What is the surface area of the combined solid, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The top of the small cube covers 2 $\times$ 2 = 4 square cm of the big cube, but it shows the same amount on its own top. So the flat surfaces total 6 $\times$ $4^2$ = 96, and the four sides of the small cube add 4 $\times$ 4 = 16. Total = 112 square centimeters.

solve.work: Big cube 96 (hidden 4 on top replaced by small cube's top). Add small cube's 4 sides 4 x 4 = 16. Total 112.

questions.skill: Surface area of a composite solid
questions.stem: The base of a prism is an L-shape with six sides of 6 cm, 2 cm, 4 cm, 3 cm, 2 cm and 5 cm (in order around the L). The area of the L is 18 square centimeters. The prism is 4 cm tall. What is its total surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Top and bottom: 2 $\times$ 18 = 36. The distance around the L is 6 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 5 = 22 cm, so the sides total 22 $\times$ 4 = 88. Total = 36 + 88 = 124 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a composite solid
questions.stem: A cube with edges of 6 cm has a square hole 2 cm by 2 cm drilled straight through the middle, from one face to the opposite face. What is the surface area of the solid that is left, including the inside of the hole, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The cube has 6 $\times$ $6^2$ = 216. Two faces lose a 2 by 2 square: $-$ 2 $\times$ 4 = $-$ 8. The inside of the hole has 4 walls, each 2 by 6: 4 $\times$ 12 = 48. Total = 256 square centimeters.

solve.work: 216 - 2 x 4 = 208 outside. Hole walls 4 x (2 x 6) = 48. Total 256.

questions.skill: Surface area of a composite solid
questions.stem: Two cylinders are stacked with the same center line. The bottom cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 3 cm. The top cylinder has a radius of 2 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is the surface area of the combined solid, in square centimeters, in terms of $\pi$?
questions.solution: The bottom cylinder alone has $2\pi(4^2) + 2\pi(4)(3) = 32\pi + 24\pi = 56\pi$. The top cylinder covers a circle of the bottom cylinder but shows an equal circle on its own top, so only its curved side is new: $2\pi(2)(5) = 20\pi$. Total = $56\pi + 20\pi = 76\pi$.

solve.work: Flat parts: bottom 16 pi + exposed ring 12 pi + small top 4 pi = 32 pi. Sides: 2 pi x 4 x 3 = 24 pi and 2 pi x 2 x 5 = 20 pi. Total 76 pi.

questions.skill: How changing dimensions changes volume
questions.stem: The height of a cylinder is doubled and its radius is cut in half. What happens to the volume?
choices: It stays the same
It becomes twice as large
It becomes half as large
It becomes one fourth as large
questions.answer: It becomes half as large
questions.solution: Volume = $\pi r^2 h$. Halving $r$ multiplies the volume by $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$, and doubling $h$ multiplies it by 2. Together: $\frac{1}{4} \times 2 = \frac{1}{2}$, so the volume is half as large.

solve.answer: It becomes half as large

questions.skill: How changing dimensions changes volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of 40 cubic centimeters. Its length is doubled, its width is tripled and its height is cut in half. What is the volume of the new prism, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The volume is multiplied by 2 $\times$ 3 $\times$ $\frac{1}{2}$ = 3. New volume = 40 $\times$ 3 = 120 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: How changing dimensions changes volume
questions.stem: A cube has edges of 3 cm. Every edge is made twice as long. By how many square centimeters does the surface area of the cube increase?
questions.solution: Old surface area: 6 $\times$ $3^2$ = 54. New edge: 6 cm, so the new surface area is 6 $\times$ $6^2$ = 216. Increase = 216 $-$ 54 = 162 square centimeters.

solve.work: Old 6 x 9 = 54. New edge 6: 6 x 36 = 216. Increase 162.

questions.skill: Complementary angles
questions.stem: Two angles are complementary. One of them measures $35^\circ$. What is the measure of the other angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add to $90^\circ$. The other angle is $90 - 35 = 55$ degrees.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles
questions.stem: Two angles are supplementary. One of them measures $112^\circ$. What is the measure of the other angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add to $180^\circ$, so the other angle is $180 - 112 = 68$ degrees. (22 subtracts from 90, 248 subtracts from 360, and 112 assumes the angles are equal.)

questions.skill: Vertical angles
questions.stem: Two straight lines cross and form four angles. One of the angles measures $65^\circ$. What is the measure of the angle directly across from it (its vertical angle) in degrees?
questions.solution: Vertical angles, the ones directly across from each other where two lines cross, are equal. The angle is also $65^\circ$.

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Angle $P$ and angle $Q$ are complementary, which means that together they make a right angle. Angle $P$ measures $28^\circ$. How many degrees is angle $Q$?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add up to $90^\circ$. So angle $Q$ is $90 - 28 = 62$ degrees.

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: What is the measure, in degrees, of the complement of an angle that measures $71^\circ$?
questions.solution: The complement is the angle that adds with $71^\circ$ to make $90^\circ$: $90 - 71 = 19$. The choice 109 is the supplement ($180 - 71$), 161 adds $90 + 71$, and 45 assumes the two angles are equal.

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: A wooden shelf bracket is fixed in a square corner of a wall (a right angle). It splits the corner into two angles. One of the angles is $40^\circ$. What is the other angle, in degrees?
questions.solution: A square corner is $90^\circ$, so the two parts add up to $90^\circ$. The other angle is $90 - 40 = 50$ degrees.

solve.work: The two angles fill a right angle: 90 - 40 = 50.

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Which statement about complementary angles is true?
choices: Their measures add up to $180^\circ$.
Their measures are always equal.
Their measures add up to $90^\circ$.
Their measures add up to $360^\circ$.
questions.answer: Their measures add up to $90^\circ$.
questions.solution: Complementary angles are two angles whose measures add up to $90^\circ$, a right angle. Angles that add up to $180^\circ$ are supplementary. Complementary angles need not be equal (for example $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$).

solve.answer: Their measures add up to $90^\circ$.
solve.work: Complementary angles sum to 90 degrees by definition. 180 is supplementary; 360 is a full turn; they need not be equal.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Angle $M$ and angle $N$ are supplementary, which means that together they make a straight angle. Angle $M$ measures $125^\circ$. How many degrees is angle $N$?
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$. So angle $N$ is $180 - 125 = 55$ degrees.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: What is the measure, in degrees, of the supplement of a $73^\circ$ angle?
questions.solution: The supplement is the angle that adds with $73^\circ$ to make $180^\circ$: $180 - 73 = 107$. The choice 17 is $90 - 73$ (the complement), 253 is $180 + 73$, and 287 is $360 - 73$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: A straight road meets a side street. The side street makes a $65^\circ$ angle with one side of the road. What angle does it make with the other side of the road, in degrees?
questions.solution: The two angles are next to each other along the straight road, so they add up to $180^\circ$. The other angle is $180 - 65 = 115$ degrees.

solve.work: The two angles on either side of the street lie on the straight road, so they are supplementary: 180 - 65 = 115.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Two supplementary angles sit next to each other and share a side. What do they make together?
choices: a right angle
a straight angle
a full turn
an acute angle
questions.answer: a straight angle
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$. Two of them side by side make a straight angle, which looks like a straight line.

solve.answer: a straight angle
solve.work: Adjacent supplementary angles (a linear pair) sum to 180 and their outer sides form a straight line: a straight angle.

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: Angle 1 and angle 3 are vertical angles. Angle 1 measures $48^\circ$. How many degrees is angle 3?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are across from each other where two lines cross, and they have equal measures. Angle 3 is $48^\circ$.

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: Two lines cross. Which statement is always true about a pair of vertical angles?
choices: They have equal measures to each other.
Their measures add up to $180^\circ$.
Their measures add up to $90^\circ$.
One is twice as large as the other.
questions.answer: They have equal measures to each other.
questions.solution: Vertical angles are the angles directly across from each other at a crossing. They always have equal measures.

solve.answer: They have equal measures to each other.
solve.work: Vertical angles are always equal. Summing to 180 is true of adjacent angles; 90 only when perpendicular-related; not double.

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: Two straight sticks cross to make an X. One angle at the crossing is $110^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle directly opposite it?
questions.solution: The angle directly opposite is its vertical angle. Vertical angles are equal, so it is $110^\circ$ too.

solve.work: The opposite angle is the vertical angle, equal: 110.

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: Two lines cross, and the four angles around the crossing are numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4 in order. Which pair of angles are vertical angles?
choices: angle 1 and angle 2
angle 2 and angle 3
angle 1 and angle 3
angle 3 and angle 4
questions.answer: angle 1 and angle 3
questions.solution: Vertical angles are across from each other, not next to each other. Going around in order, angle 1 is across from angle 3 (and angle 2 is across from angle 4). The other pairs are next to each other.

solve.answer: angle 1 and angle 3
solve.work: Numbered in order around the crossing, angles 1 and 3 are opposite (as are 2 and 4); consecutive pairs are adjacent. Only 1 and 3 is offered.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: Two angles sit side by side along a straight line. One measures $145^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the other?
questions.solution: Angles along a straight line add up to $180^\circ$: $180 - 145 = 35$. The choice 55 is $145 - 90$, 215 is $360 - 145$, and 145 repeats the given angle.

solve.work: Angles side by side on a straight line sum to 180: 180 - 145 = 35.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: A ray splits a straight angle into two angles. One of them is a right angle. What is the measure of the other angle in degrees?
questions.solution: A straight angle is $180^\circ$ and a right angle is $90^\circ$, so the other angle is $180 - 90 = 90$ degrees.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: Angle $ABC$ is a straight angle. Ray $BD$ splits it into angle $ABD$ and angle $DBC$. Angle $ABD$ measures $41^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $DBC$ in degrees?
questions.solution: A straight angle is $180^\circ$, so angle $DBC$ is $180 - 41 = 139$ degrees. The choice 49 is $90 - 41$, 319 is $360 - 41$, and 41 repeats the given angle.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles that make up a larger angle
questions.stem: Angle $AOB$ measures $30^\circ$ and the angle next to it, angle $BOC$, measures $45^\circ$. They share ray $OB$ and do not overlap. What is the measure of angle $AOC$ in degrees?
questions.solution: The two adjacent angles together make angle $AOC$, so $30 + 45 = 75$ degrees.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles that make up a larger angle
questions.stem: Angle $XYZ$ measures $120^\circ$. Ray $YW$ lies inside it and splits it into angle $XYW$ and angle $WYZ$. Angle $XYW$ measures $75^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $WYZ$ in degrees?
questions.solution: The two parts add up to the whole angle: $75 + WYZ = 120$, so angle $WYZ$ is $120 - 75 = 45$ degrees. The choice 195 adds, 105 is $180 - 75$, and 15 is $90 - 75$.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Two angles measure $50^\circ$ and $130^\circ$. Which word describes this pair of angles?
choices: supplementary
complementary
vertical
equal
questions.answer: supplementary
questions.solution: $50 + 130 = 180$, so the angles are supplementary. They are not complementary (which would add to 90), and they are not vertical or equal because $50$ is not $130$.

solve.answer: supplementary
solve.work: 50 + 130 = 180: supplementary. Not equal, not 90, and vertical angles would be equal.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Which pair of angles always have equal measures?
choices: supplementary angles
complementary angles
vertical angles
adjacent angles
questions.answer: vertical angles
questions.solution: Vertical angles, the angles across from each other where two lines cross, always have equal measures. Supplementary angles, complementary angles and adjacent angles are equal only in special cases.

solve.answer: vertical angles
solve.work: Vertical angles are always equal; the others are equal only in special cases.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Two angles share a vertex and one side, and they do not overlap. What are these angles called?
choices: vertical angles
adjacent angles
complementary angles
supplementary angles
questions.answer: adjacent angles
questions.solution: Angles that share a vertex and a side and do not overlap are adjacent angles. Whether they are also complementary or supplementary depends on their measures, not on how they are placed.

solve.answer: adjacent angles
solve.work: Common vertex, common side, no overlap is the definition of adjacent angles.

questions.skill: Complementary angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two angles are complementary. One measures $(x + 20)^\circ$ and the other measures $50^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add up to 90: $(x + 20) + 50 = 90$. So $x + 70 = 90$ and $x = 20$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and straight lines with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two angles sit side by side along a straight line. They measure $(x + 30)^\circ$ and $100^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Angles along a straight line add up to 180: $(x + 30) + 100 = 180$. So $x + 130 = 180$ and $x = 50$.

questions.skill: Vertical angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two vertical angles measure $(x + 12)^\circ$ and $40^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so $x + 12 = 40$ and $x = 28$.

questions.skill: Vertical angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two vertical angles measure $(3x)^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so $3x = 75$ and $x = 75 \div 3 = 25$. The choice 35 treats the angles as supplementary ($3x + 75 = 180$ would give 35), 225 multiplies instead of dividing, and 72 subtracts 3.

questions.skill: Choose the equation for an unknown angle
questions.stem: Two angles are complementary. One measures $x^\circ$ and the other measures $32^\circ$. Which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add up to 90, so $x + 32 = 90$. The equation with 180 is for supplementary angles, and $x = 32$ would be for vertical angles.

questions.skill: Choose the equation for an unknown angle
questions.stem: Angles $A$ and $B$ lie side by side along a straight line. Angle $A$ measures $x^\circ$ and angle $B$ measures $110^\circ$. Which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: Angles along a straight line add up to 180, so $x + 110 = 180$. The others use 90 (complementary), equal angles (vertical), or 360 (a full turn).

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One of the four angles measures $50^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of an angle that is next to it?
questions.solution: An angle next to it makes a straight line with it, so the two add up to $180^\circ$: $180 - 50 = 130$ degrees.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross and make four angles. One of the angles measures $90^\circ$. What are the measures of the other three angles?
choices: $90^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $90^\circ$
$45^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $90^\circ$
$90^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$
$30^\circ$, $30^\circ$ and $30^\circ$
questions.answer: $90^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $90^\circ$
questions.solution: The angle across from it is also $90^\circ$. The angles next to it are $180 - 90 = 90$ degrees. So all four angles are right angles (the lines are perpendicular).

solve.answer: $90^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $90^\circ$

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle measures $135^\circ$. What is the measure of the smallest of the four angles in degrees?
questions.solution: The angle across from it is $135^\circ$. The two angles next to it are $180 - 135 = 45$ degrees each. The smallest angle is 45.

questions.skill: Angles around a point
questions.stem: Four angles meet at a point and fill the whole way around it, with no gaps and no overlaps. Three of them measure $90^\circ$, $120^\circ$ and $70^\circ$. What is the measure of the fourth angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Angles that fill the whole way around a point add up to $360^\circ$. The three known angles add up to $90 + 120 + 70 = 280$. The fourth is $360 - 280 = 80$ degrees.

questions.skill: Equation for complementary angles
questions.stem: Two complementary angles measure $3x^\circ$ and $(2x + 10)^\circ$. What is the measure of the larger angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add to 90, so $3x + 2x + 10 = 90$. Then $5x = 80$ and $x = 16$. The angles are $3 \times 16 = 48$ and $2 \times 16 + 10 = 42$. The larger angle is 48 degrees.

questions.skill: Equation for vertical angles
questions.stem: Two lines cross. A pair of vertical angles measure $(4x + 5)^\circ$ and $(6x - 15)^\circ$. What is the measure of each of these two angles in degrees?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so $4x + 5 = 6x - 15$. Then $20 = 2x$ and $x = 10$. Each angle measures $4 \times 10 + 5 = 45$ degrees. Check: $6 \times 10 - 15 = 45$.

questions.skill: Angles that form a straight line
questions.stem: Three adjacent angles together form a straight line. Two of them measure $50^\circ$ and $75^\circ$, and the third measures $x^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Angles that form a straight line add to $180^\circ$. So $50 + 75 + x = 180$, and $x = 180 - 125 = 55$. (125 is the sum of the two known angles, 235 subtracts that from 360, and 15 subtracts from 90.)

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Angle $R$ has a complement that measures $38^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $R$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Angle $R$ and $38^\circ$ add up to $90^\circ$, so angle $R$ is $90 - 38 = 52$ degrees. The choice 142 is $180 - 38$, 38 repeats the given angle, and 128 is $90 + 38$.

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Which pair of angle measures is complementary?
choices: $47^\circ$ and $43^\circ$
$47^\circ$ and $133^\circ$
$57^\circ$ and $43^\circ$
$47^\circ$ and $47^\circ$
questions.answer: $47^\circ$ and $43^\circ$
questions.solution: Complementary angles add up to $90^\circ$. $47 + 43 = 90$. The pair $47^\circ$ and $133^\circ$ adds to 180 (supplementary), $57^\circ$ and $43^\circ$ adds to 100, and $47^\circ$ and $47^\circ$ adds to 94.

solve.answer: $47^\circ$ and $43^\circ$

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Two angles are supplementary. One of them measures $87^\circ$. How many degrees larger is the larger angle than the smaller angle?
questions.solution: The other angle is $180 - 87 = 93$ degrees. The larger angle is $93$ and the smaller is $87$, so the difference is $93 - 87 = 6$. The choice 93 is just the other angle, 3 is half the difference, and 87 is the given angle.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Which of these pairs of angle measures could be a pair of supplementary angles?
choices: $64^\circ$ and $26^\circ$
$64^\circ$ and $126^\circ$
$64^\circ$ and $116^\circ$
$74^\circ$ and $116^\circ$
questions.answer: $64^\circ$ and $116^\circ$
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$. $64 + 116 = 180$. The pair $64^\circ$ and $26^\circ$ adds to 90, and the other two pairs add to 190.

solve.answer: $64^\circ$ and $116^\circ$

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: A pair of scissors is opened. The two handles make an angle of $34^\circ$ at the pivot. The two blades make the vertical angle on the other side of the pivot. How many degrees is the angle between the blades?
questions.solution: The handles and the blades are parts of the same two crossing lines, so the angle between the blades is vertical to the angle between the handles. Vertical angles are equal: $34^\circ$.

solve.work: Blades' angle is vertical to the handles' angle, so equal: 34.

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: Two lines cross, and one of the angles measures $100^\circ$. Which statement is true?
choices: The angle across from it measures $80^\circ$.
The angle across from it measures $100^\circ$.
The angles next to it measure $100^\circ$.
All four angles measure $100^\circ$.
questions.answer: The angle across from it measures $100^\circ$.
questions.solution: The angle across from it is its vertical angle, so it is also $100^\circ$. The angles next to it are supplementary to it: $180 - 100 = 80$ degrees. The four angles cannot all be $100^\circ$ because they add up to $360^\circ$.

solve.answer: The angle across from it measures $100^\circ$.
solve.work: Opposite angle is equal: 100. Adjacent angles are 80, so 'next to it 100' and 'all four 100' are false; across is not 80.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: Mia draws three rays from one point on a straight line. They make four angles along the line. Three of the angles measure $28^\circ$, $47^\circ$ and $59^\circ$. What is the measure of the fourth angle in degrees?
questions.solution: All four angles along the line add up to $180^\circ$. The three known angles add up to $28 + 47 + 59 = 134$. The fourth angle is $180 - 134 = 46$ degrees.

solve.work: Four angles along the line sum to 180: 180 - (28 + 47 + 59) = 180 - 134 = 46.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: Two rays are drawn from a point on a straight line, making three angles along the line. The first angle is $25^\circ$. The second angle is $15^\circ$ more than the first angle. What is the measure of the third angle in degrees?
questions.solution: The second angle is $25 + 15 = 40$ degrees. The three angles add up to $180^\circ$, so the third angle is $180 - 25 - 40 = 115$ degrees.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: Angles 1, 2 and 3 lie side by side along a straight line. Angle 1 is $52^\circ$ and angle 3 is $71^\circ$. What is the measure of angle 2 in degrees?
questions.solution: The three angles add up to $180^\circ$. So angle 2 is $180 - 52 - 71 = 57$ degrees. The choice 128 only subtracts 52, 109 only subtracts 71, and 123 adds the two known angles.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles that make up a larger angle
questions.stem: Ray $QR$ lies inside angle $PQS$. Angle $PQR$ measures $38^\circ$ and angle $RQS$ measures $27^\circ$ more than angle $PQR$. What is the measure of angle $PQS$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Angle $RQS$ is $38 + 27 = 65$ degrees. Angle $PQS$ is the sum of its two parts: $38 + 65 = 103$ degrees.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles that make up a larger angle
questions.stem: Rays from the same point split a $150^\circ$ angle into three adjacent angles. The first two measure $42^\circ$ and $57^\circ$. What is the measure of the third angle in degrees?
questions.solution: The three angles add up to $150^\circ$: $150 - 42 - 57 = 51$. The choice 99 is $42 + 57$, 108 is $150 - 42$, and 93 is $150 - 57$.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Lines $AB$ and $CD$ cross at point $O$, which lies between $A$ and $B$ and between $C$ and $D$. Which angle is vertical to angle $AOC$?
choices: angle $COB$
angle $AOD$
angle $AOB$
angle $BOD$
questions.answer: angle $BOD$
questions.solution: Vertical angles are across from each other. Ray $OB$ is opposite ray $OA$, and ray $OD$ is opposite ray $OC$, so the angle across from angle $AOC$ is angle $BOD$. Angles $COB$ and $AOD$ are next to angle $AOC$, and angle $AOB$ is a straight angle.

solve.answer: angle $BOD$
solve.work: AOC uses rays OA and OC; the opposite rays are OB and OD, so the vertical angle is BOD. AOB is a straight angle; COB and AOD are adjacent to AOC.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Angle $P$ and angle $Q$ are supplementary. Angle $Q$ and angle $R$ are supplementary. Which statement must be true?
choices: Angle $P$ and angle $R$ have equal measures.
Angle $P$ and angle $R$ are supplementary.
Angle $P$ and angle $R$ are complementary.
Angle $P$ is larger than angle $R$.
questions.answer: Angle $P$ and angle $R$ have equal measures.
questions.solution: Angle $P = 180 - Q$ and angle $R = 180 - Q$, so angles $P$ and $R$ are equal. They add up to $2(180 - Q)$, which need not be 180 or 90, and neither one has to be larger.

solve.answer: Angle $P$ and angle $R$ have equal measures.
solve.work: P = 180 - Q and R = 180 - Q, so P = R. Complementary/supplementary would need specific values; P larger is false.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Which of these could be the measures of a pair of vertical angles?
choices: $85^\circ$ and $95^\circ$
$85^\circ$ and $5^\circ$
$85^\circ$ and $275^\circ$
$85^\circ$ and $85^\circ$
questions.answer: $85^\circ$ and $85^\circ$
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so only $85^\circ$ and $85^\circ$ can be a pair. The pair $85^\circ$ and $95^\circ$ adds to 180, and $85^\circ$ and $5^\circ$ adds to 90.

solve.answer: $85^\circ$ and $85^\circ$
solve.work: Vertical angles are equal: only 85 and 85.

questions.skill: Complementary angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two complementary angles measure $(4x + 10)^\circ$ and $(2x + 8)^\circ$. What is the measure of the smaller angle in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 90: $(4x + 10) + (2x + 8) = 90$, so $6x + 18 = 90$, $6x = 72$ and $x = 12$. The angles are $4 \times 12 + 10 = 58$ and $2 \times 12 + 8 = 32$ degrees. The smaller is 32.

questions.skill: Complementary angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Angle $A$ measures $(2x + 5)^\circ$ and its complement, angle $B$, measures $(x - 5)^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $A$ in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 90: $(2x + 5) + (x - 5) = 90$, so $3x = 90$ and $x = 30$. Angle $A$ is $2 \times 30 + 5 = 65$ degrees. The choice 25 is angle $B$, 30 is $x$, and 60 is $2x$.

questions.skill: Complementary angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: A right angle is split into three adjacent angles that measure $x^\circ$, $(x + 15)^\circ$ and $(2x + 15)^\circ$. What is the measure of the largest of the three angles in degrees?
questions.solution: The three angles add up to 90: $x + (x + 15) + (2x + 15) = 90$, so $4x + 30 = 90$, $4x = 60$ and $x = 15$. The angles are 15, 30 and 45 degrees. The largest is 45.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and straight lines with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two supplementary angles measure $(7x - 5)^\circ$ and $(3x + 15)^\circ$. What is the measure of the larger angle in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 180: $(7x - 5) + (3x + 15) = 180$, so $10x + 10 = 180$, $10x = 170$ and $x = 17$. The angles are $7 \times 17 - 5 = 114$ and $3 \times 17 + 15 = 66$ degrees. The larger is 114.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and straight lines with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Points $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on a straight line with $B$ between $A$ and $C$, and $D$ is a point off the line. Angle $ABD$ measures $(4x + 10)^\circ$ and angle $DBC$ measures $(2x + 20)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: The two angles make a straight angle, so $(4x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180$. Then $6x + 30 = 180$, $6x = 150$ and $x = 25$. The choice 10 uses 90 instead of 180, 30 ignores the added numbers, and 55 uses 360.

solve.work: ABD and DBC form a linear pair: 6x + 30 = 180, x = 25 (angles 110 and 70).

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and straight lines with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: An angle measures $(2x + 6)^\circ$ and its supplement measures $(4x - 18)^\circ$. What is the measure of the angle in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 180: $(2x + 6) + (4x - 18) = 180$, so $6x - 12 = 180$, $6x = 192$ and $x = 32$. The angle is $2 \times 32 + 6 = 70$ degrees (and its supplement is 110).

questions.skill: Vertical angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: The vertical angles formed by two crossing lines measure $(5x - 9)^\circ$ and $(3x + 15)^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so $5x - 9 = 3x + 15$. Then $2x = 24$ and $x = 12$. (Check: both angles are $51^\circ$.)

questions.skill: Vertical angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Angle 1 and angle 3 are vertical angles. Angle 1 measures $(2x + 18)^\circ$ and angle 3 measures $(5x - 24)^\circ$. What is the measure of angle 1 in degrees?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal: $2x + 18 = 5x - 24$, so $3x = 42$ and $x = 14$. Angle 1 is $2 \times 14 + 18 = 46$ degrees. The choice 14 is just $x$, 134 is the supplement, and 28 is $2x$.

questions.skill: Vertical angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two lines cross. The angles across from each other measure $(x + 40)^\circ$ and $(3x - 10)^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal: $x + 40 = 3x - 10$, so $50 = 2x$ and $x = 25$. The choice 15 comes from a sign error, 50 forgets to divide by 2, and 20 ignores the $-10$.

questions.skill: Choose the equation for an unknown angle
questions.stem: An angle measures $x^\circ$. Its supplement measures $20^\circ$ more than the angle. Which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: The supplement measures $x + 20$, and an angle and its supplement add up to 180. So $x + (x + 20) = 180$. The equation with 90 is for a complement, and $x + (x - 20) = 180$ subtracts 20 instead of adding.

solve.work: Supplement = x + 20, and angle + supplement = 180: x + (x + 20) = 180.

questions.skill: Choose the equation for an unknown angle
questions.stem: The complement of an angle is three times the angle. If the angle measures $x^\circ$, which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: The complement measures $3x$, and an angle and its complement add up to 90. So $x + 3x = 90$.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross and form four angles. One angle measures $138^\circ$. What is the sum of the measures of the other three angles in degrees?
questions.solution: The four angles around a crossing add up to $360^\circ$, so the other three add up to $360 - 138 = 222$ degrees. (They are $138$, $42$ and $42$.)

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Lines $AB$ and $CD$ cross at point $O$, which lies between $A$ and $B$ and between $C$ and $D$. Angle $AOC$ measures $64^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $AOD$ minus the measure of angle $BOD$, in degrees?
questions.solution: Angle $AOD$ is next to angle $AOC$, so it is $180 - 64 = 116$ degrees. Angle $BOD$ is vertical to angle $AOC$, so it is $64$ degrees. The difference is $116 - 64 = 52$ degrees.

solve.work: AOD is adjacent to AOC: 180 - 64 = 116. BOD is vertical to AOC: 64. 116 - 64 = 52.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross and one angle measures $70^\circ$. Going around the crossing point in order, which list gives the measures of the four angles?
questions.solution: Angles next to each other add up to 180 and angles across from each other are equal. So the order around the point is $70, 110, 70, 110$. The other lists put two equal angles next to each other, which would not make a straight line, or use the complement 20.

solve.work: Opposite angles equal, neighbours sum to 180: in order 70, 110, 70, 110. The list 70,110,110,70 would put two 110s and two 70s next to each other.

questions.skill: An angle compared with its complement or supplement
questions.stem: An angle is twice as large as its complement. What is the measure of the angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Its complement is $90 - x$, so $x = 2(90 - x)$. Then $3x = 180$ and $x = 60$. (Its complement is 30.) The choice 30 is the complement, 45 is the angle if they were equal, and 120 is twice the answer.

questions.skill: An angle compared with its complement or supplement
questions.stem: An angle is $40^\circ$ more than its complement. What is the measure of the angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Its complement is $90 - x$, so $x = (90 - x) + 40$. Then $2x = 130$ and $x = 65$. (Its complement is 25, and $65 - 25 = 40$.)

questions.skill: Adjacent angles in a ratio
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One of the angles formed is 4 times as large as an angle next to it. What is the measure of the smaller angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Two angles next to each other where lines cross add to $180^\circ$. If the smaller angle is $x$, the larger is $4x$, so $x + 4x = 180$. Then $5x = 180$ and $x = 36$ degrees.

solve.work: Adjacent angles at a crossing are supplementary: x + 4x = 180, x = 36 (other is 144).

questions.skill: Supplement and complement together
questions.stem: The supplement of an angle is $20^\circ$ more than twice the angle's complement. What is the measure of the angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Its supplement is $180 - x$ and its complement is $90 - x$. So $180 - x = 2(90 - x) + 20 = 200 - 2x$. Adding $2x$ to both sides: $180 + x = 200$, so $x = 20$. Check: supplement 160, complement 70, and $2 \times 70 + 20 = 160$.

solve.work: 180 - x = 2(90 - x) + 20 = 200 - 2x, so x = 20. Check: supplement 160, complement 70, 2 x 70 + 20 = 160.

questions.skill: Unknown angle at an intersection
questions.stem: Lines $AB$ and $CD$ cross at point $O$. Angle $AOC$ measures $(3x + 10)^\circ$ and angle $COB$ measures $(2x + 20)^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $AOD$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Angles $AOC$ and $COB$ are next to each other along the straight line $AB$, so they add to 180: $3x + 10 + 2x + 20 = 180$. Then $5x = 150$ and $x = 30$, so angle $AOC$ is $3 \times 30 + 10 = 100$ degrees. Angle $AOD$ is next to angle $AOC$ along the straight line $CD$, so it measures $180 - 100 = 80$ degrees. (It is also the vertical angle of $COB$, which is $2 \times 30 + 20 = 80$.)

solve.work: AOC and COB form straight angle AOB: 3x + 10 + 2x + 20 = 180, x = 30. AOC = 100, COB = 80. AOD is vertical to COB (OA opposite OB, OD opposite OC), so AOD = 80 (also 180 - AOC).

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Angle $P$ is complementary to angle $Q$, and angle $Q$ is complementary to angle $R$. Angle $P$ measures $31^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $R$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Angle $Q$ is $90 - 31 = 59$ degrees. Angle $R$ is $90 - 59 = 31$ degrees. Two angles that are complementary to the same angle have equal measures.

solve.work: P + Q = 90 so Q = 59. Q + R = 90 so R = 31 (R equals P).

questions.skill: Complementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: An angle measures $64^\circ$. Find its complement. Then find the supplement of that complement. What is the final measure in degrees?
questions.solution: The complement of $64^\circ$ is $90 - 64 = 26$ degrees. The supplement of $26^\circ$ is $180 - 26 = 154$ degrees.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: An angle measures $116^\circ$. A ray splits its supplement into two equal angles. What is the measure of each of the two equal angles in degrees?
questions.solution: The supplement of $116^\circ$ is $180 - 116 = 64$ degrees. Splitting it into two equal angles gives $64 \div 2 = 32$ degrees each.

solve.work: Supplement = 180 - 116 = 64. Split in two equal parts: 32.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles: find the missing angle
questions.stem: Angle $A$ and angle $B$ are supplementary, and angle $A$ is an acute angle. Which statement must be true about angle $B$?
choices: Angle $B$ is an acute angle.
Angle $B$ is a right angle.
Angle $B$ is smaller than angle $A$.
Angle $B$ is an obtuse angle.
questions.answer: Angle $B$ is an obtuse angle.
questions.solution: Angle $A$ is less than $90^\circ$, so angle $B = 180 - A$ is greater than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$. That makes it obtuse. It is larger than $A$, and it is a right angle only if $A$ is $90^\circ$.

solve.answer: Angle $B$ is an obtuse angle.
solve.work: 0 < A < 90, B = 180 - A, so 90 < B < 180: B is obtuse. B is larger than A, not smaller; not acute; not right.

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One pair of vertical angles has a sum of $146^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of each of the other two angles?
questions.solution: Each angle of the first pair is $146 \div 2 = 73$ degrees. An angle next to it is $180 - 73 = 107$ degrees, and the other pair are vertical angles with the same measure. The choice 73 is one of the first pair, 34 is $180 - 146$, and 214 is $360 - 146$.

solve.work: Vertical pair equal, each 146/2 = 73. Each of the other two = 180 - 73 = 107.

questions.skill: Vertical angles: find the measure
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One pair of vertical angles measures $d^\circ$ in all (the two angles together). Which expression gives the measure of each of the other two angles?
questions.solution: Each angle of the first pair measures $\frac{d}{2}$. An angle next to it is $180 - \frac{d}{2}$, and the other pair are vertical angles with that measure. The expression $360 - d$ is the total of the other two angles, not each one.

solve.work: Each of the pair = d/2. Each other angle = 180 - d/2 (equivalently (360 - d)/2).

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: Four angles lie side by side along a straight line. Each angle is $10^\circ$ larger than the angle before it. What is the measure of the largest angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Call the smallest angle $a$. The angles are $a$, $a + 10$, $a + 20$ and $a + 30$, and they add up to $180$. So $4a + 60 = 180$, $4a = 120$ and $a = 30$. The largest angle is $30 + 30 = 60$ degrees.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles along a straight line (sum 180)
questions.stem: Rays split a straight angle into three angles. The second angle is twice the first, and the third angle is three times the first. What is the measure of the third angle in degrees?
questions.solution: If the first angle is $x$, the angles are $x$, $2x$ and $3x$, which add up to $6x = 180$. So $x = 30$, and the third angle is $3 \times 30 = 90$ degrees.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles that make up a larger angle
questions.stem: Angle $AOD$ measures $126^\circ$. Rays $OB$ and $OC$ lie inside it, in that order from $OA$. Angle $AOB$ measures $30^\circ$, and angle $BOC$ is $12^\circ$ larger than angle $AOB$. What is the measure of angle $COD$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Angle $BOC$ is $30 + 12 = 42$ degrees. The three angles add up to angle $AOD$, so angle $COD$ is $126 - 30 - 42 = 54$ degrees.

questions.skill: Adjacent angles that make up a larger angle
questions.stem: Angle $AOC$ measures $84^\circ$ and ray $OB$ lies inside it. Angle $AOB$ is $12^\circ$ more than twice angle $BOC$. What is the measure of angle $AOB$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Let angle $BOC$ be $y$. Then angle $AOB$ is $2y + 12$, and $y + 2y + 12 = 84$. So $3y = 72$ and $y = 24$. Angle $AOB$ is $2 \times 24 + 12 = 60$ degrees.

solve.work: Let BOC = y, AOB = 2y + 12. 3y + 12 = 84, y = 24. AOB = 60.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Two lines cross and make four angles. Which statement is always true?
choices: All four angles are equal.
Two angles that are next to each other are equal.
Two angles that are next to each other add up to $180^\circ$.
Two angles that are across from each other add up to $180^\circ$.
questions.answer: Two angles that are next to each other add up to $180^\circ$.
questions.solution: Angles next to each other along one of the lines make a straight angle, so they add up to $180^\circ$. The four angles are all equal only when the lines are perpendicular, and angles across from each other are equal (so they add up to 180 only if each is 90).

solve.answer: Two angles that are next to each other add up to $180^\circ$.
solve.work: Adjacent angles at a crossing form a linear pair: always 180. Opposite angles sum to 180 only if each is 90; all equal only when perpendicular; adjacent equal only when perpendicular.

questions.skill: Name and compare angle relationships
questions.stem: Which of these is impossible?
choices: two complementary angles that are both obtuse
two supplementary angles that are both right angles
two vertical angles that are both obtuse
two complementary angles that are each $45^\circ$
questions.answer: two complementary angles that are both obtuse
questions.solution: Obtuse angles are greater than $90^\circ$, so two of them add up to more than 180 and cannot be complementary (which needs a sum of 90). Two right angles are supplementary, vertical angles of $120^\circ$ are both obtuse, and $45 + 45 = 90$.

solve.answer: two complementary angles that are both obtuse
solve.work: Two obtuse angles sum to more than 180, so cannot sum to 90: impossible. 90+90 = 180 possible; 45+45 = 90 possible; vertical angles both obtuse possible (e.g., 120 and 120).

questions.skill: Complementary angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: An angle measures $(6x - 4)^\circ$ and its complement measures $(2x + 14)^\circ$. How many degrees larger is the bigger of the two angles than the smaller one?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 90: $(6x - 4) + (2x + 14) = 90$, so $8x + 10 = 90$, $8x = 80$ and $x = 10$. The angles are $6 \times 10 - 4 = 56$ and $2 \times 10 + 14 = 34$ degrees. The difference is $56 - 34 = 22$.

questions.skill: Complementary angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Angle $A$ measures $(3x + 2)^\circ$ and angle $B$ measures $(5x - 8)^\circ$. The two angles are complementary. What is the measure of the supplement of angle $A$ in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 90: $(3x + 2) + (5x - 8) = 90$, so $8x - 6 = 90$, $8x = 96$ and $x = 12$. Angle $A$ is $3 \times 12 + 2 = 38$ degrees. Its supplement is $180 - 38 = 142$ degrees.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and straight lines with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Three angles lie side by side along a straight line. They measure $x^\circ$, $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and $(3x - 10)^\circ$. What is the measure of the largest angle in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 180: $x + (2x + 10) + (3x - 10) = 180$, so $6x = 180$ and $x = 30$. The angles are 30, 70 and 80 degrees. The largest is 80. The choice 70 is the middle angle, 30 is $x$, and 90 is $3x$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and straight lines with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: A straight line is split into two angles that measure $(5x + 7)^\circ$ and $(7x - 19)^\circ$. What is the positive difference between the two angles in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 180: $(5x + 7) + (7x - 19) = 180$, so $12x - 12 = 180$, $12x = 192$ and $x = 16$. The angles are $5 \times 16 + 7 = 87$ and $7 \times 16 - 19 = 93$ degrees. The difference is $93 - 87 = 6$.

solve.issues: Minor: 'A straight line is split into two angles' is loose; 'A ray splits a straight angle into two angles' would be precise. Meaning is still clear.

questions.skill: Vertical angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle measures $(9x - 20)^\circ$ and the angle across from it measures $(6x + 25)^\circ$. What is the measure of an angle next to either of them, in degrees?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal: $9x - 20 = 6x + 25$, so $3x = 45$ and $x = 15$. Each of these angles is $9 \times 15 - 20 = 115$ degrees. An angle next to one of them is $180 - 115 = 65$ degrees. The choice 115 is the vertical pair itself, 15 is $x$, and 295 is $180 + 115$.

questions.skill: Vertical angles with expressions (equation)
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle measures $(3x + 10)^\circ$ and its vertical angle measures $(5x - 20)^\circ$. What is the sum of the measures of the other two angles in degrees?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal: $3x + 10 = 5x - 20$, so $30 = 2x$ and $x = 15$. Each of these angles is $3 \times 15 + 10 = 55$ degrees. The four angles add up to 360, so the other two add up to $360 - 2 \times 55 = 250$ degrees. (Each is $180 - 55 = 125$.)

questions.skill: Choose the equation for an unknown angle
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle measures $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and an angle next to it measures $(3x - 5)^\circ$. Which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: Angles next to each other where two lines cross are supplementary, so they add up to 180. The equation $2x + 10 = 3x - 5$ would be for vertical angles, 90 is for complements, and 360 is for all four angles.

solve.work: Adjacent angles at a crossing are a linear pair: (2x + 10) + (3x - 5) = 180 (x = 35, angles 80 and 100).

questions.skill: Choose the equation for an unknown angle
questions.stem: The supplement of an angle is $15^\circ$ less than four times the angle's complement. If the angle measures $x^\circ$, which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.solution: The supplement is $180 - x$ and the complement is $90 - x$. "$15$ less than four times the complement" is $4(90 - x) - 15$. So $180 - x = 4(90 - x) - 15$. The other choices add 15, swap supplement and complement, or use the angle itself instead of its complement.

solve.work: Supplement 180 - x; complement 90 - x; '15 less than four times the complement' = 4(90 - x) - 15. Check: x = 55 gives 125 = 4(35) - 15.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle is $30^\circ$ more than an angle next to it. What is the measure of the larger of these two angles in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the smaller angle be $a$. The larger is $a + 30$, and they are next to each other so $a + (a + 30) = 180$. Then $2a = 150$ and $a = 75$. The larger angle is $75 + 30 = 105$ degrees.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle is $30^\circ$ less than twice the measure of an angle next to it. What is the measure of the smaller of the two angles in degrees?
questions.solution: Let one angle be $a$. The angle next to it is $2a - 30$. They add up to 180: $a + 2a - 30 = 180$, so $3a = 210$ and $a = 70$. The other angle is $2 \times 70 - 30 = 110$. The smaller is 70 degrees.

solve.work: Let neighbour = y, angle = 2y - 30. y + 2y - 30 = 180, y = 70, angle = 110. Smaller = 70.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Lines $AB$ and $CD$ cross at point $O$, which lies between $A$ and $B$ and between $C$ and $D$. Angle $AOC$ measures $(4x - 6)^\circ$ and angle $COB$ measures $(2x + 30)^\circ$. What is the sum of the measures of angle $AOC$ and angle $BOD$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Angles $AOC$ and $COB$ are next to each other, so $(4x - 6) + (2x + 30) = 180$. Then $6x + 24 = 180$, $6x = 156$ and $x = 26$. Angle $AOC$ is $4 \times 26 - 6 = 98$ degrees. Angle $BOD$ is vertical to it, so it is also 98. The sum is $98 + 98 = 196$ degrees.

solve.work: AOC and COB are a linear pair: 6x + 24 = 180, x = 26. AOC = 98, COB = 82. BOD is vertical to AOC = 98. Sum = 196.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Two lines cross. Sam says, "If one of the four angles is acute, then exactly two of the angles are acute." Which sentence tells whether Sam is correct?
choices: No. Only the one angle is acute, and all the other angles are obtuse.
Yes. The angle across from it is also acute, and the other two are obtuse.
No. All four angles are acute when one of the angles is acute.
No. Three of the angles are acute when one of the angles is acute.
questions.answer: Yes. The angle across from it is also acute, and the other two are obtuse.
questions.solution: The angle across from an acute angle is equal to it, so it is acute too. An angle next to an acute angle is $180$ minus an acute angle, which is more than 90, so the other two angles are obtuse. Sam is correct.

solve.answer: Yes. The angle across from it is also acute, and the other two are obtuse.
solve.work: If one angle is acute, its vertical angle is equal (acute) and the two neighbours are 180 minus it (obtuse). Exactly two acute: Sam is right.

questions.skill: Intersecting lines: several angles, several steps
questions.stem: Lines $AB$ and $CD$ cross at point $O$, which lies between $A$ and $B$ and between $C$ and $D$. Ray $OE$ lies inside angle $AOC$. Angle $AOE$ measures $25^\circ$ and angle $EOC$ measures $40^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $BOC$ in degrees?
questions.solution: Angle $AOC$ is made of angles $AOE$ and $EOC$, so it is $25 + 40 = 65$ degrees. Angle $BOC$ is next to angle $AOC$ along line $AB$, so it is $180 - 65 = 115$ degrees.

solve.work: AOC = 25 + 40 = 65. BOC is adjacent to AOC on line AB: 180 - 65 = 115.

questions.skill: An angle compared with its complement or supplement
questions.stem: The supplement of an angle is three times the angle's complement. What is the measure of the angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Then $180 - x = 3(90 - x)$, so $180 - x = 270 - 3x$, $2x = 90$ and $x = 45$. Check: the supplement is 135 and the complement is 45, and $3 \times 45 = 135$. The choice 135 is the supplement itself. For 60, the supplement (120) is four times the complement (30), not three times.

questions.skill: An angle compared with its complement or supplement
questions.stem: The complement of an angle is $10^\circ$ less than one third of the angle's supplement. What is the measure of the angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Its complement is $90 - x$ and its supplement is $180 - x$. So $90 - x = \frac{180 - x}{3} - 10$. Multiply by 3: $270 - 3x = 180 - x - 30$, so $120 = 2x$ and $x = 60$. Check: the complement is 30 and the supplement is 120, and $\frac{120}{3} - 10 = 30$.

questions.skill: An angle compared with its complement or supplement
questions.stem: For any angle that is smaller than $90^\circ$, how does the angle's supplement compare with its complement?
choices: The supplement is always $180^\circ$ greater than the complement.
The supplement is always twice the complement.
The supplement and the complement are always equal.
The supplement is always $90^\circ$ greater than the complement.
questions.answer: The supplement is always $90^\circ$ greater than the complement.
questions.solution: For an angle $x$, the supplement is $180 - x$ and the complement is $90 - x$. Their difference is $(180 - x) - (90 - x) = 90$, whatever $x$ is.

solve.answer: The supplement is always $90^\circ$ greater than the complement.
solve.work: (180 - x) - (90 - x) = 90 for every x, so the supplement is always 90 greater.

questions.skill: An angle compared with its complement or supplement
questions.stem: The complement and the supplement of an angle add up to $210^\circ$. What is the measure of the angle in degrees?
questions.solution: Let the angle be $x$. Then $(90 - x) + (180 - x) = 210$, so $270 - 2x = 210$, $2x = 60$ and $x = 30$. Check: the complement is 60, the supplement is 150, and $60 + 150 = 210$.

questions.skill: Angles around a point
questions.stem: Three straight lines cross at the same point, forming six angles. Each angle has an equal angle directly across from it. Going once around the point, the first three angles measure $35^\circ$, $62^\circ$ and $x^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: The six angles add up to 360, and the second three are equal to the first three (they are across from them). So the first three add up to $360 \div 2 = 180$. Then $35 + 62 + x = 180$ and $x = 83$.

solve.work: The six angles in order are 35, 62, x, 35, 62, x (each opposite its equal). Also 35 + 62 + x = 180 since three consecutive angles span a straight line. x = 180 - 97 = 83.

questions.skill: Theoretical probability of one event
questions.stem: A bag has 3 red marbles, 5 blue marbles and 2 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is green? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: There are $3 + 5 + 2 = 10$ marbles and 2 of them are green. The probability is $\frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}$.

questions.skill: Size of a sample space
questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped and a fair six-sided die is rolled. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.solution: The coin can land 2 ways and the die can land 6 ways. Every coin result pairs with every die result: $2 \times 6 = 12$ outcomes, such as (heads, 1) and (tails, 6).

questions.skill: Probability of two heads
questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped two times. What is the probability of getting two heads?
questions.solution: List the equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. Only HH is two heads, so the probability is $\frac{1}{4}$. (1/3 wrongly counts HT and TH as one outcome; 3/4 is the chance of at least one head.)

questions.skill: Theoretical probability of a single event
questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.solution: The numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so 2 of the 6 equally likely outcomes work. The probability is $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$. (1/2 wrongly counts the 4 as well, 1/6 counts only one number, and 2/3 is the chance of rolling 4 or less.)

solve.work: Numbers greater than 4 on a die: 5 and 6, so 2 of 6 outcomes. 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.skill: Theoretical probability of a single event
questions.stem: A fair spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability that it lands on an even number?
questions.solution: The even numbers are 2, 4, 6 and 8, which is 4 of the 8 equally likely sections. The probability is $\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$. (1/8 counts one section, 3/8 leaves out the 8, and 1/4 counts only 2 sections.)

solve.work: Even numbers 1-8: 2, 4, 6, 8, so 4 of 8 equal sections. 4/8 = 1/2.

questions.skill: Probability when outcomes are not equally likely
questions.stem: A spinner is split into three sections that are red, blue and green. The red section covers $\frac{1}{2}$ of the spinner and the blue section covers $\frac{1}{4}$. What is the probability that the spinner lands on green? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: The probabilities of all the outcomes add to 1. Red and blue together are $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$, so green is $1 - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.skill: Probability when outcomes are not equally likely
questions.stem: A bag has 2 red marbles and 8 blue marbles. Tia says, "There are 2 colors, so the probability of drawing a red marble is $\frac{1}{2}$." What is the actual probability of drawing a red marble?
questions.solution: The marbles are not equally split between the colors. There are $2 + 8 = 10$ marbles and 2 are red, so the probability is $\frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}$. (1/2 is Tia's mistake of counting colors instead of marbles; 1/4 compares the 2 red marbles to the 8 blue ones, and 1/8 uses only the blue count.)

solve.work: 10 marbles, 2 red: 2/10 = 1/5. Colors are not equally likely, so Tia is wrong.

questions.skill: Probability when outcomes are not equally likely
questions.stem: A weighted coin lands on heads with probability $\frac{3}{5}$. What is the probability that it lands on tails? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: Heads and tails are the only outcomes, so their probabilities add to 1. The probability of tails is $1 - \frac{3}{5} = \frac{2}{5}$.

questions.skill: Counting the outcomes of a compound event
questions.stem: A lunch special comes with one sandwich (turkey, cheese or egg) and one fruit (apple or banana). How many different lunches are possible?
questions.solution: Each of the 3 sandwiches can be paired with either of the 2 fruits. The number of lunches is $3 \times 2 = 6$.

questions.skill: Counting the outcomes of a compound event
questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 4 equal sections numbered 1 to 4 is spun. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.solution: The coin has 2 results and the spinner has 4 results, and every coin result can go with every spinner result. The sample space has $2 \times 4 = 8$ outcomes, such as (heads, 3). (6 adds instead of multiplying; 16 multiplies 4 by 4.)

questions.skill: Counting the outcomes of a compound event
questions.stem: A fair die is rolled two times, and the two results are recorded in order. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.solution: The first roll can be any of 6 numbers and so can the second roll. The number of outcomes is $6 \times 6 = 36$.

solve.issues: Minor: says 'a fair die' without 'six-sided', unlike the other questions; the usual reading gives 36, but stating six-sided would remove any doubt.
solve.work: Assuming a standard six-sided die: 6 x 6 = 36 ordered outcomes.

questions.skill: Listing a sample space
questions.stem: Nia spins a spinner with 3 equal sections labeled A, B and C, and then she flips a fair coin. What is the probability that the spinner lands on B and the coin lands on tails?
questions.solution: List the outcomes: A-heads, A-tails, B-heads, B-tails, C-heads, C-tails. There are 6 equally likely outcomes and only B-tails works, so the probability is $\frac{1}{6}$. (1/3 uses only the spinner, 1/2 uses only the coin, and 1/5 adds the 3 and the 2.)

questions.skill: Listing a sample space
questions.stem: A penny and a dime are tossed at the same time. Which list shows every outcome in the sample space, where H is heads and T is tails? (The first letter is the penny and the second letter is the dime.)
choices: HH, HT, TT
HH, TT
HT, TH
HH, HT, TH, TT
questions.answer: HH, HT, TH, TT
questions.solution: The penny can be H or T, and for each of those the dime can be H or T. That gives HH, HT, TH and TT. HT and TH are different outcomes because it matters which coin shows heads.

solve.answer: HH, HT, TH, TT
solve.work: Penny H or T, dime H or T: HH, HT, TH, TT (4 outcomes). Other lists omit outcomes.

questions.skill: Listing a sample space
questions.stem: Ben picks one shirt (red or blue) and one hat (green, yellow or black) at random. What is the probability that his outfit includes the blue shirt? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: List the outfits: red-green, red-yellow, red-black, blue-green, blue-yellow, blue-black. That is 6 outcomes and 3 of them have the blue shirt. The probability is $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$.

solve.work: Sample space 2 x 3 = 6 outfits; blue shirt in 3 of them: 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.skill: Using a table of outcomes
questions.stem: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled and the numbers are added. All 36 outcomes are written in a table, with one die down the side and the other across the top. What is the probability that the sum is 2?
questions.solution: A sum of 2 happens in only one cell of the table, when both dice show 1. The probability is $\frac{1}{36}$. (1/11 wrongly treats the 11 possible sums as equally likely.)

questions.skill: Using a table of outcomes
questions.stem: Two fair 4-sided dice, each numbered 1 to 4, are rolled and the numbers are added. The 16 outcomes are written in a table with one die down the side and the other across the top. What is the probability that the sum is 5? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: A sum of 5 comes from 1 and 4, 2 and 3, 3 and 2, or 4 and 1, which is 4 cells of the 16. The probability is $\frac{4}{16} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.skill: Using a tree diagram
questions.stem: Zoe draws a tree diagram for choosing a snack and a drink. The first stage has 4 branches, one for each snack. From the end of each of those branches, 3 more branches show the drinks. How many complete paths does the tree have?
questions.solution: Each of the 4 first branches continues with 3 second branches. The number of complete paths is $4 \times 3 = 12$.

solve.work: 4 first-stage branches, each with 3 second-stage branches: 4 x 3 = 12 paths.

questions.skill: Using a tree diagram
questions.stem: In a tree diagram for a game, the first branch "win" has probability $\frac{3}{4}$. From the end of that branch, the second branch "win again" has probability $\frac{1}{2}$. What is the probability of the path win, then win again? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: To find the probability of a path, multiply the probabilities along its branches: $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Using a tree diagram
questions.stem: A tree diagram shows the probabilities of the outcomes of one stage on its branches. When the probabilities on all the branches that start from the same point are added, what should the sum be?
questions.solution: The branches from one point show every possible outcome of that stage, so their probabilities must add to 1.

solve.work: Branches from one point cover all outcomes of that stage, so their probabilities sum to 1.

questions.skill: Compound events with replacement
questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped and a fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of getting heads and a 6?
questions.solution: The coin and the die do not affect each other, so multiply: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}$. (1/8 adds the 2 and 6 outcomes, 1/6 ignores the coin, and 2/3 adds the two probabilities.)

questions.skill: Compound events with replacement
questions.stem: A spinner has 5 equal sections and 2 of them are red. The spinner is spun two times. What is the probability that it lands on red both times?
questions.solution: Each spin is red with probability $\frac{2}{5}$, and the spins do not affect each other. Multiply: $\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{4}{25}$. (2/5 is the chance for one spin, 4/5 adds, and 2/25 forgets to multiply the tops.)

questions.skill: Compound events without replacement
questions.stem: A bag has 1 red marble and 1 blue marble. One marble is drawn and kept out of the bag, and then the other marble is drawn. What is the probability that the first marble is red and the second marble is blue? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: The two orders are red then blue, and blue then red, and they are equally likely. Only red then blue works, so the probability is $\frac{1}{2}$. (Or: the first is red with probability $\frac{1}{2}$, and then the second must be blue, which has probability 1.)

solve.work: P(first red) = 1/2; then only blue remains, P(second blue) = 1. 1/2 x 1 = 1/2.

questions.skill: Compound events without replacement
questions.stem: Three tickets labeled A, B and C are in a hat. Two tickets are drawn one after the other, and the first ticket is NOT put back. How many different ordered outcomes are there?
questions.solution: There are 3 choices for the first ticket and then 2 left for the second, so $3 \times 2 = 6$ outcomes: AB, AC, BA, BC, CA, CB. (9 would be right only if the first ticket were put back.)

solve.work: 3 choices for first, 2 for second: 3 x 2 = 6 (AB, AC, BA, BC, CA, CB).

questions.skill: Compound events without replacement
questions.stem: A bag has 2 red marbles and 2 blue marbles. Kai draws one marble and it is red. He does not put it back. He then draws a second marble. What is the probability that the second marble is red? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: After a red marble is removed, 3 marbles are left: 1 red and 2 blue. The chance that the second marble is red is $\frac{1}{3}$.

solve.work: After one red is removed: 1 red, 2 blue left. P(red) = 1/3.

questions.skill: Designing a simulation
questions.stem: A game has a 50% chance of winning each round. Which of these can be used to simulate one round?
choices: Flip a fair coin; heads means a win
Roll a fair six-sided die; 1 or 2 means a win
Spin a spinner with 5 equal sections; 1 or 2 means a win
Pick a random digit from 0 to 9; 0, 1, 2 or 3 means a win
questions.answer: Flip a fair coin; heads means a win
questions.solution: A fair coin lands heads half of the time, which matches a 50% chance. The die rule gives $\frac{2}{6}$, about 33%. The spinner rule gives $\frac{2}{5} = 40\%$, and the digit rule gives $\frac{4}{10} = 40\%$.

solve.answer: Flip a fair coin; heads means a win
solve.work: Digits 0-3: 4/10 = 0.4. Spinner 2/5 = 0.4. Die 1 or 2: 1/3. Coin heads: 1/2 = 50%. Only the coin works.

questions.skill: Designing a simulation
questions.stem: A student uses random digits from 0 to 9, each equally likely, to simulate an event with probability 0.4. How many of the ten digits should stand for the event happening?
questions.solution: Each digit has a $\frac{1}{10}$ chance. To get a probability of 0.4, which is $\frac{4}{10}$, the event should use 4 of the 10 digits.

questions.skill: Designing a simulation
questions.stem: A student uses random digits from 0 to 9 to simulate rolling a fair six-sided die. The digits 1 to 6 stand for the faces of the die. What should the student do when a 0, 7, 8 or 9 comes up?
choices: Count it as a 6
Count it as a 1
Stop and start the whole simulation over
Ignore it and use the next digit
questions.answer: Ignore it and use the next digit
questions.solution: Only the digits 1 to 6 match the die, and each is equally likely. Digits that do not stand for a face are skipped. Counting an extra digit as a 6 or a 1 would make that face more likely than the others.

solve.answer: Ignore it and use the next digit
solve.work: To keep 1-6 equally likely, discard 0, 7, 8, 9 and use the next digit. Counting them as 1 or 6 would bias those faces; restarting is wasteful and unnecessary.

questions.skill: Experimental probability from trials and simulations
questions.stem: A fair coin was flipped 20 times and landed on heads 9 times. What is the experimental probability of heads? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: The experimental probability is the number of times the event happened divided by the number of trials: $\frac{9}{20}$.

questions.skill: Experimental probability from trials and simulations
questions.stem: Rina dropped a paper cup 50 times. It landed on its side 14 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability that the cup lands on its side?
questions.solution: The cup landed on its side 14 times in 50 drops, so the experimental probability is $\frac{14}{50} = \frac{7}{25}$. (7/18 compares 14 to the 36 other drops, and 18/25 is the chance it did NOT land on its side.)

questions.skill: Experimental probability from trials and simulations
questions.stem: A spinner was spun 40 times and landed on blue 10 times. Based on these results, about how many times would you expect it to land on blue in 200 spins?
questions.solution: The experimental probability of blue is $\frac{10}{40} = \frac{1}{4}$. In 200 spins you would expect $\frac{1}{4} \times 200 = 50$ blues.

questions.skill: Expected results and the effect of more trials
questions.stem: A fair coin has landed on heads 5 times in a row. What is the probability that the next flip is heads?
questions.solution: A coin has no memory. Every flip of a fair coin has probability $\frac{1}{2}$ of heads, no matter what came before. (1/64 is the chance of six heads in a row before any flips are made.)

solve.work: Flips are independent; a fair coin still has P(heads) = 1/2.

questions.skill: Expected results and the effect of more trials
questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled 600 times. About how many times would you expect it to land on 4?
questions.solution: The probability of rolling a 4 is $\frac{1}{6}$. In 600 rolls you would expect about $\frac{1}{6} \times 600 = 100$ fours.

questions.skill: Expected results and the effect of more trials
