choices: The mean decreases from 17.5 to 16, and the median stays at 16.
The mean decreases from 17.5 to 16, and the median decreases to 15.
The mean stays at 17.5, and the median decreases to 15.
The mean and the median both stay the same.
questions.answer: The mean decreases from 17.5 to 16, and the median stays at 16.
questions.solution: With all 10 values the sum is 175, so the mean is 17.5, and the median is (16 + 16) / 2 = 16. Without 31, the sum is 144 and the mean is 144 / 9 = 16. The middle (5th) of the 9 remaining values is still 16. The extreme value changed the mean, not the median.

solve.answer: The mean decreases from 17.5 to 16, and the median stays at 16.

questions.skill: Judge the overlap of two distributions
questions.stem: Set A is 40, 42, 45, 47, 50, 52. Set B is 51, 53, 55, 56, 58, 60. Which statement is correct?
choices: Every value in Set B is greater than every value in Set A.
The sets overlap heavily, and their centers are about equal.
The sets overlap only between 51 and 52, and Set A's center is much greater.
The sets overlap only between 51 and 52, and Set B's center is much greater.
questions.answer: The sets overlap only between 51 and 52, and Set B's center is much greater.
questions.solution: A's greatest value is 52 and B's least value is 51, so the sets share only the stretch from 51 to 52. That is almost no overlap, but not none: 52 is not less than 51. The medians are 46 and 55.5, so B's center is 9.5 greater.

solve.answer: The sets overlap only between 51 and 52, and Set B's center is much greater.
solve.work: A 40-52, median 46; B 51-60, median 55.5. Overlap only 51-52 (B's 51 < A's 52, so 'every value' false). B's center ~9.5 greater.

questions.skill: Judge the overlap of two distributions
questions.stem: Set A has a mean of 30 and a mean absolute deviation (MAD) of 4. Set B has a mean of 42 and a MAD of 4. The difference between the means is how many times the MAD?
questions.solution: The difference between the means is 42 - 30 = 12. Since the MAD is 4, the difference is 12 / 4 = 3 times the MAD. The bigger this number is, the less the two sets overlap.

questions.skill: Judge the overlap of two distributions
questions.stem: Pair P is two data sets with means of 40 and 52, each with a MAD of 3. Pair Q is two data sets with means of 40 and 52, each with a MAD of 10. Which statement is correct?
choices: The two sets in Pair Q overlap less, because their MADs are greater.
The two sets in Pair P overlap less than the two sets in Pair Q.
The two pairs overlap equally, because the means are the same.
The two sets in Pair P overlap more, because their MADs are smaller.
questions.answer: The two sets in Pair P overlap less than the two sets in Pair Q.
questions.solution: The means are 12 apart in both pairs. In Pair P the values typically stay within about 3 of their mean, so the two sets barely touch (12 is 4 times the MAD). In Pair Q the values stray about 10 from their mean, so the sets overlap a lot (12 is only 1.2 times the MAD).

solve.answer: The two sets in Pair P overlap less than the two sets in Pair Q.
solve.work: Same mean gap 12. Small MAD (3) means tight sets so Pair P overlaps less; MAD 10 sets overlap more.

questions.skill: Plot two distributions on one number line
questions.stem: Class 1's 5 scores have a mean of 8. Class 2's 3 scores have a mean of 12. When all 8 scores are put on one number line, what is the mean of all of them?
questions.solution: Class 1 adds to 5 x 8 = 40 and Class 2 adds to 3 x 12 = 36. All 8 scores add to 76, so the mean is 76 / 8 = 9.5. (It is not 10, the mean of 8 and 12, because Class 1 has more scores.)

questions.skill: Plot two distributions on one number line
questions.stem: Set A has values from 0.2 to 1.4. Set B has values from 0.5 to 2.6. Which number line, with the marks shown, can display every value from both sets?
choices: From 0.2 to 1.4, with a mark every 0.2
From 0 to 3, with a mark every 0.5
From 0 to 2, with a mark every 0.5
From 0.5 to 2.6, with a mark every 0.5
questions.answer: From 0 to 3, with a mark every 0.5
questions.solution: The values run from 0.2 up to 2.6. A number line from 0 to 3 covers all of them. The line ending at 1.4 and the line ending at 2 cut off the greater values of Set B, and the line starting at 0.5 cuts off 0.2.

solve.answer: From 0 to 3, with a mark every 0.5
solve.work: Need 0.2 to 2.6. 0.2-1.4 and 0-2 miss 2.6; 0.5-2.6 misses 0.2. 0 to 3 covers all.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf plot
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf plot shows the masses of 11 rocks in kilograms. The key is 1 | 8 means 1.8 kilograms. Stem 1 has leaves 2, 5, 8, 8. Stem 2 has leaves 0, 1, 4, 4, 7. Stem 3 has leaves 3, 6. What is the median mass in kilograms?
questions.solution: The 11 masses in order are 1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 1.8, 2.0, 2.1, 2.4, 2.4, 2.7, 3.3, 3.6. The middle value is the 6th, which is 2.1 kilograms.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf plot
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf plot shows the number of cups of juice a shop sold each day. The key is 12 | 3 means 123. Stem 12 has leaves 3, 8. Stem 13 has leaves 0, 4, 4, 9. Stem 14 has leaves 2, 5, 6. Stem 15 has leaf 1. What is the range of the sales?
questions.solution: The least value is 123 (stem 12, leaf 3) and the greatest is 151 (stem 15, leaf 1). The range is 151 - 123 = 28 cups.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf plot
questions.stem: Two teams' points in nine games are shown in a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot. Team X: stem 3 has leaves 2, 6, 8; stem 4 has leaves 0, 1, 5, 5, 7; stem 5 has leaf 2. Team Y: stem 3 has leaf 1; stem 4 has leaves 4, 6; stem 5 has leaves 0, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9. A stem of 3 and a leaf of 2 means 32. Which statement is true?
choices: Team X's median is 12 greater than Team Y's median.
Team Y's median is 12 greater than Team X's median.
Team X has the greater range of the two teams.
Both teams have the same median.
questions.answer: Team Y's median is 12 greater than Team X's median.
questions.solution: Team X's scores in order: 32, 36, 38, 40, 41, 45, 45, 47, 52, so the median is 41 and the range is 20. Team Y's: 31, 44, 46, 50, 53, 55, 57, 58, 59, so the median is 53 and the range is 28. Y's median is 53 - 41 = 12 greater, and Y has the greater range.

solve.answer: Team Y's median is 12 greater than Team X's median.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf plot
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf plot shows six ages. Stem 2 has leaves 1, 4. Stem 3 has leaves 0, 5, 8. Stem 4 has leaf 4. A stem of 2 and a leaf of 1 means 21. What is the mean age?
questions.solution: The ages are 21, 24, 30, 35, 38 and 44. They add to 192, and 192 / 6 = 32.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or grouped frequency table
questions.stem: Two histograms use the same scores. Class A: 40 to 49: 2 students; 50 to 59: 6 students; 60 to 69: 9 students; 70 to 79: 3 students. Class B: 40 to 49: 1 student; 50 to 59: 3 students; 60 to 69: 8 students; 70 to 79: 8 students. How many more students in Class B than in Class A scored 60 or higher?
questions.solution: Class A: 9 + 3 = 12 students scored 60 or higher. Class B: 8 + 8 = 16 students. The difference is 16 - 12 = 4 students.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or grouped frequency table
questions.stem: Class A has 20 students and Class B has 40 students. In the histogram of Class A, the bar for scores of 80 to 89 shows 5 students. In the histogram of Class B, the bar for 80 to 89 shows 8 students. Which statement is correct?
choices: A greater fraction of Class A scored 80 to 89, because 5 out of 20 is greater than 8 out of 40.
A greater fraction of Class B scored 80 to 89, because 8 students is more than 5 students.
The two classes had the same fraction score 80 to 89, because both bars are tall.
The two classes cannot be compared, because they have different numbers of students.
questions.answer: A greater fraction of Class A scored 80 to 89, because 5 out of 20 is greater than 8 out of 40.
questions.solution: Compare fractions of each class, not counts. Class A: 5/20 = 1/4 = 25%. Class B: 8/40 = 1/5 = 20%. So a greater fraction of Class A scored 80 to 89, even though Class B has more such students.

solve.answer: A greater fraction of Class A scored 80 to 89, because 5 out of 20 is greater than 8 out of 40.

questions.skill: Read a box plot from its five-number summary
questions.stem: A box plot has a minimum of 10, a first quartile of 14, a median of 16, a third quartile of 28 and a maximum of 60. Which describes the data?
choices: The data are skewed toward the low values.
The data are skewed toward the high values.
The data are symmetric, because the median is inside the box.
The data are evenly spread across the whole range.
questions.answer: The data are skewed toward the high values.
questions.solution: The lower part of the box (14 to 16) is short and the upper part (16 to 28) is long. The upper whisker (28 to 60) is much longer than the lower whisker (10 to 14). The long tail is on the high side, so the data are skewed toward high values.

solve.answer: The data are skewed toward the high values.
solve.issues: Minor: 'skewed toward the high values' vs 'toward the low values' can be misread (most data ARE toward the low values). Clearer: 'skewed right, with a long tail toward the high values'.
solve.work: Left whisker 4, left box half 2, right box half 12, right whisker 32: long tail to the high side, i.e. skewed right.

questions.skill: Read a box plot from its five-number summary
questions.stem: Box plot A has a median of 36 and an interquartile range of 8. Box plot B has a median of 52 and an interquartile range of 8. The difference between the medians is how many times the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The difference between the medians is 52 - 36 = 16. Since the interquartile range is 8, the difference is 16 / 8 = 2 times the IQR.

questions.skill: Read a box plot from its five-number summary
questions.stem: A box plot has a minimum of 3, a first quartile of 9, a median of 14, a third quartile of 21 and a maximum of 38. Which statement is true?
choices: Half of the values are greater than 21.
Three quarters of the values are less than 14.
A quarter of the values are between 9 and 21.
Half of the values are between 9 and 21.
questions.answer: Half of the values are between 9 and 21.
questions.solution: The box, from the first quartile (9) to the third quartile (21), holds the middle half of the values. Only a quarter of the values are greater than 21, and half of the values are less than 14.

solve.answer: Half of the values are between 9 and 21.
solve.work: Middle half lies between Q1=9 and Q3=21. Others: quarter (wrong), half > 21 (only a quarter), 3/4 < 14 (only half).

questions.skill: Read a box plot from its five-number summary
questions.stem: In a box plot, the first quartile is 22, the median is 30, and the interquartile range is 16. What is the third quartile?
questions.solution: The interquartile range is the third quartile minus the first quartile, so the third quartile is 22 + 16 = 38.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: A dot plot of the heights of 20 people at a youth center shows one cluster of dots from 50 to 56 inches and a second cluster from 66 to 72 inches, with no dots between 57 and 65 inches. Which is the most reasonable conclusion?
choices: The data must contain mistakes, because heights should form one cluster.
The people probably come from two groups, such as children and adults, with different typical heights.
Most of the people are about 61 inches tall, the middle of the plot.
The people are all about the same height, because the dots are close together.
questions.answer: The people probably come from two groups, such as children and adults, with different typical heights.
questions.solution: Two separate clusters with a gap between them suggest two different groups mixed together. Nobody is about 61 inches tall, since there are no dots there, and the dots are not all close together.

solve.answer: The people probably come from two groups, such as children and adults, with different typical heights.
solve.work: Two separated clusters suggest two groups (e.g. children and adults) with different typical heights.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: Set 1 is 10, 20, 20, 20, 20, 30. Set 2 is 10, 10, 10, 30, 30, 30. Maia says, "Both sets have a range of 20 and a mean of 20, so they are spread out in the same way." Which reply is correct?
choices: She is not right: most of Set 1's values are at the center, but every value of Set 2 is far from the center.
She is right: sets with the same range and mean must be spread out in the same way.
She is not right: Set 1 has the greater range.
She is not right: the two sets have different means.
questions.answer: She is not right: most of Set 1's values are at the center, but every value of Set 2 is far from the center.
questions.solution: Both sets have a range of 20 and a mean of 20. But four of Set 1's six values equal 20, while every value of Set 2 is 10 away from 20. Set 2's values are typically much farther from the mean, so Set 2 is more spread out.

solve.answer: She is not right: most of Set 1's values are at the center, but every value of Set 2 is far from the center.
solve.work: Set 1 sum 120, mean 20, range 20; Set 2 sum 120, mean 20, range 20. Set 1 mostly at 20; Set 2 every value 10 from 20. Distributions differ.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: Box plot X has a minimum of 30, a first quartile of 52, a median of 60, a third quartile of 70 and a maximum of 80. Box plot Y has a minimum of 20, a first quartile of 35, a median of 50, a third quartile of 55 and a maximum of 65. Which statement is true?
choices: Every value in Plot X is greater than Plot Y's median.
Plot Y's median is greater than Plot X's first quartile.
Half of Plot Y's values are greater than Plot X's median.
At least three quarters of Plot X's values are greater than Plot Y's median.
questions.answer: At least three quarters of Plot X's values are greater than Plot Y's median.
questions.solution: Plot Y's median is 50 and Plot X's first quartile is 52, so at least three quarters of X's values are above 50. But X's minimum is 30, so not every value is. 50 is less than 52, so Plot Y's median is not greater than Plot X's first quartile. Y's third quartile is 55, below X's median of 60, so fewer than a quarter of Y's values are above 60.

solve.answer: At least three quarters of Plot X's values are greater than Plot Y's median.
solve.work: Y median 50. X Q1=52>50, so at least 75% of X values >50. Others: Y Q3 55 < X median 60 (false); 50<52 (false); X min 30<50 (false).

questions.skill: Compare two distributions on one number line
questions.stem: Dot plots of two classes' quiz scores share one number line. Class X has scores 52, 55, 58, 60, 63 and 70, and its median is 59. Class Y has scores 48, 61, 62, 66, 71 and 73. How many more of Class Y's scores than of Class X's scores are greater than 59?
questions.solution: In Class X, the scores greater than 59 are 60, 63 and 70, which is 3 scores. In Class Y, the scores greater than 59 are 61, 62, 66, 71 and 73, which is 5 scores. The difference is $5 - 3 = 2$.

questions.skill: Range
questions.stem: A set of data is 12, 7, 15, 9, 20, 11. What is the range?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value: $20 - 7 = 13$.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: A coach wants to describe how much the heights of her players vary from the shortest to the tallest. Which should she find?
choices: The median
The mean
The mode
The range
questions.answer: The range
questions.solution: The range, the greatest value minus the least value, describes how spread out the data are. The median, mean and mode describe the center, not the spread.

solve.answer: The range
solve.work: Shortest to tallest spread is the range.

questions.skill: Interquartile range from quartiles
questions.stem: The first quartile of a data set is 18 and the third quartile is 31. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The interquartile range (IQR) is the third quartile minus the first quartile: $31 - 18 = 13$.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: The heights of five bean plants, in centimeters, are 14, 9, 21, 17 and 12. What is the range of the heights?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value: 21 - 9 = 12 centimeters.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: The oldest member of a hiking club is 68 years old and the youngest member is 23 years old. What is the range of the members' ages in years?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value: 68 - 23 = 45 years.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: Which data set has a range of 9?
questions.solution: The range of 15, 6, 9 is 15 - 6 = 9. The others have ranges of 14 - 6 = 8, 20 - 7 = 13 and 9 - 2 = 7. Each of those contains the number 9, but the range is the greatest minus the least value.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: In seven soccer games, a team scored 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 2 and 6 goals. What is the range of the numbers of goals?
questions.solution: The greatest number of goals is 6 and the least is 0, so the range is 6 - 0 = 6 goals.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: Which calculation gives the range of a data set?
choices: greatest value - least value
greatest value + least value
greatest value / least value
(greatest value + least value) / 2
questions.answer: greatest value - least value
questions.solution: The range tells how far apart the ends of the data are, so it is the greatest value minus the least value.

solve.answer: greatest value - least value

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: A summary of test scores gives a least score of 41, a first quartile of 58, a median of 67, a third quartile of 79 and a greatest score of 96. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The interquartile range (IQR) is the third quartile minus the first quartile: 79 - 58 = 21. (The other numbers are not needed.)

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: What does the interquartile range (IQR) of a data set measure?
choices: The difference between the greatest and least values
How far the values are from the mean on average
The value in the middle of the data set
How spread out the middle half of the values is
questions.answer: How spread out the middle half of the values is
questions.solution: The IQR is the third quartile minus the first quartile, which is the length of the interval holding the middle half of the values. The difference between the greatest and least is the range, the average distance from the mean is the MAD, and the middle value is the median.

solve.answer: How spread out the middle half of the values is
solve.work: IQR = Q3-Q1, spread of the middle half.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: Find the interquartile range of the data 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13.
questions.solution: The lower half is 3, 5, 7 with median 5, so Q1 = 5. The upper half is 9, 11, 13 with median 11, so Q3 = 11. The IQR is 11 - 5 = 6.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: The mean of the data 3, 5, 9, 11 is 7. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the data?
questions.solution: The distances from the mean 7 are 4, 2, 2 and 4. Their mean is (4 + 2 + 2 + 4) / 4 = 12 / 4 = 3.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Five values have distances from their mean of 2, 0, 3, 1 and 4 units. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the five values?
questions.solution: The MAD is the mean of the distances from the mean: (2 + 0 + 3 + 1 + 4) / 5 = 10 / 5 = 2.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: What is the first step in finding the mean absolute deviation of a data set?
choices: Find the median of the data
Put the values in order from least to greatest
Square each value
Find the mean of the data
questions.answer: Find the mean of the data
questions.solution: The MAD measures the distances of the values from the MEAN, so the mean must be found first. Then find each value's distance from it, and take the mean of those distances.

solve.answer: Find the mean of the data
solve.work: MAD needs distances from the mean, so first find the mean.

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: Class A's quiz scores have a MAD of 1.5 points. Class B's quiz scores have a MAD of 4 points. Which class's scores are closer to their mean on average?
choices: Class A
Class B
Both classes are the same
It cannot be told from the MAD
questions.answer: Class A
questions.solution: The MAD is the average distance of the values from the mean. A smaller MAD means the scores are closer to the mean, so Class A's scores are.

solve.answer: Class A
solve.work: Smaller MAD means closer to the mean on average: Class A (1.5).

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: The IQR of Data Set P is much larger than the IQR of Data Set Q. What does this tell you?
choices: The values of P are greater than the values of Q.
Data Set P has more values than Data Set Q.
The middle half of the values of P is more spread out than the middle half of Q.
The median of P is greater than the median of Q.
questions.answer: The middle half of the values of P is more spread out than the middle half of Q.
questions.solution: The IQR measures how spread out the middle half of the values is, so a larger IQR means more spread. It does not say how large the values are, how many there are, or where the median is.

solve.answer: The middle half of the values of P is more spread out than the middle half of Q.
solve.work: IQR measures spread of the middle half; says nothing of count, median or size of values.

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: In one town the range of the daily high temperatures last month was 8 degrees. In another town it was 20 degrees. Which statement is correct?
choices: The temperatures varied more in the first town.
The temperatures varied more in the second town.
The second town was warmer.
The temperatures varied the same amount in both towns.
questions.answer: The temperatures varied more in the second town.
questions.solution: The range tells how far apart the greatest and least values are. A range of 20 is greater than a range of 8, so the temperatures varied more in the second town. The range says nothing about which town was warmer.

solve.answer: The temperatures varied more in the second town.
solve.work: Larger range (20 vs 8) means more variation in the second town; warmth not implied.

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: The scores on a quiz have a mean of 70 and a MAD of 6. On average, how many points are the scores away from the mean of 70?
questions.solution: The MAD is the average distance of the values from the mean, so the scores are on average 6 points away from 70.

solve.work: MAD is the average distance from the mean: 6.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: A data set is symmetric and has no extreme values. Which pair of measures is usually used to describe its center and spread?
choices: The mean and the interquartile range
The mean and the MAD
The median and the mean absolute deviation
The mode and the range
questions.answer: The mean and the MAD
questions.solution: For symmetric data without extreme values, the mean is a good center, and the MAD (which measures distance from the mean) goes with it. The median and the IQR are used together when the data are skewed or have extreme values.

solve.answer: The mean and the MAD
solve.work: Symmetric, no outliers: mean with MAD.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: Five houses on a street sold for 150, 155, 160, 162 and 900 thousand dollars. Which measure best describes a typical sale price?
choices: The median, 160 thousand dollars
The mean, 305.4 thousand dollars
The range, 750 thousand dollars
The greatest price, 900 thousand dollars
questions.answer: The median, 160 thousand dollars
questions.solution: One very high price (900) pulls the mean up to 305.4, which is higher than four of the five prices. The median, 160, is not affected by that extreme value, so it describes a typical price better. The range is a measure of spread, not of a typical price.

solve.answer: The median, 160 thousand dollars
solve.work: Mean (150+155+160+162+900)/5=305.4 is pulled by 900; median 160 is typical.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: A teacher wants to describe how spread out the middle half of her students' scores is. Which measure should she use?
choices: The range
The mean
The greatest score
The interquartile range
questions.answer: The interquartile range
questions.solution: The interquartile range is the length of the interval holding the middle half of the values. The range uses the extreme scores, and the mean and the greatest score are not measures of spread.

solve.answer: The interquartile range

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Bakery X puts a median of 12 cookies in a box, with an IQR of 1. Bakery Y also puts a median of 12 cookies in a box, with an IQR of 3. Which bakery's boxes are more consistent?
choices: Bakery X's, because their IQR is smaller
Bakery Y's, because their IQR is larger
They are equally consistent, because the medians are equal
Bakery X's, because its median is smaller
questions.answer: Bakery X's, because their IQR is smaller
questions.solution: The medians are equal, so the centers are the same. The IQR of X is smaller, so the middle half of its box counts are closer together: X's boxes are more consistent.

solve.answer: Bakery X's, because their IQR is smaller
solve.work: Same median; smaller IQR (1) means less variation: Bakery X.

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Set P is 4, 7, 9, 12. Set Q is 5, 6, 9, 10. How much greater is the range of Set P than the range of Set Q?
questions.solution: The range of P is 12 - 4 = 8. The range of Q is 10 - 5 = 5. The difference is 8 - 5 = 3.

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Set P is 3, 8, 10, 11, 14. Set Q is 6, 9, 9, 10, 11. Which statement is correct?
choices: Set P has the greater median and the smaller range.
Set P has the greater median and the greater range.
Set Q has the greater median and the greater range.
Set Q has the greater median and the smaller range.
questions.answer: Set P has the greater median and the greater range.
questions.solution: Median of P = 10 and median of Q = 9, so P has the greater median. Range of P = 14 - 3 = 11 and range of Q = 11 - 6 = 5, so P has the greater range.

solve.answer: Set P has the greater median and the greater range.
solve.work: P: median 10, range 11. Q: median 9, range 5. P greater on both.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The data set 10, 12, 13, 15 has a range of 5. A new value, 40, is added. What is the range of the data set now?
questions.solution: The new value is the greatest, so the range is 40 - 10 = 30. One extreme value raised the range from 5 to 30.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The greatest value in a data set of nine values is replaced by a much greater value. Which measure stays the same?
choices: The mean
The range
The mean absolute deviation
The median
questions.answer: The median
questions.solution: The median depends on the middle of the ordered list, and the replaced value is at the very end, so it stays the same. The mean, the range and the MAD all use the value that changed.

solve.answer: The median
solve.work: With 9 values the median is the 5th value, unchanged when the greatest grows. Range, mean and MAD all grow.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The data set 22, 25, 27, 30, 31, 78 has an extreme value, 78. By how much does the range decrease if 78 is removed?
questions.solution: With 78 the range is 78 - 22 = 56. Without it the greatest value is 31, so the range is 31 - 22 = 9. The range decreases by 56 - 9 = 47.

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: A data set has a range of 15 and a least value of 9. What is its greatest value?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value, so the greatest value is the least value plus the range: 9 + 15 = 24.

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A table shows how many pets students have. 0 pets: 6 students. 1 pet: 9 students. 2 pets: 5 students. 3 pets: 3 students. 5 pets: 1 student. What is the range of the number of pets?
questions.solution: The least number of pets is 0 and the greatest is 5, so the range is 5 - 0 = 5. (The counts of students do not matter for the range.)

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A dot plot of the ages of children at a party has 2 dots at 9, 5 dots at 10, 4 dots at 11 and 1 dot at 15. What is the range of the ages?
questions.solution: The leftmost dot is at 9 and the rightmost dot is at 15, so the range is 15 - 9 = 6 years.

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A dot plot has 3 dots at 2, 4 dots at 3 and 2 dots at 5. What is the median of the 9 values?
questions.solution: There are 9 dots, so the median is the 5th value in order. The first 3 dots are at 2, and the next 4 dots (the 4th to 7th) are at 3, so the 5th value is 3.

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A table shows the number of books students read: 2 books for 3 students, 4 books for 3 students, 5 books for 2 students and 7 books for 2 students. What is the mean number of books?
questions.solution: The total number of books is 2 x 3 + 4 x 3 + 5 x 2 + 7 x 2 = 6 + 12 + 10 + 14 = 42. There are 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10 students, so the mean is 42 / 10 = 4.2 books. (4.5 is the mean of 2, 4, 5 and 7, which ignores how many students read each amount; 42 is the total; 5.25 divides by 8.)

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: Which measure can be read directly from the leftmost and rightmost dots of a dot plot?
choices: The mean absolute deviation
The interquartile range
The mean
The range
questions.answer: The range
questions.solution: The leftmost dot is the least value and the rightmost dot is the greatest value, and their difference is the range. The IQR, MAD and mean all need more of the data.

solve.answer: The range

questions.skill: Mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the data set 2, 5, 5, 8.
questions.solution: The mean is $(2 + 5 + 5 + 8) \div 4 = 5$. The distances from 5 are 3, 0, 0 and 3. The mean of these distances is $6 \div 4 = 1.5$.

questions.skill: Interquartile range from raw data
questions.stem: Find the interquartile range of the data set 13, 3, 8, 5, 11, 2, 9, 6.
questions.solution: Put the values in order: 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13. The lower half is 2, 3, 5, 6, so the first quartile is $(3 + 5) \div 2 = 4$. The upper half is 8, 9, 11, 13, so the third quartile is $(9 + 11) \div 2 = 10$. The IQR is $10 - 4 = 6$.

questions.skill: Which measure resists extreme values
questions.stem: Which of these is least affected by one very extreme value in a data set?
choices: Interquartile range
Range
Mean absolute deviation
Mean
questions.answer: Interquartile range
questions.solution: The range uses the extreme values directly, and the mean and the MAD both use every value, so an extreme value changes them. The interquartile range uses only the middle half of the data, so one extreme value barely affects it.

solve.answer: Interquartile range
solve.work: IQR uses only the middle half, so one extreme value barely moves it; mean, range and MAD all use every value.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: The temperatures at noon on five winter days were $-3$, 2, $-8$, 0 and 5 degrees. What is the range of the temperatures?
questions.solution: The greatest temperature is 5 and the least is -8. The range is 5 - (-8) = 5 + 8 = 13 degrees.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: Six apples have masses of 1.2, 0.9, 1.5, 1.1, 0.7, 1.3 kilograms. What is the range of the masses, in kilograms?
questions.solution: The greatest mass is 1.5 and the least is 0.7. The range is 1.5 - 0.7 = 0.8 kilograms.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: The data set 12, 15, 19, 24, 30 has a range of 18. One more value will be added. Which new value would NOT change the range?
questions.solution: The range is set by the least and greatest values, 12 and 30. A new value of 20 lies between them, so the range stays 18. A new value of 10 or 8 would be the new least value (range 20 or 22), and 35 would be the new greatest value (range 23).

solve.work: Range stays 18 only if new value is within 12..30: 20. 10, 8 lower the least; 35 raises the greatest.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: Eight students recorded how many minutes they read: 7, 12, 15, 9, 20, 16, 11, 22. What is the interquartile range of the reading times?
questions.solution: Put the values in order: 7, 9, 11, 12, 15, 16, 20, 22. The lower half is 7, 9, 11, 12, so Q1 = (9 + 11) / 2 = 10. The upper half is 15, 16, 20, 22, so Q3 = (16 + 20) / 2 = 18. The IQR is 18 - 10 = 8.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: The number of points a player scored in ten games was 18, 5, 12, 3, 9, 15, 13, 20, 6, 8. What is the interquartile range of the scores?
questions.solution: In order: 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 13, 15, 18, 20. There are 10 values, so each half has 5. The lower half 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 has median 6 (Q1). The upper half 12, 13, 15, 18, 20 has median 15 (Q3). The IQR is 15 - 6 = 9.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: The data set 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 17, 19, 25 is in order. What are its first and third quartiles?
choices: 8 and 17
9 and 17
6 and 25
questions.solution: There are 8 values, so each half has 4. The lower half 6, 8, 9, 12 has median (8 + 9) / 2 = 8.5, which is Q1. The upper half 14, 17, 19, 25 has median (17 + 19) / 2 = 18, which is Q3. (6 and 25 are the least and greatest values.)

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: A shop sold the following numbers of sandwiches on twelve days: 24, 5, 13, 8, 27, 10, 18, 22, 7, 15, 12, 20. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: In order: 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 15, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27. Each half has 6 values. The lower half has median (8 + 10) / 2 = 9 (Q1). The upper half has median (20 + 22) / 2 = 21 (Q3). The IQR is 21 - 9 = 12.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: To find the interquartile range of the data 1, 3, 4, 8, 9, 12, a student calculates 12 - 1 = 11. What did the student actually find?
choices: The IQR. The student is correct.
The median. The IQR is 6.
The range. The IQR is 6.
The range. The IQR is 8.
questions.answer: The range. The IQR is 6.
questions.solution: 12 - 1 is the greatest value minus the least value, which is the range. For the IQR: the lower half 1, 3, 4 has median 3 (Q1) and the upper half 8, 9, 12 has median 9 (Q3), so IQR = 9 - 3 = 6.

solve.answer: The range. The IQR is 6.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the data 12, 15, 9, 18 and 6.
questions.solution: The mean is 60 / 5 = 12. The distances from 12 are 0, 3, 3, 6 and 6, which add to 18. The MAD is 18 / 5 = 3.6.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Six friends are 20, 24, 18, 26, 22, 22 years old. Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of their ages.
questions.solution: The mean is 132 / 6 = 22. The distances from 22 are 2, 2, 4, 4, 0 and 0, which add to 12. The MAD is 12 / 6 = 2 years.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: A weather station recorded these temperatures in degrees on eight mornings: 52, 55, 50, 58, 49, 56, 53, 51. Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the temperatures.
questions.solution: The mean is 424 / 8 = 53. The distances from 53 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 4, 3, 0 and 2, which add to 20. The MAD is 20 / 8 = 2.5 degrees.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: The mean absolute deviation of a data set is 0. Which statement must be true?
choices: All of the values are 0.
The mean and the median are both 0.
All of the values are equal.
The values are listed in order.
questions.answer: All of the values are equal.
questions.solution: A MAD of 0 means the average distance from the mean is 0, and distances cannot be negative, so every distance is 0. That happens only when every value equals the mean, so all the values are equal (but not necessarily 0).

solve.answer: All of the values are equal.
solve.work: MAD 0 means every distance from the mean is 0, so all values equal the mean (need not be 0).

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the quiz scores 5, 9, 10, 12 and 14.
questions.solution: The mean is 50 / 5 = 10. The distances from 10 are 5, 1, 0, 2 and 4, which add to 12. The MAD is 12 / 5 = 2.4.

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: A set of test scores has a mean of 80 and a mean absolute deviation (MAD) of 2. Which statement is correct?
choices: Every score is between 78 and 82.
The range of the scores is 2.
The middle score is 2 points above 80.
The scores are typically about 2 points away from 80.
questions.answer: The scores are typically about 2 points away from 80.
questions.solution: A MAD of 2 means the scores are 2 points from the mean on average. Some scores can be farther away, so not every score has to be between 78 and 82, and the MAD is not the range.

solve.answer: The scores are typically about 2 points away from 80.
solve.work: MAD 2 means scores are typically about 2 points from 80; it does not bound every score or give the range.

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: Which of these measures of spread uses every value in the data set?
choices: The mean absolute deviation
The range
The interquartile range
The greatest value
questions.answer: The mean absolute deviation
questions.solution: The MAD finds the distance of every value from the mean. The range uses only the greatest and least values, and the IQR uses only the quartiles. (The greatest value is not a measure of spread.)

solve.answer: The mean absolute deviation
solve.work: MAD averages every value's distance from the mean; range uses only extremes; IQR only quartiles.

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: The times of a group of runners have a mean of 40 seconds and a MAD of 5 seconds. One runner took 47 seconds. How many seconds farther from the mean than the average distance is this runner's time?
questions.solution: This runner is 47 - 40 = 7 seconds from the mean. The average distance is the MAD, 5 seconds. So 7 - 5 = 2 seconds farther than average.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: A data set is 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 15, 16, 48. Which measure of spread is least affected by the value 48?
choices: The range
The interquartile range
The mean absolute deviation
All three are affected equally
questions.answer: The interquartile range
questions.solution: The range jumps to 36 because of the 48, and the mean (18.25) is pulled up, which raises the MAD. The IQR uses only the middle half of the values: Q1 = 13 and Q3 = 15.5, so IQR = 2.5, and it hardly notices the 48.

solve.answer: The interquartile range
solve.work: Q1=(13+13)/2=13, Q3=(15+15)/2=15; IQR does not depend on 48's size. Range and MAD do.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: A coach wants to know how far, on average, her players' sprint times are from the team's mean time. Which measure should she use?
choices: The range
The interquartile range
The mean absolute deviation
The median
questions.answer: The mean absolute deviation
questions.solution: The MAD is, by definition, the average distance of the values from the mean. The range and the IQR describe the spread of the ends and of the middle half, and the median is a measure of center.

solve.answer: The mean absolute deviation
solve.work: Average distance from the mean = MAD.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: For which situation are the median and the interquartile range the better choice to describe the data?
choices: The heights of 25 same-age students, which cluster evenly around the average
The number of minutes a train arrives early or late, which is balanced around zero
The weights of 30 identical bags of rice, which are all very close to the labeled weight
The ages of guests at a party where most are 8 to 12 years old and two are grandparents aged 70
questions.answer: The ages of guests at a party where most are 8 to 12 years old and two are grandparents aged 70
questions.solution: The median and IQR are used when data are skewed or have extreme values. The two grandparents are extreme values that would distort the mean and the MAD. The other three situations are roughly symmetric without extreme values, so the mean and the MAD describe them well.

solve.answer: The ages of guests at a party where most are 8 to 12 years old and two are grandparents aged 70
solve.work: Party ages are skewed by two 70-year-olds: median and IQR resist extremes. Others are symmetric.

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Two machines fill boxes. The weights, in ounces, of five boxes from Machine A are 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, and from Machine B are 22, 23, 24, 25, 26. Both sets have a mean of 24. The MAD of Machine A's weights is how many times the MAD of Machine B's weights?
questions.solution: Machine A: distances from 24 are 6, 3, 0, 3, 6, which add to 18, so MAD = 18 / 5 = 3.6. Machine B: distances are 2, 1, 0, 1, 2, which add to 6, so MAD = 6 / 5 = 1.2. Since 3.6 / 1.2 = 3, A's MAD is 3 times B's MAD.

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Class 1's test scores have a median of 78 and an IQR of 6. Class 2's test scores have a median of 82 and an IQR of 16. Which statement is correct?
choices: Class 2's scores are typically higher, and they vary less.
Class 1's scores are typically higher, and they vary more.
Class 1's scores are typically higher, but they vary less.
Class 2's scores are typically higher, but they vary more.
questions.answer: Class 2's scores are typically higher, but they vary more.
questions.solution: The median of Class 2 (82) is greater than that of Class 1 (78), so its scores are typically higher. The IQR of Class 2 (16) is greater than that of Class 1 (6), so its middle half is more spread out: its scores vary more.

solve.answer: Class 2's scores are typically higher, but they vary more.
solve.work: Class 2 median 82 > 78 (typically higher) and IQR 16 > 6 (varies more).

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Tomato plants in Garden A produced 10, 12, 15, 19, 22, 30 tomatoes. Tomato plants in Garden B produced 14, 16, 17, 20, 21, 23 tomatoes. The IQR of Garden A is how many times the IQR of Garden B?
questions.solution: Garden A in order: Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 22, so IQR = 10. Garden B in order: Q1 = 16 and Q3 = 21, so IQR = 5. Since 10 / 5 = 2, the IQR of A is 2 times the IQR of B.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The mean of five values is 20. A sixth value, 50, is added. What is the mean of all six values?
questions.solution: The five values add to 5 x 20 = 100. With 50 the total is 150. The mean of six values is 150 / 6 = 25. The one extreme value raised the mean by 5. (35 is the mean of 20 and 50, which ignores that there are five values at around 20, and 150 is the total.)

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The median of the data 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 is 7. A sixth value, 100, is added. What is the median of the six values?
questions.solution: The six values in order are 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 100. The median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: (7 + 9) / 2 = 8. Even a value as extreme as 100 moved the median by only 1.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: In the data set 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, the greatest value, 14, is changed to 60. Which statement is true?
choices: The range, the mean and the median all increase.
Only the range increases; the mean stays the same.
The mean and the IQR increase, but the range stays the same.
The range and the mean increase, but the median and the IQR stay the same.
questions.answer: The range and the mean increase, but the median and the IQR stay the same.
questions.solution: The range goes from 14 - 3 = 11 to 60 - 3 = 57, and the mean rises from 68 / 8 = 8.5 to 114 / 8 = 14.25. The median (8 + 9) / 2 = 8.5 and the quartiles (5.5 and 11.5) use only the middle values, so the median and the IQR (6) do not change.

solve.answer: The range and the mean increase, but the median and the IQR stay the same.
solve.work: Before: median (8+9)/2=8.5, Q1=(5+6)/2=5.5, Q3=(11+12)/2=11.5. Changing 14 to 60 leaves median, Q1, Q3 unchanged; range and mean increase.

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: The range of five values is 18. Four of the values are 23, 31, 27 and 35, and the fifth value is the least. What is the fifth value?
questions.solution: The greatest value is 35. The range is 18, so the least value is 35 - 18 = 17. Check: 17 is less than the other four values, and 35 - 17 = 18.

solve.work: Greatest of the five is 35 (fifth is least). Least = 35-18 = 17 (below 23, consistent).

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: A data set has a least value of 8 and a range of 12. A new value is added that is greater than every other value, and the range becomes 20. What is the new value?
questions.solution: The new value is the new greatest value, and the least value is still 8. The range is 20, so the new value is 8 + 20 = 28.

solve.work: Old greatest 8+12=20. New value is new greatest: 8+20 = 28.

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the number of points scored in eight games: 3 points 2 times, 5 points 1 time, 7 points 2 times, 9 points 1 time and 11 points 2 times. What is the interquartile range of the scores?
questions.solution: List all 8 scores in order: 3, 3, 5, 7, 7, 9, 11, 11. The lower half 3, 3, 5, 7 has median (3 + 5) / 2 = 4 (Q1). The upper half 7, 9, 11, 11 has median (9 + 11) / 2 = 10 (Q3). The IQR is 10 - 4 = 6.

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A dot plot has 1 dot at 1, 2 dots at 3, 4 dots at 5, 2 dots at 7 and 1 dot at 9. The mean of the 10 values is 5. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
questions.solution: The distances from 5 are: 4 (one dot), 2 (two dots at 3), 0 (four dots), 2 (two dots at 7) and 4 (one dot). They add to 4 + 2 x 2 + 0 + 2 x 2 + 4 = 16. The MAD is 16 / 10 = 1.6. (2.4 ignores how many dots are at each value, 3.2 divides the 16 by 5 instead of 10, and 16 is the total before dividing.)

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: Plot P has 3 dots at each of 4, 6 and 8. Plot Q has 2 dots at 4, 5 dots at 6 and 2 dots at 8. Both plots have a mean of 6 and a range of 4. Which plot has the greater MAD?
choices: Plot P, because more of its dots are far from the mean.
Plot Q, because it has the tallest stack of dots.
Neither: they have the same MAD, because the mean and the range are the same.
Plot Q, because it has more dots at the mean.
questions.answer: Plot P, because more of its dots are far from the mean.
questions.solution: Plot P: the distances from 6 are 2 (three dots), 0 (three dots) and 2 (three dots), which add to 12, so MAD = 12 / 9 = 4/3. Plot Q: 2 (two dots), 0 (five dots) and 2 (two dots) add to 8, so MAD = 8 / 9. P has the greater MAD. Equal means and ranges do not make equal MADs.

solve.answer: Plot P, because more of its dots are far from the mean.

questions.skill: Effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The value 30 is added to the data set 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Which statement is true?
choices: The median increases a lot, but the range changes only a little
Neither the range nor the median changes
The range increases a lot, but the median changes only a little
The range and the median increase by the same amount
questions.answer: The range increases a lot, but the median changes only a little
questions.solution: Before: the range is $8 - 4 = 4$ and the median is 6. After adding 30 the data are 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 30. The range is $30 - 4 = 26$, an increase of 22. The median is $(6 + 7) \div 2 = 6.5$, an increase of only 0.5.

solve.answer: The range increases a lot, but the median changes only a little
solve.work: Before: range 4, median 6. After: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 30: range 26, median 6.5.

questions.skill: Compare two sets using MAD
questions.stem: Set A is 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Set B is 2, 6, 10, 14, 18. Both sets have a mean of 10. The MAD of Set B is how many times the MAD of Set A?
questions.solution: Set A: the distances from 10 are 4, 2, 0, 2, 4. Their mean is $12 \div 5 = 2.4$. Set B: the distances from 10 are 8, 4, 0, 4, 8. Their mean is $24 \div 5 = 4.8$. Since $4.8 \div 2.4 = 2$, the MAD of B is 2 times the MAD of A.

questions.skill: Compare two sets using IQR
questions.stem: Set X is 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 17. Set Y is 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. How much greater is the interquartile range of Set X than the interquartile range of Set Y?
questions.solution: Set X: the lower half is 3, 5, 6, 8 with first quartile $(5 + 6) \div 2 = 5.5$. The upper half is 9, 12, 14, 17 with third quartile $(12 + 14) \div 2 = 13$. IQR = $13 - 5.5 = 7.5$. Set Y: the lower half is 10, 11, 12, 13 with first quartile 11.5. The upper half is 14, 15, 16, 17 with third quartile 15.5. IQR = $15.5 - 11.5 = 4$. The difference is $7.5 - 4 = 3.5$.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: Set A has a range of 14 and a least value of 6. Set B has a least value of 10 and a greatest value of 31. All the values of both sets are put together. What is the range of the combined values?
questions.solution: The greatest value of Set A is 6 + 14 = 20, which is less than 31. So the combined greatest value is 31 and the combined least value is 6. The range is 31 - 6 = 25.

solve.work: A: least 6, greatest 6+14=20. B: 10 to 31. Combined 6 to 31: 25.

questions.skill: Find the range of a data set
questions.stem: Six values have a range of 9, and their least value is 11. A seventh value, 23, is added. What is the range of the seven values?
questions.solution: The greatest of the six values is 11 + 9 = 20. The new value, 23, is greater than 20, so it is the new greatest value. The range is 23 - 11 = 12.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: Ten students finished a puzzle in the following numbers of seconds: 45, 38, 52, 41, 60, 47, 55, 36, 49, 58. What is the interquartile range of the times?
questions.solution: In order: 36, 38, 41, 45, 47, 49, 52, 55, 58, 60. The lower half 36, 38, 41, 45, 47 has median 41 (Q1). The upper half 49, 52, 55, 58, 60 has median 55 (Q3). The IQR is 55 - 41 = 14.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: The interquartile range of a data set is 12 and its range is 30. The IQR is what fraction of the range?
questions.solution: The fraction is IQR / range = 12 / 30, which simplifies to 2/5. (5/2 turns it upside down, 3/5 is (30 - 12) / 30, and 2/7 is 12 / (30 + 12).)

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: Data Set A has an interquartile range of 10. Data Set B has an interquartile range of 6. Which statement must be true?
choices: The middle half of the values covers a wider interval in Set A than in Set B.
Set A has the greater range.
Set A has the greater median.
Set A has more values than Set B.
questions.answer: The middle half of the values covers a wider interval in Set A than in Set B.
questions.solution: The IQR is the length of the interval holding the middle half of the values, so Set A's middle half is wider. Nothing is known about the extremes (range), the median, or how many values there are.

solve.answer: The middle half of the values covers a wider interval in Set A than in Set B.
solve.work: IQR is the width of the interval holding the middle half; 10 > 6. Median, count and range not determined.

questions.skill: Find the interquartile range
questions.stem: Find the interquartile range of the data set 6, 9, 10, 14, 16, 21, 25, 40. Then remove the least and greatest values, leaving six values, and find the IQR again. By how much does the IQR decrease?
questions.solution: All 8 values: Q1 = (9 + 10) / 2 = 9.5 and Q3 = (21 + 25) / 2 = 23, so IQR = 13.5. The six values 9, 10, 14, 16, 21, 25: Q1 = 10 and Q3 = 21, so IQR = 11. The IQR decreases by 13.5 - 11 = 2.5.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: The temperatures at eight times of a night were $-6$, 2, $-1$, 4, 0, $-2$, 1 and 2 degrees. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the temperatures?
questions.solution: The values add to 0, so the mean is 0. The distances from 0 are 6, 2, 1, 4, 0, 2, 1 and 2, which add to 18. The MAD is 18 / 8 = 2.25 degrees. (0 comes from averaging the signed values, which cancel; 18 is the total distance before dividing; 4.5 divides by 4.)

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: A toy car rolled down a ramp five times, in 1.2, 1.8, 1.5, 2.1 and 1.4 seconds. Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the times, in seconds.
questions.solution: The mean is 8.0 / 5 = 1.6 seconds. The distances from 1.6 are 0.4, 0.2, 0.1, 0.5 and 0.2, which add to 1.4. The MAD is 1.4 / 5 = 0.28 seconds.

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Ten students counted the following numbers of jumps in a minute: 34, 41, 38, 45, 29, 52, 36, 40, 47, 38. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the numbers of jumps?
questions.solution: The values add to 400, so the mean is 40. The distances from 40 are 6, 1, 2, 5, 11, 12, 4, 0, 7 and 2, which add to 50. The MAD is 50 / 10 = 5. (50 is the total distance before dividing, and 40 is the mean.)

questions.skill: Find the mean absolute deviation
questions.stem: Every value in a data set is increased by 10. What happens to the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
choices: It increases by 10.
It is multiplied by 10.
It decreases by 10.
It stays the same.
questions.answer: It stays the same.
questions.solution: Adding 10 to every value also adds 10 to the mean, so every value stays the same distance from the mean. The distances, and so the MAD, do not change. (Example: 2, 4, 6 has mean 4 and MAD 4/3; after adding 10, 12, 14, 16 has mean 14 and the same MAD.)

solve.answer: It stays the same.
solve.work: Shifting all values and the mean by 10 leaves each distance unchanged.

questions.skill: Interpret range, IQR and MAD
questions.stem: Which of these CANNOT be true for a data set?
choices: A range of 10 and a MAD of 3
A range of 20 and a MAD of 2
A range of 6 and a MAD of 9
A range of 8 and a MAD of 4
questions.answer: A range of 6 and a MAD of 9
questions.solution: Every value lies between the least and the greatest value, so no value can be farther from the mean than the range. The average distance (the MAD) cannot be greater than the range. A range of 6 and a MAD of 9 is impossible. (For a range of 8 and a MAD of 4, take 0, 0, 8, 8.)

solve.answer: A range of 6 and a MAD of 9
solve.work: Every distance from the mean is at most the range, so MAD <= range; MAD 9 > range 6 impossible. Range 8, MAD 4 is possible (0,0,8,8); others fine.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: A data set is 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 60, and the value 60 is much greater than the others. Which pair of measures best describes its center and spread?
choices: Mean 9.8 and IQR 3
Median 4.5 and range 58
Median 4.5 and IQR 3
Mean 9.8 and range 58
questions.answer: Median 4.5 and IQR 3
questions.solution: With an extreme value, use the median and the IQR. The median is (4 + 5) / 2 = 4.5. The IQR is 6 - 3 = 3. The mean (9.8) is pulled far above nine of the ten values, and the range (58) is created almost entirely by the 60.

solve.answer: Median 4.5 and IQR 3

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: Which statement about choosing measures for a data set is correct?
choices: Use the mean and the range when the data have extreme values.
Use the mean and the MAD when the data are roughly symmetric with no extreme values.
Use the median and the MAD when the data are symmetric.
Use the mean and the IQR when the data are skewed.
questions.answer: Use the mean and the MAD when the data are roughly symmetric with no extreme values.
questions.solution: Measures are chosen in matching pairs. The mean goes with the MAD for symmetric data without extreme values; the median goes with the IQR for skewed data or data with extreme values. The range is not a good choice when there are extreme values, because they set it.

solve.answer: Use the mean and the MAD when the data are roughly symmetric with no extreme values.
solve.work: Mean & MAD for roughly symmetric data without extremes; median & IQR otherwise.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: The center of the data set 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 55 can be described by its mean or by its median. One value is much greater than the others. Which measure better describes a typical value? Give the value of that measure.
questions.solution: The value 55 is far greater than the others, so the mean (96 / 7, about 13.7) is pulled up and is greater than six of the seven values. The median, the 4th value in order, is 7. Choose the median, 7.

solve.work: Sorted 5,6,6,7,8,9,55; median 7. Mean 96/7 ~ 13.7 pulled by 55. Median 7 better.

questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread
questions.stem: The mean of a data set is much greater than its median. Which is most likely, and which measures would you then choose?
choices: The data are skewed to the high values; use the median and the IQR.
The data are symmetric; use the mean and the MAD.
The data are skewed to the low values; use the mean and the MAD.
The data are skewed to the high values; use the mean and the range.
questions.answer: The data are skewed to the high values; use the median and the IQR.
questions.solution: A few very high values pull the mean above the median, so the data are skewed toward the high values. For such data, the median and the IQR are the better pair, because they are not pulled by those few values.

solve.answer: The data are skewed to the high values; use the median and the IQR.
solve.work: Mean pulled far above median by high values: skewed to the high values (right); use median and IQR.

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Data Set X has a range of 40 and a MAD of 5. Data Set Y has a range of 25 and a MAD of 8. Which statement is correct?
choices: Set X's values are typically farther from their mean, because its range is greater.
Set Y has the greater range, because its MAD is greater.
Set X has the greater range, but Set Y's values are typically farther from their mean.
Set X is more spread out by both the range and the MAD.
questions.answer: Set X has the greater range, but Set Y's values are typically farther from their mean.
questions.solution: Range 40 is greater than 25, so X has the greater range. MAD 8 is greater than 5, so Y's values are typically farther from their mean. X's large range can come from one or two far-away values, while the MAD looks at every value.

solve.answer: Set X has the greater range, but Set Y's values are typically farther from their mean.
solve.work: X range 40 > 25; Y MAD 8 > 5, so Y's values typically farther from their mean.

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Set A is 25, 28, 30, 32, 35. Set B is 18, 24, 30, 36, 42. Both sets have a mean of 30. How much greater is the MAD of Set B than the MAD of Set A?
questions.solution: Set A: distances from 30 are 5, 2, 0, 2, 5, which add to 14, so MAD = 14 / 5 = 2.8. Set B: distances are 12, 6, 0, 6, 12, which add to 36, so MAD = 36 / 5 = 7.2. The difference is 7.2 - 2.8 = 4.4. (7.2 and 2.8 are the two MADs themselves, and 22 is the difference of the totals, 36 - 14, before dividing.)

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Box plot A has a least value of 10, a first quartile of 20, a median of 30, a third quartile of 40 and a greatest value of 50. Box plot B has a least value of 10, a first quartile of 25, a median of 30, a third quartile of 35 and a greatest value of 50. Which statement is correct?
choices: The two plots have the same median and IQR, but Plot A has the greater range.
The two plots have the same median, range and IQR.
The two plots have the same median and range, but Plot A has the greater IQR.
The two plots have the same range and IQR, but Plot A has the greater median.
questions.answer: The two plots have the same median and range, but Plot A has the greater IQR.
questions.solution: Both plots have a median of 30 and a range of 50 - 10 = 40. Plot A has IQR 40 - 20 = 20, and Plot B has IQR 35 - 25 = 10. So A has the greater IQR.

solve.answer: The two plots have the same median and range, but Plot A has the greater IQR.
solve.work: A: median 30, range 40, IQR 20. B: median 30, range 40, IQR 10. Same median and range, A greater IQR.

questions.skill: Compare two data sets using center and spread
questions.stem: Plot R has 2 dots at 3, 6 dots at 5 and 2 dots at 7. Plot S has 4 dots at 3, 2 dots at 5 and 4 dots at 7. Both plots have a mean of 5. The MAD of Plot S is how many times the MAD of Plot R?
questions.solution: Plot R: the distances from 5 are 2 (twice), 0 (six times) and 2 (twice), which add to 8, so MAD = 8 / 10 = 0.8. Plot S: 2 (four times), 0 (twice) and 2 (four times), which add to 16, so MAD = 16 / 10 = 1.6. Since 1.6 / 0.8 = 2, the MAD of S is 2 times the MAD of R.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The mean of six values is 15. When one value is removed, the mean of the remaining five values is 12. What value was removed?
questions.solution: The six values add to 6 x 15 = 90. The remaining five add to 5 x 12 = 60. The removed value was 90 - 60 = 30.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The data set 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 has a mean of 14. The value 18 is replaced by 38, so the new data set is 10, 12, 14, 16, 38. By how much does the mean absolute deviation (MAD) increase?
questions.solution: Original: distances from 14 are 4, 2, 0, 2 and 4, which add to 12, so MAD = 12 / 5 = 2.4. New: the mean is 90 / 5 = 18; distances from 18 are 8, 6, 4, 2 and 20, which add to 40, so MAD = 40 / 5 = 8. The MAD increases by 8 - 2.4 = 5.6.

solve.work: Old: distances 4,2,0,2,4 = 12, MAD 2.4. New 10,12,14,16,38: sum 90, mean 18; distances 8,6,4,2,20 = 40, MAD 8. Increase 8-2.4 = 5.6.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The data set 2, 4, 6, 8 has a mean of 5 and a MAD of 2. A fifth value, 5, equal to the mean, is added. What happens?
choices: The mean stays 5, and the MAD decreases to 1.6.
The mean stays 5, and the MAD stays 2.
The mean decreases, and the MAD decreases.
The mean stays 5, and the MAD increases.
questions.answer: The mean stays 5, and the MAD decreases to 1.6.
questions.solution: The five values add to 25, so the mean is still 5. The new value is 0 away from the mean, so the distances still add to 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 + 0 = 8, but they are now shared among 5 values: 8 / 5 = 1.6, which is less than 2.

solve.answer: The mean stays 5, and the MAD decreases to 1.6.

questions.skill: Describe the effect of an extreme value
questions.stem: The data set 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 has an IQR of 6. Two extreme values, 50 and 60, are added. By how much does the IQR increase?
questions.solution: With 8 values in order: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 50, 60, the lower half 4, 6, 8, 10 has median 7 (Q1) and the upper half 12, 14, 50, 60 has median (14 + 50) / 2 = 32 (Q3). The IQR is 32 - 7 = 25. It increases by 25 - 6 = 19. (Two extreme values are enough to move the quartiles.)

solve.issues: Arithmetic is sound (19), but adding two extremes to six values moves Q3 a lot, which cuts against the usual 'IQR resists extreme values' lesson this standard teaches; worth checking the key is 19, not a smaller intended value.

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: The six values 4, 7, 10, 14, e, 25 are in order and have an interquartile range of 12. What is the value of e?
questions.solution: The lower half 4, 7, 10 has median 7, so Q1 = 7. The upper half is 14, e, 25, whose median is e, so Q3 = e. The IQR is e - 7 = 12, so e = 19. Check: 14 < 19 < 25. (22 would come from Q1 = 10, 16 from Q1 = 4, and 5 from 12 - 7.)

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: The five values 12, 15, 18, 21 and x have a mean of 18. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the five values?
questions.solution: The five values add to 5 x 18 = 90, so x = 90 - (12 + 15 + 18 + 21) = 24. The distances from 18 are 6, 3, 0, 3 and 6, which add to 18. The MAD is 18 / 5 = 3.6.

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: A data set has a range of 24, and its greatest value is 3 times its least value. All the values are positive. What is the least value?
questions.solution: Let the least value be L. The greatest is 3L, so the range is 3L - L = 2L = 24, and L = 12. Check: the greatest value is 36, and 36 - 12 = 24.

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: A data set has a range of 30. After 4 is added to every value, the greatest value is 52. What was the least value before 4 was added?
questions.solution: Adding 4 to every value does not change the range, which is still 30. Before adding, the greatest value was 52 - 4 = 48. So the least value was 48 - 30 = 18. (22 forgets to take off the 4, 26 adds the 4 instead, and 14 takes it off twice.)

solve.work: Range unchanged by +4. Original greatest 52-4 = 48; least 48-30 = 18.

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A table shows the number of minutes 10 students spent on a project: 20 minutes for 3 students, 25 minutes for 2 students, 30 minutes for 1 student and 35 minutes for 4 students. Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the times.
questions.solution: The total is 3 x 20 + 2 x 25 + 30 + 4 x 35 = 280, so the mean is 280 / 10 = 28. The distances from 28 are 8 (three students), 3 (two students), 2 (one student) and 7 (four students). They add to 24 + 6 + 2 + 28 = 60. The MAD is 60 / 10 = 6 minutes.

questions.skill: Find a missing value from a measure
questions.stem: Eight values in order are 3, 5, 8, 10, 14, $x$, 22 and 26. The interquartile range is 12. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: The lower half is 3, 5, 8, 10, so the first quartile is $(5 + 8) \div 2 = 6.5$. The IQR is 12, so the third quartile is $6.5 + 12 = 18.5$. The upper half is 14, $x$, 22, 26, so the third quartile is $(x + 22) \div 2 = 18.5$. Then $x + 22 = 37$ and $x = 15$.

solve.work: Lower half 3,5,8,10: Q1=6.5. IQR 12 gives Q3=18.5 = median of upper half 14, x, 22, 26 = (x+22)/2 when 14<=x<=22. x+22=37, x=15 (in range).

questions.skill: Find a measure from a frequency table or dot plot
questions.stem: A team played 12 games. It scored 0 goals in 3 games, 1 goal in 4 games, 2 goals in 2 games, 3 goals in 1 game and 5 goals in 2 games. What is the interquartile range of the number of goals per game?
questions.solution: In order the 12 numbers of goals are 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 5, 5. The lower half is 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, so the first quartile is $(0 + 1) \div 2 = 0.5$. The upper half is 1, 2, 2, 3, 5, 5, so the third quartile is $(2 + 3) \div 2 = 2.5$. The IQR is $2.5 - 0.5 = 2$.

questions.skill: Compare two groups by their medians
questions.stem: The median reading time of Group A is 24 minutes and the median reading time of Group B is 30 minutes. Which statement is best supported by these medians?
choices: A typical student in Group B read longer than a typical student in Group A
Every student in Group B read longer than every student in Group A
A typical student in Group A read longer than a typical student in Group B
Both groups read for about the same amount of time
questions.answer: A typical student in Group B read longer than a typical student in Group A
questions.solution: The median describes a typical value. Group B's median is greater, so a typical student in Group B read longer. The medians do not tell us that every student in B read longer than every student in A.

solve.answer: A typical student in Group B read longer than a typical student in Group A
solve.work: Median B 30 > median A 24, so a typical B student read longer. Medians say nothing about every student.

questions.skill: Compare two groups by their means
questions.stem: Group A read for 20, 25, 30 and 35 minutes. Group B read for 12, 14, 18 and 22 minutes. How many more minutes did Group A read than Group B, on average (using the mean)?
questions.solution: Mean of A: $110 \div 4 = 27.5$ minutes. Mean of B: $66 \div 4 = 16.5$ minutes. The difference is $27.5 - 16.5 = 11$ minutes.

questions.skill: Plan an investigation of two groups
questions.stem: A student wants to compare how many books sixth graders and seventh graders read in a month. Which plan is best?
choices: Ask 20 students who are checking out books at the library
Ask 20 sixth graders and 20 seventh graders, each chosen at random, how many books they read this month
Ask 20 seventh graders and use the answers for both grades
Ask 20 sixth graders and 20 seventh graders which grade reads more
questions.answer: Ask 20 sixth graders and 20 seventh graders, each chosen at random, how many books they read this month
questions.solution: To compare two groups we need numerical data from a random sample of each group. Library visitors are likely to read more than other students, using only one grade says nothing about the other, and asking which grade reads more gathers opinions instead of counts.

solve.answer: Ask 20 sixth graders and 20 seventh graders, each chosen at random, how many books they read this month
solve.work: Random samples from both groups, asking the numeric question, is the sound comparison.

questions.skill: Compare the means of two groups
questions.stem: On four days, Rosa walked 3, 5, 4 and 4 kilometers. On the same four days, Eli walked 2, 3, 3 and 4 kilometers. How many kilometers greater is Rosa's mean daily distance than Eli's mean daily distance?
questions.solution: Rosa's mean is (3 + 5 + 4 + 4) divided by 4, which is 4. Eli's mean is (2 + 3 + 3 + 4) divided by 4, which is 3. The difference is 4 - 3 = 1 kilometer.

questions.skill: Compare the means of two groups
questions.stem: Each of two teams played 5 games. Team A scored a mean of 18 points per game and Team B scored a mean of 14 points per game. How many more points did Team A score than Team B in all 5 games?
questions.solution: A mean of 18 over 5 games means 5 x 18 = 90 points in all for Team A. Team B scored 5 x 14 = 70 points. The difference is 90 - 70 = 20 points.

solve.work: Team A total 18*5=90; Team B total 14*5=70; 90-70=20.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two groups
questions.stem: Seven students in Room 1 own 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3 and 5 pets. Seven students in Room 2 own 1, 2, 2, 4, 4, 5 and 6 pets. (Both lists are in order.) How many more pets does the median student in Room 2 own than the median student in Room 1?
questions.solution: With 7 values the median is the 4th one. Room 1: the 4th value is 2. Room 2: the 4th value is 4. The difference is 4 - 2 = 2.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two groups
questions.stem: Lila's group has the values 3, 5, 6, 9 and 12. Marco's group has the values 2, 7, 8, 10 and 11. (Both lists are in order.) What are the medians of the two groups?
choices: Lila: 6, Marco: 8
Lila: 7, Marco: 7.6
Lila: 5, Marco: 7
Lila: 12, Marco: 11
questions.answer: Lila: 6, Marco: 8
questions.solution: With 5 values in order, the median is the middle (3rd) value: 6 for Lila and 8 for Marco. (7 and 7.6 are the means, 5 and 7 are the 2nd values, and 12 and 11 are the greatest values.)

solve.answer: Lila: 6, Marco: 8
solve.work: Lila middle (3rd) value 6; Marco middle value 8.

questions.skill: Compare the ranges of two groups
questions.stem: Over a season, Team X scored as few as 10 points and as many as 30 points in a game. Team Y scored as few as 12 points and as many as 22 points. How much greater is the range of Team X's scores than the range of Team Y's scores?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value. Team X: 30 - 10 = 20. Team Y: 22 - 12 = 10. The range of Team X is 20 - 10 = 10 points greater.

questions.skill: Compare the ranges of two groups
questions.stem: Group A has the values 5, 9, 12 and 20. Group B has the values 7, 10, 11 and 13. Which group has the greater range?
choices: Group B, whose range is 13
Group A, whose range is 15
Group A, whose range is 20
Group B, whose range is 6
questions.answer: Group A, whose range is 15
questions.solution: Range = greatest value - least value. Group A: 20 - 5 = 15. Group B: 13 - 7 = 6. Group A has the greater range, 15. (13 and 20 are greatest values, not ranges, and 6 is the range of the other group.)

solve.answer: Group A, whose range is 15
solve.work: A range 20-5=15; B range 13-7=6. A greater, range 15.

questions.skill: Compare the IQRs of two groups
questions.stem: Group 1 has a first quartile of 12 and a third quartile of 20. Group 2 has a first quartile of 14 and a third quartile of 18. How much greater is the IQR of Group 1 than the IQR of Group 2?
questions.solution: The IQR is the third quartile minus the first quartile. Group 1: 20 - 12 = 8. Group 2: 18 - 14 = 4. The IQR of Group 1 is 8 - 4 = 4 greater.

questions.skill: Compare the IQRs of two groups
questions.stem: Group A has an IQR of 6 and Group B has an IQR of 11. Which statement must be true?
choices: The middle half of Group A's values is more spread out than the middle half of Group B's
The median of Group B is 5 greater than the median of Group A
Group B has 5 more values than Group A
The middle half of Group B's values is more spread out than the middle half of Group A's
questions.answer: The middle half of Group B's values is more spread out than the middle half of Group A's
questions.solution: The IQR measures how spread out the middle half of the data is. A larger IQR means more spread, so the middle half of Group B (IQR 11) is more spread out than that of Group A (IQR 6). The IQR says nothing about the medians or the number of values.

solve.answer: The middle half of Group B's values is more spread out than the middle half of Group A's
solve.work: IQR measures the spread of the middle half; 11>6 so B's middle half is more spread. Says nothing about count or median.

questions.skill: Compare the mean absolute deviations of two groups
questions.stem: The values 7, 9, 11 and 13 have a mean of 10. What is their mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
questions.solution: The distances from the mean of 10 are 3, 1, 1 and 3. The MAD is the mean of these distances: (3 + 1 + 1 + 3) / 4 = 8 / 4 = 2.

questions.skill: Compare the mean absolute deviations of two groups
questions.stem: What does the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of a data set tell you?
choices: How far the values are from the mean, on average
The value in the middle of the data
The difference between the greatest and least values
How many values are in the data set
questions.answer: How far the values are from the mean, on average
questions.solution: The MAD is the mean of the distances between each value and the mean, so it describes how spread out the values are around the mean. The middle value is the median, and the difference between the greatest and least values is the range.

solve.answer: How far the values are from the mean, on average
solve.work: MAD is the mean of the distances from the mean.

questions.skill: Describe the centre and spread together
questions.stem: Ana scored 10, 10, 10 and 10 points in four games. Ben scored 2, 8, 12 and 18 points in four games. Which statement is true?
choices: The means are equal, but Ana's scores vary more than Ben's
Ana's mean is greater, because she never scored below 10
Ben's mean is greater, because he scored 18 in one game
The means are equal, but Ben's scores vary more than Ana's
questions.answer: The means are equal, but Ben's scores vary more than Ana's
questions.solution: Both means are 40 / 4 = 10. Ana scored exactly 10 every game, so her scores do not vary at all. Ben's scores range from 2 to 18, so they vary much more.

solve.answer: The means are equal, but Ben's scores vary more than Ana's
solve.work: Ana mean 10; Ben 2+8+12+18=40, mean 10. Equal means; Ben's vary more (Ana's not at all).

questions.skill: Describe the centre and spread together
questions.stem: Class 1 has a median of 70 and an IQR of 8. Class 2 has a median of 75 and an IQR of 8. Which statement is true?
choices: Class 1 has the higher median, and the spread of the middle half is the same
Class 2 has the higher median, and the spread of the middle half is the same
Class 2 has the higher median, and its middle half is more spread out
The classes have the same median, but different spreads
questions.answer: Class 2 has the higher median, and the spread of the middle half is the same
questions.solution: Class 2's median (75) is higher than Class 1's (70). The IQRs are both 8, so the middle halves are equally spread out.

solve.answer: Class 2 has the higher median, and the spread of the middle half is the same
solve.work: 75>70 so Class 2 higher median; IQRs both 8, same middle-half spread.

questions.skill: Compare a difference in centres with the variability
questions.stem: Two groups each have a MAD of 5. The mean of one group is 20 and the mean of the other is 30. How many MADs apart are the two means?
questions.solution: The means are 30 - 20 = 10 apart. Each MAD is 5, so the means are 10 / 5 = 2 MADs apart.

questions.skill: Choose the better measure of centre
questions.stem: Five houses on Oak Street cost 150, 155, 160, 165 and 900 thousand dollars. Which measure better describes the price of a typical house on this street?
choices: The mean, because it uses every value, so it is always the best choice
The range, because it shows how far apart the prices are
The greatest price, because it is the most important
The median, because one very high price pulls the mean far above the others
questions.answer: The median, because one very high price pulls the mean far above the others
