questions.solution: The median is 160 thousand dollars, which is close to four of the five prices. The mean is 306 thousand dollars, which is pulled far up by the one house that costs 900 thousand and is higher than four of the five prices. So the median describes a typical house better.

solve.answer: The median, because one very high price pulls the mean far above the others
solve.work: Mean = 1530/5 = 306, far above four of five prices; median 160 is typical.

questions.skill: Choose the better measure of centre
questions.stem: The weights of five backpacks, in pounds, are 8, 9, 9, 10 and 24. Because 24 is much heavier than the rest, the median describes a typical backpack better than the mean does. What is the median weight?
questions.solution: The weights are already in order, and the middle (3rd) one is 9 pounds. The mean would be 60 / 5 = 12 pounds, which is higher than 4 of the 5 backpacks.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier on the mean and median
questions.stem: The five values 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10 have a median of 7. The 10 is changed to 100. What is the new median?
questions.solution: In order the values are now 4, 6, 7, 9, 100. The middle (3rd) value is still 7. Changing the greatest value does not change the median.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a distribution
questions.stem: Test scores: 70, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 79, 20. Which statement describes the score of 20?
choices: It is the median of the scores
It is an outlier, far below the other scores
It is in the cluster where most scores are
It is the score that occurs most often
questions.answer: It is an outlier, far below the other scores
questions.solution: Eight of the nine scores are between 70 and 79, forming a cluster. The score of 20 is far from that cluster, so it is an outlier. It is not the median (the median is 74) and it occurs only once.

solve.answer: It is an outlier, far below the other scores
solve.work: All other scores are 70-79; 20 is far below them: an outlier. No mode; median is 74.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a distribution
questions.stem: The data are 3, 10, 11, 12, 12, 13, 14, 30. Most of the values form a cluster from 10 to 14. How many values are in this cluster?
questions.solution: The values from 10 to 14 are 10, 11, 12, 12, 13 and 14, which is 6 values. The values 3 and 30 are outside the cluster.

questions.skill: Compare the share of each group above a cutoff
questions.stem: At the Lakeside club, 6 of the 8 members ran more than 5 kilometers. What percent of the members ran more than 5 kilometers?
questions.solution: 6 out of 8 is 6 / 8 = 0.75, which is 75 percent.

solve.issues: Weakly aligned: a one-group percent (6.RP-level) with no comparison; serves only as a step toward comparing groups.

questions.skill: Compare the share of each group above a cutoff
questions.stem: Of the 10 players on Team A, 7 scored at least 12 points. Of the 20 players on Team B, 10 scored at least 12 points. How many percentage points greater is the percent of Team A players who scored at least 12 than the percent of Team B players who did?
questions.solution: Team A: 7 of 10 is 70 percent. Team B: 10 of 20 is 50 percent. The difference is 70 - 50 = 20 percentage points.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: A survey of 10 students in Class 1 and 10 students in Class 2 found a mean of 2 hours of screen time a day in Class 1 and 3 hours in Class 2. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Every student in Class 2 spent more time on screens than every student in Class 1
Class 2 students have more homework, which is why they use screens more
In these two samples, the Class 2 students spent more time on screens on average
Students in every class at the school use screens for about 3 hours a day
questions.answer: In these two samples, the Class 2 students spent more time on screens on average
questions.solution: The means describe the students surveyed: 3 hours compared with 2 hours. That supports a statement about averages in these samples only. It does not say that every student differs, why the difference exists, or what students in other classes do.

solve.answer: In these two samples, the Class 2 students spent more time on screens on average
solve.work: Data only support that in these samples Class 2's mean is higher; not every student, not the whole school, not causes.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: In a sample, the students who ate breakfast had a mean test score of 84 and the students who skipped breakfast had a mean test score of 78. Which conclusion is best supported by this data alone?
choices: Eating breakfast makes students score 6 points higher
Every student who ate breakfast scored above 78
Skipping breakfast lowers a student's score
The students who ate breakfast scored higher on average in this sample
questions.answer: The students who ate breakfast scored higher on average in this sample
questions.solution: The data show only that the mean score of the breakfast group (84) was higher than the mean of the other group (78). They do not show that breakfast caused the difference, and a mean says nothing about every individual student.

solve.answer: The students who ate breakfast scored higher on average in this sample
solve.work: Observational data: only a description of averages in the sample is supported; no causation, no claim about every student.

questions.skill: Communicate a comparison in words
questions.stem: The median homework time of Class A is 24 minutes and its IQR is 4 minutes. The median homework time of Class B is 20 minutes and its IQR is 4 minutes. Which sentence reports the comparison correctly?
choices: Class B's median is 4 minutes longer than Class A's, and the IQRs are equal
Class A's median is 4 minutes longer than Class B's, and Class A varies more
Class A's median is 4 minutes longer, so every student in Class A worked longer
Class A's median is 4 minutes longer than Class B's, and the IQRs are equal
questions.answer: Class A's median is 4 minutes longer than Class B's, and the IQRs are equal
questions.solution: 24 - 20 = 4, so Class A's median is 4 minutes longer. Both IQRs are 4, so the spread is equal. A median does not tell us about every student.

solve.answer: Class A's median is 4 minutes longer than Class B's, and the IQRs are equal

questions.skill: Communicate a comparison in words
questions.stem: The boys' mean long jump was 156 cm and the girls' mean long jump was 150 cm. Which sentence reports this correctly?
choices: The boys' mean jump (156 cm) was 6 cm longer than the girls' mean jump (150 cm)
The girls' mean jump (150 cm) was 6 cm longer than the boys' mean jump (156 cm)
The boys' mean jump (156 cm) was 12 cm longer than the girls' mean jump (150 cm)
The boys' median jump (156 cm) was 6 cm longer than the girls' median jump (150 cm)
questions.answer: The boys' mean jump (156 cm) was 6 cm longer than the girls' mean jump (150 cm)
questions.solution: 156 - 150 = 6, so the boys' mean was 6 cm longer. The sentence must name the mean, because the data give means, not medians.

solve.answer: The boys' mean jump (156 cm) was 6 cm longer than the girls' mean jump (150 cm)
solve.work: 156-150=6, boys' mean longer; the figures are means, not medians.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and sample size
questions.stem: A student wants to compare the lunch preferences of sixth graders and eighth graders at her school. Which is the best way to choose the students to ask?
choices: Choose students at random from each grade's list
Ask only her friends in each grade
Ask only the students in her own class
Ask the first five students to arrive each morning in each grade
questions.answer: Choose students at random from each grade's list
questions.solution: A random sample gives every student in the grade an equal chance of being asked, so it is likely to represent the whole grade. Friends, classmates or early arrivers may all differ from the rest of the grade.

solve.answer: Choose students at random from each grade's list
solve.work: A random sample from each grade's list is representative; the others are convenience samples.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and sample size
questions.stem: Which plan will give the most trustworthy comparison of the number of hours that sixth graders and eighth graders sleep?
choices: Asking 3 students in each grade
Asking 30 students in grade 6 but only 3 in grade 8
Asking 30 randomly chosen students in each grade
Asking 30 students who are all on one sports team
questions.answer: Asking 30 randomly chosen students in each grade
questions.solution: A larger random sample from each grade is more likely to represent that grade. Three students may not be typical, an unbalanced plan treats the grades unequally, and one team may sleep differently from other students.

solve.answer: Asking 30 randomly chosen students in each grade
solve.work: Large, equal, random samples from each grade give the fairest comparison.

questions.skill: Reflect on the question and the method
questions.stem: Which question can be answered by collecting and comparing data from two groups?
choices: How many hours did Mia sleep last night?
Do seventh graders at Oak Middle sleep more hours than sixth graders there?
How many students are in the seventh grade?
What time does Oak Middle start?
questions.answer: Do seventh graders at Oak Middle sleep more hours than sixth graders there?
questions.solution: A question that compares two groups expects different answers from different people, so it needs data from many students in each group. The other questions each have a single answer.

solve.answer: Do seventh graders at Oak Middle sleep more hours than sixth graders there?
solve.work: Only the 7th vs 6th grade sleep question involves two groups and variable data.

questions.skill: Use samples to compare two populations
questions.stem: A random sample of 10 seventh graders had a mean of 40 minutes of homework a night. A random sample of 10 eighth graders had a mean of 55 minutes. Based on these samples, how many more minutes of homework a night does the average eighth grader do than the average seventh grader?
questions.solution: The sample means estimate the means of the whole grades. The estimated difference is 55 - 40 = 15 minutes.

questions.skill: Use samples to compare two populations
questions.stem: A random sample of 25 people from Town A had a mean age of 34 years. A random sample of 25 people from Town B had a mean age of 41 years. By how many years is the mean age of the Town B sample greater than that of the Town A sample?
questions.solution: Subtract the two sample means: $41 - 34 = 7$ years. This is the difference the samples suggest between the two towns.

questions.skill: Use samples to compare two populations
questions.stem: A researcher compares two towns by taking a sample of people from each one. Why should each sample be chosen at random?
choices: So that the two samples have exactly the same mean
So that each sample is likely to represent its own town fairly
So that the two towns have the same number of people
So that the survey does not need any questions
questions.answer: So that each sample is likely to represent its own town fairly
questions.solution: A random sample gives every person in a town a fair chance of being chosen, so the sample is likely to represent that town. Random choice does not make the samples equal, does not change the towns, and does not remove the need for questions.

solve.answer: So that each sample is likely to represent its own town fairly
solve.work: Random selection makes a sample likely to be representative of its population.

questions.skill: Describe centre and spread together
questions.stem: Group A has a median score of 78 and an IQR of 6. Group B has a median score of 78 and an IQR of 18. Which statement is correct?
choices: Group B scored higher, since its IQR is greater
The typical scores are about the same, but A's scores vary more
The typical scores are about the same, but B's scores vary more
Group A's typical score is lower, since its IQR is smaller
questions.answer: The typical scores are about the same, but B's scores vary more
questions.solution: The medians are equal, so the typical scores are the same. The IQR measures spread, and B's IQR is greater, so B's scores vary more. A greater IQR does not mean a higher score.

solve.answer: The typical scores are about the same, but B's scores vary more
solve.work: Same medians, so typical scores alike; B's IQR 18 > 6, so B varies more.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two groups
questions.stem: Group A traveled to school for 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 minutes. Group B traveled for 5, 10, 12, 15 and 20 minutes. How many more minutes is the median travel time of Group A than the median of Group B?
questions.solution: Both lists are in order. The middle value of A is 20 and the middle value of B is 12. The difference is $20 - 12 = 8$ minutes.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: A teacher compares quiz scores of the 15 students in her morning class with the 15 in her afternoon class. The afternoon class had the higher mean. Which conclusion is best supported by this data?
choices: Afternoon classes make students learn more
Every student scores higher in the afternoon
Every afternoon student scored higher than every morning student
The 15 afternoon students scored higher on this quiz, on average
questions.answer: The 15 afternoon students scored higher on this quiz, on average
questions.solution: The data show only that the mean score of these 15 afternoon students was higher. They do not show that the time of day caused the difference, that it holds for every student, or that every individual score was higher.

solve.answer: The 15 afternoon students scored higher on this quiz, on average
solve.work: A higher mean supports only that these afternoon students scored higher on average on this quiz; no causal or every-student claim.

questions.skill: Compare the means of two groups
questions.stem: Five students at Maple School sent 12, 18, 9, 21 and 15 text messages in one day. Five students at Pine School sent 20, 14, 26, 17 and 18. How many more messages did a Pine student send than a Maple student, on average?

questions.skill: Compare the means of two groups
questions.stem: Class A has 20 students and a mean of 14 books read per student. Class B has 25 students and a mean of 12 books read per student. Which statement is true?
choices: Class A read more books altogether, because its mean is higher
The two classes read the same number of books altogether
Class A read 20 more books altogether than Class B
Class B read more books altogether, even though its mean is lower
questions.answer: Class B read more books altogether, even though its mean is lower
questions.solution: Class A read 20 x 14 = 280 books altogether. Class B read 25 x 12 = 300 books altogether. So Class B read 20 more books in total, even though its mean is lower, because it has more students.

solve.answer: Class B read more books altogether, even though its mean is lower
solve.work: A: 20*14=280 books. B: 25*12=300 books. B read 20 more despite the lower mean.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two groups
questions.stem: Eight students in Class 1 ran 100 meters in these times, in seconds: 16, 14, 18, 15, 20, 15, 17, 18. Eight students in Class 2 ran it in 19, 13, 15, 17, 14, 19, 15, 16 seconds. How many seconds greater is the median time of Class 1 than the median time of Class 2?
questions.solution: Put each list in order. Class 1: 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 18, 18, 20; the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th values, (16 + 17) / 2 = 16.5. Class 2: 13, 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 19, 19; the median is (15 + 16) / 2 = 15.5. The difference is 16.5 - 15.5 = 1 second.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two groups
questions.stem: Group A has the values 2, 3, 3, 4, 28. Group B has the values 5, 6, 6, 7, 9. Which statement is true?
choices: Group A has the greater mean and the greater median
Group B has the greater mean, but Group A has the greater median
Group A has the greater mean, but Group B has the greater median
Group B has the greater mean and the greater median
questions.answer: Group A has the greater mean, but Group B has the greater median
questions.solution: Group A: the mean is 40 / 5 = 8 and the median (middle value) is 3. Group B: the mean is 33 / 5 = 6.6 and the median is 6. So A has the greater mean (8 compared with 6.6), but B has the greater median (6 compared with 3). The very large value 28 pulls Group A's mean up.

solve.answer: Group A has the greater mean, but Group B has the greater median
solve.work: A: sum 40, mean 8, median 3. B: sum 33, mean 6.6, median 6. A greater mean, B greater median.

questions.skill: Compare the ranges of two groups
questions.stem: The daily high temperatures, in degrees, one week in March were 61, 65, 70, 68, 72, 63 and 66. One week in April they were 55, 63, 71, 75, 80, 58 and 69. By how many degrees is the range of the April temperatures greater than the range of the March temperatures?
questions.solution: March: greatest 72, least 61, so the range is 72 - 61 = 11. April: greatest 80, least 55, so the range is 80 - 55 = 25. The difference is 25 - 11 = 14 degrees.

solve.work: March: max 72, min 61, range 11. April: max 80, min 55, range 25. 25-11=14.

questions.skill: Compare the ranges of two groups
questions.stem: Group A has the values 20, 21, 22, 23, 24. Group B has the values 10, 21, 22, 23, 34. Which statement is true?
choices: The groups have the same mean and median, but Group A has the greater range
Group B has the greater mean and the greater range
The groups have the same mean and median, but Group B has the greater range
The groups have the same mean, median and range
questions.answer: The groups have the same mean and median, but Group B has the greater range
questions.solution: Both groups have a mean of 110 / 5 = 22 and a median of 22. The range of Group A is 24 - 20 = 4. The range of Group B is 34 - 10 = 24. So the centres are the same but Group B is far more spread out.

solve.answer: The groups have the same mean and median, but Group B has the greater range
solve.work: A: mean 110/5=22, median 22, range 4. B: sum 110, mean 22, median 22, range 24. Same mean and median, B greater range.

questions.skill: Compare the IQRs of two groups
questions.stem: Both lists have 8 values and are in order. Group X: 2, 5, 7, 9, 10, 13, 15, 20. Group Y: 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 17. The first quartile is the median of the lower 4 values and the third quartile is the median of the upper 4 values. How much greater is the IQR of Group X than the IQR of Group Y?
questions.solution: Group X: lower half 2, 5, 7, 9 has median (5 + 7) / 2 = 6; upper half 10, 13, 15, 20 has median (13 + 15) / 2 = 14; IQR = 14 - 6 = 8. Group Y: lower half 7, 8, 10, 11 has median (8 + 10) / 2 = 9; upper half 13, 14, 16, 17 has median (14 + 16) / 2 = 15; IQR = 15 - 9 = 6. The difference is 8 - 6 = 2.

questions.skill: Compare the IQRs of two groups
questions.stem: Group A: least value 10, first quartile 20, median 30, third quartile 40, greatest value 70. Group B: least value 5, first quartile 25, median 30, third quartile 35, greatest value 75. Which statement is true?
choices: Group B has the greater IQR, but Group A has the greater range
Group A has the greater IQR, but Group B has the greater range
Group A has the greater IQR and the greater range
Group B has the greater IQR and the greater range
questions.answer: Group A has the greater IQR, but Group B has the greater range
questions.solution: Group A: IQR = 40 - 20 = 20 and range = 70 - 10 = 60. Group B: IQR = 35 - 25 = 10 and range = 75 - 5 = 70. So A has the greater IQR (20 compared with 10), but B has the greater range (70 compared with 60).

solve.answer: Group A has the greater IQR, but Group B has the greater range
solve.work: A: IQR 40-20=20, range 70-10=60. B: IQR 35-25=10, range 75-5=70. A greater IQR, B greater range.

questions.skill: Compare the mean absolute deviations of two groups
questions.stem: Team 1 scored 12, 14, 16 and 18 points in four games. Team 2 scored 10, 13, 17 and 20 points in four games. By how many points is the MAD of Team 2 greater than the MAD of Team 1?
questions.solution: Both teams have a mean of 60 / 4 = 15. Team 1 distances from 15: 3, 1, 1, 3, so the MAD is 8 / 4 = 2. Team 2 distances from 15: 5, 2, 2, 5, so the MAD is 14 / 4 = 3.5. The difference is 3.5 - 2 = 1.5 points.

solve.work: Team 1 mean 60/4=15; deviations 3,1,1,3 =8; MAD 2. Team 2 mean 60/4=15; deviations 5,2,2,5 =14; MAD 3.5. 3.5-2=1.5.

questions.skill: Compare the mean absolute deviations of two groups
questions.stem: Group 1 has the values 18, 19, 20, 21, 22. Group 2 has the values 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Both groups have a mean of 20. Which group has the smaller MAD?
choices: Group 2, because its values are closer to the mean on average
Neither, because the groups have the same mean, so their MADs are equal
Group 1, because its values are closer to the mean on average
Group 2, because its data have the greater range
questions.answer: Group 1, because its values are closer to the mean on average
questions.solution: Group 1 distances from 20: 2, 1, 0, 1, 2, so the MAD is 6 / 5 = 1.2. Group 2 distances from 20: 10, 5, 0, 5, 10, so the MAD is 30 / 5 = 6. Group 1 has the smaller MAD because its values sit closer to the mean. Equal means do not mean equal MADs.

solve.answer: Group 1, because its values are closer to the mean on average
solve.work: Group 1 deviations 2,1,0,1,2 -> MAD 1.2; Group 2 deviations 10,5,0,5,10 -> MAD 6. Group 1 smaller.

questions.skill: Describe the centre and spread together
questions.stem: Team X has a mean of 24 points and a MAD of 2. Team Y has a mean of 30 points and a MAD of 8. Which statement is true?
choices: Team X scores more on average, and its scores are less consistent
Team Y scores more on average, and its scores are more consistent
Team Y scores more on average, but its scores are less consistent
Team X scores more on average, but its scores are less consistent
questions.answer: Team Y scores more on average, but its scores are less consistent
questions.solution: Team Y's mean (30) is higher than Team X's (24), so Y scores more on average. A larger MAD means the scores are more spread out around the mean. Y's MAD (8) is larger than X's (2), so Y is less consistent.

solve.answer: Team Y scores more on average, but its scores are less consistent
solve.work: Y mean 30 > 24; Y MAD 8 > 2, so Y is less consistent.

questions.skill: Describe the centre and spread together
questions.stem: Store A has a mean of 80 customers a day and a MAD of 5. Store B has a mean of 80 customers a day and a MAD of 20. A manager plans staff by how predictable the daily customers are. Which store is more predictable, and why?
choices: Store B, because its MAD is larger
Store A, because its mean is smaller
Neither, because the means are equal
Store A, because its MAD is smaller
questions.answer: Store A, because its MAD is smaller
questions.solution: The means are the same, so the means cannot tell the stores apart. The MAD tells how far the daily numbers usually are from 80. Store A's MAD of 5 is much smaller than Store B's MAD of 20, so Store A's daily customers stay closer to 80 and are more predictable.

solve.answer: Store A, because its MAD is smaller
solve.work: Equal means; smaller MAD (5) means daily counts stay closer to 80, so Store A is more predictable.

questions.skill: Compare a difference in centres with the variability
questions.stem: The medians of two groups are 45 and 60. Each group has an IQR of 10. The medians are how many IQRs apart?
questions.solution: The medians are 60 - 45 = 15 apart. One IQR is 10, so they are 15 / 10 = 1.5 IQRs apart.

questions.skill: Compare a difference in centres with the variability
questions.stem: Group X has a mean of 40 and Group Y has a mean of 43. Each group has a MAD of 6. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Group Y is clearly better, because its mean is higher
The means are only half a MAD apart, so the groups overlap a lot
Group X is clearly better, because its MAD is smaller
The means are 6 MADs apart, so the groups barely overlap
questions.answer: The means are only half a MAD apart, so the groups overlap a lot
questions.solution: The means differ by 3, and the MAD is 6, so they are 3 / 6 = 0.5 MAD apart. That difference is small compared with how much the values vary within each group, so the two groups overlap a lot and a difference of 3 does not show that one group is clearly higher.

solve.answer: The means are only half a MAD apart, so the groups overlap a lot
solve.work: Means differ by 3; MAD 6; 3/6 = 0.5 MAD apart, so large overlap.

questions.skill: Choose the better measure of centre
questions.stem: The mean of a data set is much greater than its median. What does this suggest?
choices: A few unusually large values pull the mean up
A few unusually small values pull the mean up
The values are spread evenly on both sides of the median
All of the values are equal
questions.answer: A few unusually large values pull the mean up
questions.solution: Large values raise the mean but barely change the median. So a mean far above the median suggests a few very large values stretching the data to the high side.

solve.answer: A few unusually large values pull the mean up
solve.work: Mean well above median indicates a few large values pulling the mean up (right skew).

questions.skill: Choose the better measure of centre
questions.stem: For which data set is the median a better description of a typical value than the mean?
questions.solution: In 5, 6, 6, 7, 40 the value 40 is far from the rest, so the mean (12.8) is higher than four of the five values, while the median (6) is typical. In the other sets the values are evenly spread, so the mean and the median are the same and both describe the data well.

solve.work: Only 5,6,6,7,40 has an outlier (mean 12.8 vs median 6). Others are symmetric, mean = median.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier on the mean and median
questions.stem: The four values 8, 9, 9 and 10 have a mean of 9. A fifth value, 30, is added. What is the mean of all five values?
questions.solution: The total of the five values is 36 + 30 = 66. The mean is 66 / 5 = 13.2. One large value raised the mean from 9 to 13.2.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier on the mean and median
questions.stem: The values 52, 55, 58, 60 and 61 are in a group. A new value of 90 is added to the group. Which statement is true?
choices: The median increases by more than the mean does
The mean and the median increase by the same amount
Neither the mean nor the median changes
The mean increases by more than the median does
questions.answer: The mean increases by more than the median does
questions.solution: Before: the mean is 286 / 5 = 57.2 and the median is 58. After adding 90: the mean is 376 / 6, about 62.7, and the median is (58 + 60) / 2 = 59. The mean rose by about 5.5 and the median rose by only 1, so the large new value affects the mean much more.

solve.answer: The mean increases by more than the median does
solve.work: Before: sum 286, mean 57.2, median 58. After: sum 376, mean about 62.67 (up ~5.47); median (58+60)/2=59 (up 1). Mean rises more.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a distribution
questions.stem: The data 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 15, 16, 16, 17 fall into two clusters with a gap between them. What is the width of the gap, that is, the difference between the least value of the upper cluster and the greatest value of the lower cluster?
questions.solution: The lower cluster is 4 to 7 and the upper cluster is 15 to 17. The gap runs from 7 to 15, so its width is 15 - 7 = 8.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a distribution
questions.stem: A data set is skewed right if a few unusually large values stretch out its upper end. Which data set is skewed right?
questions.solution: In 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 20 most values are small and one value, 20, stretches the data to the right, so it is skewed right (mean about 5.9, median 4). 1, 16, 17, 17, 18, 18, 19 has one very small value, so it is skewed left. The other two are symmetric.

solve.work: 2,3,3,4,4,5,20 has one large value stretching the upper end. The 1,16,... set is skewed left; others symmetric/constant.

questions.skill: Compare the share of each group above a cutoff
questions.stem: Ten runners on the Red team and ten on the Blue team ran one lap. Red times, in seconds: 62, 65, 58, 70, 61, 66, 59, 64, 68, 63. Blue times: 67, 72, 66, 74, 69, 63, 71, 70, 65, 68. A time under 65 seconds earns a ribbon. How many percentage points greater is the percent of Red runners who earned a ribbon than the percent of Blue runners who did?
questions.solution: Red times under 65: 62, 58, 61, 59, 64 and 63, which is 6 of 10, or 60 percent. Blue times under 65: only 63, which is 1 of 10, or 10 percent. (The 65 is not under 65.) The difference is 60 - 10 = 50 percentage points.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: Group A has a median of 65, with a first quartile of 55 and a third quartile of 75. Group B has a median of 70, with a first quartile of 60 and a third quartile of 80. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Group B is clearly better, because its median is higher
Group A is more spread out, because its third quartile is lower
Group B's median is 5 higher, but the middle halves overlap a lot, so the groups are fairly similar
Every student in Group B scored higher than every student in Group A
questions.answer: Group B's median is 5 higher, but the middle halves overlap a lot, so the groups are fairly similar
questions.solution: The medians differ by only 5. Both IQRs are 20, so the groups are equally spread out. The middle halves, 55 to 75 and 60 to 80, overlap for most of their length, so the groups are fairly similar and many scores in A are higher than many scores in B.

solve.answer: Group B's median is 5 higher, but the middle halves overlap a lot, so the groups are fairly similar
solve.work: Both IQRs = 20 (55-75, 60-80); medians differ by 5; middle halves overlap from 60 to 75. Option on 'fairly similar' is best supported.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: Maya chose a random sample of 30 sixth graders and a random sample of 30 seventh graders at her school. The sixth graders slept a mean of 9.4 hours a night and the seventh graders slept a mean of 8.6 hours. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Every seventh grader at the school sleeps less than every sixth grader
Seventh graders at the school probably sleep less than sixth graders on average
All seventh graders in the country sleep exactly 8.6 hours
Growing older makes students need less sleep
questions.answer: Seventh graders at the school probably sleep less than sixth graders on average
questions.solution: Random samples let us make a careful statement about the whole grades at that school: the seventh graders probably sleep less on average, with some chance variation. The data cannot show that every student differs, cannot describe other schools, and cannot explain why the difference exists.

solve.answer: Seventh graders at the school probably sleep less than sixth graders on average
solve.work: Random samples of 30 support a tentative inference about the school's grades; not causation, not the country, not every student.

questions.skill: Communicate a comparison in words
questions.stem: Minutes to read a chapter. Boys: 12, 14, 15, 15, 19. Girls: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Which sentence is a correct report?
choices: The boys' median is 2 minutes greater, and the girls' range is 3 minutes greater
The girls' median is 2 minutes greater, and the boys' range is 3 minutes greater
The boys' median is 2 minutes greater, and the boys' range is 3 minutes greater
The boys' median is 3 minutes greater, and the boys' range is 2 minutes greater
questions.answer: The boys' median is 2 minutes greater, and the boys' range is 3 minutes greater
questions.solution: Boys: the median is 15 and the range is 19 - 12 = 7. Girls: the median is 13 and the range is 15 - 11 = 4. The boys' median is 15 - 13 = 2 greater and the boys' range is 7 - 4 = 3 greater.

solve.answer: The boys' median is 2 minutes greater, and the boys' range is 3 minutes greater
solve.work: Boys median 15, range 19-12=7. Girls median 13, range 15-11=4. Boys median 2 greater, boys range 3 greater.

questions.skill: Communicate a comparison in words
questions.stem: Group A has a mean of 35 and a MAD of 4. Group B has a mean of 35 and a MAD of 11. Which sentence best reports the comparison?
choices: Both groups scored 35, so the groups are the same
On average both groups scored 35, but Group B's scores are more spread out (MAD 11 compared with 4)
Group B scored higher than Group A, because its MAD is higher
Group A scored 35 and Group B scored 11
questions.answer: On average both groups scored 35, but Group B's scores are more spread out (MAD 11 compared with 4)
questions.solution: The means are equal, so the typical score is the same. The MADs differ, so the spread is not: Group B's scores are farther from 35 on average. A good report mentions both.

solve.answer: On average both groups scored 35, but Group B's scores are more spread out (MAD 11 compared with 4)
solve.work: Same mean 35; B's MAD 11 > 4, so B more spread out.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and sample size
questions.stem: A principal wants to know how many hours students at her school sleep. She asks only the students who arrive before 7 a.m. Why may this give a poor estimate?
choices: The sample is too large to give a mean
She should have asked about days, not hours
Students who arrive early all sleep the same number of hours
Early arrivers may sleep differently from other students, so the sample may not be representative
questions.answer: Early arrivers may sleep differently from other students, so the sample may not be representative
questions.solution: Students who arrive before 7 a.m. are not chosen at random: they may get up earlier and sleep less than most students. A sample that leaves out many students is biased and may not represent the school.

solve.answer: Early arrivers may sleep differently from other students, so the sample may not be representative
solve.work: Early arrivers are a biased subgroup whose sleep may differ.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and sample size
questions.stem: One student compared 10 random seventh graders with 10 random eighth graders and found the mean times on homework differed by 1 hour. A second student used 100 random students from each grade and found a difference of 0.2 hour. Which statement is most reasonable?
choices: The smaller samples are more reliable, because they are easier to check
Both samples are equally reliable, because both are random
The larger samples probably give a more reliable picture of the difference
Neither result tells us anything about the grades
questions.answer: The larger samples probably give a more reliable picture of the difference
questions.solution: Random samples of 100 are less affected by chance than random samples of 10, so they usually estimate the true difference more reliably. Both results say something about the grades, but the larger samples say more.

solve.answer: The larger samples probably give a more reliable picture of the difference
solve.work: Larger random samples vary less, so the 100-per-grade result is more reliable.

questions.skill: Reflect on the question and the method
questions.stem: Ana measures the long jumps of one group in centimeters. Ben measures the long jumps of a second group in inches. What should they do before comparing the groups?
choices: Compare the numbers as they are, because a larger number always means a longer jump
Use only the greatest value from each group
Write both sets of measurements in the same unit
Use the range for one group and the mean for the other
questions.answer: Write both sets of measurements in the same unit
questions.solution: Numbers measured in different units cannot be compared directly: 60 inches is longer than 100 centimeters. Both groups must be measured in the same unit, and both must be summarized with the same statistics.

solve.answer: Write both sets of measurements in the same unit
solve.work: Measurements must be in the same unit to compare.

questions.skill: Reflect on the question and the method
questions.stem: A student wants to compare how two groups rate the school lunch. Which survey question is worded most fairly?
choices: How would you rate the school lunch from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent)?
Don't you think the school lunch is terrible?
Isn't the school lunch the best part of your day?
Most students hate the lunch, so what score do you give it?
questions.answer: How would you rate the school lunch from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent)?
questions.solution: A fair question does not push people toward an answer. The three other questions suggest what the answer should be, which would bias the results.

solve.answer: How would you rate the school lunch from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent)?
solve.work: The 1-5 rating question is neutral; the others are leading.

questions.skill: Use samples to compare two populations
questions.stem: A random sample of 40 students at North School found that 12 ride a bike to school. A random sample of 50 students at South School found that 20 ride a bike. North School has 500 students and South School has 600. Based on the samples, about how many more students ride a bike at South School than at North School?
questions.solution: North: 12 / 40 = 30 percent, and 30 percent of 500 is 150 students. South: 20 / 50 = 40 percent, and 40 percent of 600 is 240 students. The estimated difference is 240 - 150 = 90 students.

questions.skill: Communicate a comparison of two groups
questions.stem: Plants in the sun had a median height of 24 cm and an IQR of 4 cm. Plants in the shade had a median height of 15 cm and an IQR of 5 cm. Which statement best summarizes the comparison?
choices: Sun plants were typically 9 cm taller, and varied much more than shade plants
Sun plants were typically 9 cm taller, and both groups varied by a similar amount
Shade plants were typically 9 cm taller, and both groups varied by a similar amount
The groups were typically the same height, but shade plants varied more
questions.answer: Sun plants were typically 9 cm taller, and both groups varied by a similar amount
questions.solution: The medians differ by $24 - 15 = 9$ cm, with the sun plants taller. The IQRs, 4 cm and 5 cm, are close compared with a 9 cm difference, so the spread is similar. Only "Sun plants were typically 9 cm taller, and both groups varied by a similar amount" reports both correctly.

solve.answer: Sun plants were typically 9 cm taller, and both groups varied by a similar amount
solve.work: Sun median 24 vs shade 15: sun 9 cm taller. IQRs 4 and 5: similar spread.

questions.skill: Difference of means in units of MAD
questions.stem: Group A has the values 8, 10 and 12. Group B has the values 12, 14 and 16. The difference between the two means is how many times the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of Group A?
questions.solution: Mean of A is 10 and mean of B is 14, so the difference is 4. The distances of A's values from 10 are 2, 0 and 2, so the MAD of A is $4 \div 3 = \frac{4}{3}$. Then $4 \div \frac{4}{3} = 3$, so the difference is 3 times the MAD.

solve.work: Means 10 and 14; difference 4. MAD A: distances 2, 0, 2; 4/3. 4 / (4/3) = 3.

questions.skill: Compare the means of two groups
questions.stem: Group A has 4 students with a mean score of 70 points. Group B has 6 students with a mean score of 80 points. What is the mean score of all 10 students together?
questions.solution: Group A scored 4 x 70 = 280 points in total and Group B scored 6 x 80 = 480 points. Together that is 760 points for 10 students, so the mean is 760 / 10 = 76 points. (It is not 75, because Group B has more students.)

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two groups
questions.stem: Group P has the values 4, 7, 10, 12, 15 and 21. Group Q has seven values in order: 5, 8, 10, $x$, 14, 16 and 20. The two groups have the same median. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Group P has 6 values, so its median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: (10 + 12) / 2 = 11. Group Q has 7 values, so its median is the 4th value, which is $x$. For the medians to match, $x$ = 11. (11 fits between 10 and 14, so the list stays in order.)

solve.work: P median (6 values) = (10+12)/2 = 11. Q median is the 4th value x, so x=11 (fits 10<=11<=14).

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two groups
questions.stem: A group has 11 values listed from least to greatest, and the median is 30. At least how many of the 11 values are 30 or greater?
questions.solution: With 11 values in order, the median is the 6th value. So the 6th value is 30, and the 7th through 11th values are at least 30. That makes at least 6 values (the 6th to the 11th) that are 30 or greater.

solve.work: Median of 11 ordered values is the 6th, =30. The 6th through 11th values are all >=30: 6 values guaranteed.

questions.skill: Compare the ranges of two groups
questions.stem: Data set 1 has a least value of 13 and a range of 24. Data set 2 has the same greatest value as data set 1, but its range is only 9. What is the least value of data set 2?
questions.solution: The greatest value of data set 1 is 13 + 24 = 37. Data set 2 also has a greatest value of 37, and its range is 9, so its least value is 37 - 9 = 28.

questions.skill: Compare the IQRs of two groups
questions.stem: Both lists have 9 values and are in order. Group P: 3, 6, 7, 9, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22. Group Q: 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 16. To find the quartiles, leave out the median, then take the median of the 4 values below it and of the 4 values above it. By how much does the IQR of Group P exceed the IQR of Group Q?
questions.solution: Group P: the median is 12. Lower four values 3, 6, 7, 9 have median 6.5; upper four values 14, 15, 18, 22 have median 16.5; IQR = 16.5 - 6.5 = 10. Group Q: the median is 10. Lower four values 5, 7, 8, 9 have median 7.5; upper four values 11, 12, 13, 16 have median 12.5; IQR = 12.5 - 7.5 = 5. The difference is 10 - 5 = 5.

questions.skill: Compare the IQRs of two groups
questions.stem: Group S has an IQR of 18 and a first quartile of 42. Group T has an IQR of 12 and a third quartile of 70. How much greater is the third quartile of Group T than the third quartile of Group S?
questions.solution: The third quartile equals the first quartile plus the IQR. For Group S: 42 + 18 = 60. Group T's third quartile is 70. The difference is 70 - 60 = 10.

questions.skill: Compare the mean absolute deviations of two groups
questions.stem: A group has four values and a mean of 20. Three of the values are 14, 18 and 24. What is the MAD of the group?
questions.solution: The four values add to 4 x 20 = 80. The three known values add to 56, so the fourth value is 80 - 56 = 24. The distances from the mean of 20 are 6, 2, 4 and 4. The MAD is (6 + 2 + 4 + 4) / 4 = 16 / 4 = 4.

questions.skill: Compare the mean absolute deviations of two groups
questions.stem: Every value in a data set is increased by 5. What happens to the mean and to the MAD of the data set?
choices: The mean increases by 5 and the MAD stays the same
The mean and the MAD both increase by 5
The mean stays the same and the MAD increases by 5
The mean and the MAD both stay the same
questions.answer: The mean increases by 5 and the MAD stays the same
questions.solution: Adding 5 to every value moves the whole data set up by 5, so the mean goes up by 5. But every value is still the same distance from the mean as before, so the MAD does not change. Example: 4, 8, 9, 15 has mean 9 and MAD 3; 9, 13, 14, 20 has mean 14 and MAD 3.

solve.answer: The mean increases by 5 and the MAD stays the same
solve.work: Shifting every value by 5 shifts the mean by 5; distances from the mean are unchanged, so MAD unchanged.

questions.skill: Describe the centre and spread together
questions.stem: Group A has a median of 20 and an IQR of 6. Group B has a median of 24 and an IQR of 14. Which statement is true?
choices: Group A has the higher median, but its middle half is more than twice as spread out as Group B's
Group B has the higher median, but its middle half is more than twice as spread out as Group A's
Group B has the higher median, and its middle half is less spread out than Group A's
Group A has the higher median, and its middle half is less spread out than Group B's
questions.answer: Group B has the higher median, but its middle half is more than twice as spread out as Group A's
questions.solution: Group B's median (24) is higher than Group A's (20). Group B's IQR is 14 and Group A's is 6, so B's middle half is more spread out; 14 is more than 2 x 6 = 12, so it is more than twice as spread out.

solve.answer: Group B has the higher median, but its middle half is more than twice as spread out as Group A's
solve.work: B median 24 > 20. B IQR 14 > 2*6=12, so more than twice as spread.

questions.skill: Describe the centre and spread together
questions.stem: Which pair of groups has the same center (median) but different spread (IQR)?
choices: Group 1: median 15, IQR 4; Group 2: median 15, IQR 9
Group 1: median 15, IQR 4; Group 2: median 19, IQR 4
Group 1: median 15, IQR 4; Group 2: median 19, IQR 9
Group 1: median 15, IQR 4; Group 2: median 4, IQR 15
questions.answer: Group 1: median 15, IQR 4; Group 2: median 15, IQR 9
questions.solution: Same median and different IQR is needed. Only the first pair has two medians of 15 with IQRs of 4 and 9. The other pairs have different medians.

solve.answer: Group 1: median 15, IQR 4; Group 2: median 15, IQR 9
solve.work: Need equal medians, different IQRs: median 15 both, IQR 4 vs 9.

questions.skill: Compare a difference in centres with the variability
questions.stem: Group A has the values 20, 22, 26 and 28. Group B has a mean of 36 and the same MAD as Group A. The means of the two groups are how many MADs apart?
questions.solution: Group A's mean is 96 / 4 = 24. Its distances from 24 are 4, 2, 2 and 4, so its MAD is 12 / 4 = 3. Group B has the same MAD, 3. The means are 36 - 24 = 12 apart, which is 12 / 3 = 4 MADs.

solve.work: A: sum 96, mean 24; deviations 4,2,2,4 =12; MAD 3. Means 36-24=12; 12/3=4.

questions.skill: Compare a difference in centres with the variability
questions.stem: Two groups have the same MAD. Their means are 25 and 40, and that is exactly 3 MADs apart. What is the MAD?
questions.solution: The means are 40 - 25 = 15 apart. That equals 3 MADs, so one MAD is 15 / 3 = 5.

questions.skill: Choose the better measure of centre
questions.stem: Group A has the values 48, 49, 50, 51, 52. Group B has the values 40, 44, 45, 46, 75. Both groups have a mean of 50. Which statement is true?
choices: The mean describes a typical value equally well in both groups, because the means are equal
The median of Group B is greater than the median of Group A
The mean describes a typical value less well in Group B than in Group A
The range of Group B is smaller than the range of Group A
questions.answer: The mean describes a typical value less well in Group B than in Group A
questions.solution: Group A's median is 50, matching its mean. Group B's median is 45, and four of its five values are 46 or less, so the mean of 50 is pulled up by the value 75 and is not typical. Group B has the lower median and the greater range (35 compared with 4).

solve.answer: The mean describes a typical value less well in Group B than in Group A
solve.work: B: sum 250, mean 50, median 45, range 35. A: median 50, range 4. B's mean 50 is above four of its five values, so it describes B less well. Other options false.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier on the mean and median
questions.stem: A group has the values 12, 14, 15, 16, 18 and 45. By how much does the mean decrease when the value 45 is removed?
questions.solution: With 45: the total is 120 and the mean is 120 / 6 = 20. Without 45: the total is 75 and the mean is 75 / 5 = 15. The mean decreases by 20 - 15 = 5.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier on the mean and median
questions.stem: A data set has the values 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 20. The greatest value, 20, is changed to 50. Which measure does NOT change?
choices: The median
The mean
The range
The MAD
questions.answer: The median
questions.solution: The median is the 4th value, 12, before and after, since the changed value is still the greatest. The mean rises (from 12.9 to about 17.1), the range rises (from 12 to 42), and the MAD also changes because the mean and the greatest distance both change.

solve.answer: The median
solve.work: Median is the 4th value, 12, unchanged. Mean (90/7 -> 120/7), MAD and range (12 -> 42) all change.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a distribution
questions.stem: Group A has the values 10, 11, 12, 12, 13, 14. Group B has the values 1, 2, 3, 30, 31, 32. Which statement is true?
choices: Group A has two clusters with a gap between them
Group B has two clusters with a gap, and its mean and median fall in the gap
Group B has one cluster, and its mean and median lie within it
Group A has the greater range
questions.answer: Group B has two clusters with a gap, and its mean and median fall in the gap
questions.solution: Group B's values form two clusters (1 to 3 and 30 to 32) with a large gap between them. Its mean is 99 / 6 = 16.5 and its median is (3 + 30) / 2 = 16.5, and both fall in the gap, where there are no data. Group A forms one tight cluster, and its range (4) is far less than Group B's (31).

solve.answer: Group B has two clusters with a gap, and its mean and median fall in the gap
solve.work: A: one cluster, range 4. B: clusters 1-3 and 30-32; mean 99/6=16.5, median (3+30)/2=16.5, both in the gap.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a distribution
questions.stem: The data 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 11 are skewed to the right. How much greater is the mean than the median?
questions.solution: The mean is 28 / 7 = 4. The median (4th value) is 3. The mean is 4 - 3 = 1 greater than the median, as is usual when a few large values pull the mean toward the right.

questions.skill: Compare the share of each group above a cutoff
questions.stem: In Group A, 40 students took a test and 45 percent scored above 70. In Group B, 80 students took the test and 30 percent scored above 70. How many more students in Group B than in Group A scored above 70?
questions.solution: Group A: 45 percent of 40 is 0.45 x 40 = 18 students. Group B: 30 percent of 80 is 0.30 x 80 = 24 students. Group B has 24 - 18 = 6 more students above 70, even though a smaller percent of Group B scored above 70.

questions.skill: Compare the share of each group above a cutoff
questions.stem: Group A has 30 students and 24 of them scored above 70. Group B has 60 students and 30 of them scored above 70. Sam says Group B did better because 30 is more than 24. Which statement is correct?
choices: Sam is wrong: 80 percent of Group A scored above 70, but only 50 percent of Group B did
Sam is right: more students in Group B scored above 70
Sam is wrong: the same percent of each group scored above 70
Sam is right: Group B is bigger, so its score is more reliable
questions.answer: Sam is wrong: 80 percent of Group A scored above 70, but only 50 percent of Group B did
questions.solution: The groups have different sizes, so compare percents. Group A: 24 / 30 = 80 percent. Group B: 30 / 60 = 50 percent. A greater share of Group A scored above 70.

solve.answer: Sam is wrong: 80 percent of Group A scored above 70, but only 50 percent of Group B did
solve.work: A: 24/30=80%. B: 30/60=50%. Groups differ in size, so compare percents; Sam is wrong.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion the data support
questions.stem: Four pairs of groups each have means that differ by 6 points. Which pair gives the strongest evidence that the two groups really differ?
choices: Each group has a MAD of 1
Each group has a MAD of 3
Each group has a MAD of 6
Each group has a MAD of 10
questions.answer: Each group has a MAD of 1
questions.solution: A difference in means is more convincing when it is large compared with the variation within the groups. A difference of 6 is 6 MADs when the MAD is 1, 2 MADs when it is 3, 1 MAD when it is 6, and only 0.6 of a MAD when it is 10.

solve.answer: Each group has a MAD of 1
solve.work: A difference of 6 is 6 MADs when MAD=1, the largest relative to variability: strongest evidence.

questions.skill: Communicate a comparison in words
questions.stem: A student writes: "Team A is better because its mean score is 5 higher." Team A's MAD is 20 and Team B's MAD is 3. What should the report add?
choices: Nothing more: the means alone show which team is better
That Team A's scores vary much more than Team B's, since the MADs are 20 and 3
That Team A is more consistent, since its MAD is larger
That Team B scored more in total, since its MAD is smaller
questions.answer: That Team A's scores vary much more than Team B's, since the MADs are 20 and 3
questions.solution: A comparison of centres alone leaves out how spread out the scores are. Team A's MAD of 20 is far larger than Team B's MAD of 3, so A's scores vary a lot and its mean is not very typical of its games. A larger MAD means less consistent, and the MAD does not tell us anything about total scores.

solve.answer: That Team A's scores vary much more than Team B's, since the MADs are 20 and 3
solve.work: A difference of 5 is small against A's MAD of 20; the report should note A's far greater variability.

questions.skill: Communicate a comparison in words
questions.stem: Nine girls ran a race in 31, 27, 35, 29, 33, 28, 36, 30, 34 seconds. Nine boys ran it in 38, 33, 41, 36, 35, 40, 34, 37, 39 seconds. A report says: "The median time of the girls was ___ seconds less than the median time of the boys." What number goes in the blank?
questions.solution: Girls in order: 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 33, 34, 35, 36; the median (5th value) is 31. Boys in order: 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41; the median (5th value) is 37. The difference is 37 - 31 = 6 seconds.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and sample size
questions.stem: Mia and Leo each take a random sample from the same school to estimate the mean number of books its students read in a month. Mia uses 5 students and Leo uses 50 students. Which statement is most likely true?
choices: Leo's estimate is more likely to be close to the school's true mean
Mia's estimate is more likely to be close, because her sample is smaller
Both estimates are equally likely to be close, because both samples are random
Leo's estimate is exactly equal to the school's true mean
questions.answer: Leo's estimate is more likely to be close to the school's true mean
questions.solution: A larger random sample varies less from one sample to the next, so it is more likely to be close to the true mean. But even a large sample estimate is usually not exactly equal to the true mean.

solve.answer: Leo's estimate is more likely to be close to the school's true mean
solve.work: Larger random sample has less sampling variability, so Leo's estimate is more likely close (not exact).

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and sample size
questions.stem: A class posts an online poll on its website and anyone can answer. Of the 80 people who answer, most say they love the new school schedule. Why may these results not represent all students?
choices: 80 answers is too many to be reliable
Online polls always ask the questions in the wrong order
The mean of an online poll is always equal to its median
People with strong opinions are more likely to answer, so the sample is not random
questions.answer: People with strong opinions are more likely to answer, so the sample is not random
questions.solution: In an open poll, people choose whether to answer, and those with strong feelings are more likely to do so. A voluntary sample is not random and may not represent all students. A larger number of answers does not fix that.

solve.answer: People with strong opinions are more likely to answer, so the sample is not random
solve.work: Voluntary-response sample: those with strong views answer, not random.

questions.skill: Reflect on the question and the method
questions.stem: Jess grows 5 plants under Brand X light in a sunny room and 5 plants under Brand Y light in a shaded room. The Brand X plants grow taller. Which change to her method would best let her conclude that the light caused the difference?
choices: Grow more plants in the sunny room
Measure the Brand X plants more often
Report only the tallest plant from each group
Grow both groups in the same room with the same water, changing only the light
questions.answer: Grow both groups in the same room with the same water, changing only the light
questions.solution: To compare two groups fairly, only the thing being tested should differ. In her method the room also differs, so the room could explain the height. Using the same room and the same water isolates the light.

solve.answer: Grow both groups in the same room with the same water, changing only the light
solve.work: Room (sun vs shade) is a confounder; hold everything else constant and vary only the light.

questions.skill: Reflect on the question and the method
questions.stem: A student finds that Class A's mean quiz score is 2 points higher than Class B's, and that each class has a MAD of 10. What is the best next step?
choices: Report that Class A is clearly better
Collect more data from larger random samples, because the difference is small compared with the variability
Throw out the scores that are far from the mean
Report only the range of each class
questions.answer: Collect more data from larger random samples, because the difference is small compared with the variability
questions.solution: The means are only 2 / 10 = 0.2 of a MAD apart, which is small compared with how much the scores vary. This could easily be chance, so more data from larger random samples is the sensible step. Dropping data points or reporting one statistic would not fix that.

solve.answer: Collect more data from larger random samples, because the difference is small compared with the variability
solve.work: Difference 2 is only 0.2 MAD; inconclusive, so gather more data.

questions.skill: Use samples to compare two populations
questions.stem: Random samples suggest that students at School A read a mean of 3 books a month and students at School B read a mean of 5 books a month. School A has 450 students and School B has 300 students. Based on these estimates, how many more books are read in a month by all the students at School B than by all the students at School A?
questions.solution: School A: 3 x 450 = 1,350 books. School B: 5 x 300 = 1,500 books. School B students read 1,500 - 1,350 = 150 more books in total, even though School B has fewer students.

questions.skill: Use samples to compare two populations
questions.stem: In a random sample of 50 people from Town X, 35 prefer the new park plan. In a random sample of 80 people from Town Y, 40 prefer it. Town X has 2,000 residents and Town Y has 1,500. Based on the samples, about how many more residents of Town X than of Town Y prefer the plan?
questions.solution: Town X: 35 / 50 = 70 percent, and 70 percent of 2,000 is 1,400 residents. Town Y: 40 / 80 = 50 percent, and 50 percent of 1,500 is 750 residents. The estimated difference is 1,400 - 750 = 650 residents.

questions.skill: Use samples to compare two populations
questions.stem: Two different random samples of 20 students from the same school gave mean amounts of sleep of 8.4 hours and 8.9 hours. Which is the best explanation for the difference?
choices: One of the samples must have been chosen incorrectly
The school's true mean changed between the samples
One of the students made an arithmetic mistake
Different random samples usually give slightly different means
questions.answer: Different random samples usually give slightly different means
questions.solution: Random samples contain different students, so their means vary a little by chance. A small difference like this is normal and does not mean that anything went wrong.

solve.answer: Different random samples usually give slightly different means
solve.work: Sampling variability: different random samples give slightly different means.

questions.skill: Compare the means of two groups
questions.stem: Group P has the values 12, 18, 9 and 21. Group Q has five values: 10, 12, 17, 20 and $x$. The two groups have the same mean. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: The mean of Group P is $(12 + 18 + 9 + 21) \div 4 = 60 \div 4 = 15$. Group Q has 5 values and the same mean, so they must add to $15 \times 5 = 75$. The four known values add to $10 + 12 + 17 + 20 = 59$. So $x = 75 - 59 = 16$.

questions.skill: Compare the variability of two groups with the IQR
questions.stem: Two groups of students timed how many minutes they took to finish a puzzle. Group A: 3, 7, 9, 12, 17, 20. Group B: 10, 12, 13, 15, 17, 19. Each list is in order. The quartiles are the medians of the lower half and the upper half of the data. The IQR of Group A is how many times the IQR of Group B?
questions.solution: Group A: the lower half is 3, 7, 9 so Q1 = 7, and the upper half is 12, 17, 20 so Q3 = 17. The IQR is 17 - 7 = 10. Group B: the lower half is 10, 12, 13 so Q1 = 12, and the upper half is 15, 17, 19 so Q3 = 17. The IQR is 17 - 12 = 5. Then 10 / 5 = 2, so the IQR of Group A is 2 times the IQR of Group B.

solve.work: Group A (6 values): lower half 3, 7, 9 -> Q1 = 7; upper half 12, 17, 20 -> Q3 = 17; IQR = 10. Group B: lower half 10, 12, 13 -> Q1 = 12; upper half 15, 17, 19 -> Q3 = 17; IQR = 5. Ratio 10 / 5 = 2.
